## Summary
After Copilot Connector authentication changes, a new Copilot chat can wait indefinitely for the shared Copilot client to restart while an unrelated chat in another window has an active turn. The waiting chat displays `Reasoning`, then `This is taking a little longer than usual`, although it has not reached a model request.

This also blocks agent-driven testing: the controlling chat waits for the new chat, but its own active turn prevents the client restart needed to launch that chat.

## Environment
- Windows, VS Code Insiders commit `ff00e788322523ee1e9e8ee2c9bb4b89af93a3c2`
- Copilot session target; two windows sharing an agent host
- `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled: true`
- `chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled: true`

## Steps observed
1. Keep a Copilot chat running in window A. In this case it used dbgjs Playwright to control window B.
2. In window B, connect Microsoft Learn Docs and Azure Data Explorer through Customizations > Discover > Copilot Connectors, completing browser authorization.
3. Reload window B and start a completely new Copilot chat.
4. Send: `Use the Microsoft Learn Docs connector to find the official documentation for the Kusto Query Language where operator. Return the page title and its learn.microsoft.com URL. You must call the connector.`
5. Keep the original chat in window A active while waiting for or investigating the result.

## Actual
The new chat remains in `prepareTurn`, without a tool call or model response, while the UI indicates reasoning/model delay.

At 11:09:42 the agent-host log reported:
```
Deferring CopilotClient restart (Copilot Connector authentication changed before session launch) until 1 chat(s) finish their in-flight turns and subagents
```
At 11:10:42:
```
Chat queue task stalled: ... operation=prepareTurn
```

A non-pausing dbgjs logpoint in the live agent host confirmed:
- Pending restart reasons: `Copilot Connector authentication updated` and `Copilot Connector authentication changed before session launch`.
- A restart waiter existed; credential updates were no longer running.
- The only busy chat was the controlling chat in window A (`hasActiveTurn=true`, `hasActiveSubagents=false`).
- The pending turn belonged to the new chat in window B.

No credential values were inspected. The diagnostic logpoint was removed afterward.

## Recovery verified
Ending the controlling chat turn allowed the waiting test chat to finish. On the next inspection, its transcript contained the requested Microsoft Learn title and URL and reported a total duration of **12m 28s**. No forced client restart was performed. Connector tool-call details were still being verified when this issue was filed.

## Relevant implementation
At the tested revision:
- [copilotAgent.ts:1228](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ff00e788322523ee1e9e8ee2c9bb4b89af93a3c2/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts#L1228): `_ensureClientForSession` waits for a restart when connector authentication differs.
- [copilotAgent.ts:1356](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ff00e788322523ee1e9e8ee2c9bb4b89af93a3c2/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts#L1356): restart is deferred while another chat has in-flight work.
- [copilotAgent.ts:1502](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ff00e788322523ee1e9e8ee2c9bb4b89af93a3c2/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts#L1502): busy work is counted across live sessions.
- [copilotAgent.ts:1395](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ff00e788322523ee1e9e8ee2c9bb4b89af93a3c2/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts#L1395): chat completion retries the deferred restart.

## Expected
Connector authentication changes should not silently block new chats behind unrelated long-running turns. If a shared-client restart cannot be avoided, show the actual wait reason and provide a safe way forward instead of presenting it as model reasoning. Consider refreshing connector authentication without restarti
state.title: Copilot Connectors: new chat waits for shared-client restart while another chat is active

state.body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/341692, which fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341502 for local terminals only.

Restored terminal editors are meant to attach to their revived process first, and otherwise to their saved persistent process ID only if it still has the saved pid. On remotes, both steps are skipped and the editor always reattaches by the saved ID.

- `TerminalEditorService.reviveInput` sets `findRevivedId` for every restored terminal editor ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalEditorService.ts#L238-L244)), but `TerminalProcessManager.createProcess` only honors it for local terminals ([local](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L339-L340)). The remote branch calls `attachToProcess(id)` directly ([remote](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L290-L291)).
- `RemoteTerminalBackend.attachToRevivedProcess` has no callers ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/remoteTerminalBackend.ts#L231-L243)). It was added alongside the local path in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/7aa326e2d7a802cb8622842309e10196ce228b53.
- Its lookup couldn't match anyway: `RemoteTerminalChannelClient.getRevivedPtyNewId` sends `[id]` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/remote/remoteTerminalChannel.ts#L319-L321)), but `PtyService.getRevivedPtyNewId` takes `(workspaceId, id)` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L561-L569)), and the server forwards the arguments unchanged ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/server/node/remoteTerminalChannel.ts#L154)).
- A remote server runs one pty host for all windows connected to it ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/server/node/serverServices.ts#L244), [code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/server/node/serverServices.ts#L416)), and persistent process IDs restart at 1 whenever that pty host restarts ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L121), [code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L336)).

Expected impact, from reading the code (not reproduced yet):

- With two windows on the same remote, after the remote server restarts, a terminal editor restored in one window can attach to a terminal running in the other, like https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341502.
- After the remote server revives terminals, restored terminal editors attach by their old ID instead of their revived process.

Steps to try (any SSH, WSL or container remote, or a TestResolver window in a dev build):

1. Open folder B on the remote, run **Terminal: Create New Terminal in Editor Area** three times, then close the window.
2. Restart the remote server, for example with `wsl --shutdown`, a host reboot, or a container rebuild.
3. Open folder A on the same remote, create three terminals, and run `sleep 600` in the third.
4. Open folder B on the same remote in a new window.

Expected: B starts new terminals and A's terminals stay in A.

Possible fix:

- Route remote terminal editors through `attachToRevivedProcess(id, pid)`, the same as local ones.
- Make `RemoteTerminalBackend.attachToRevivedProcess` match `LocalTerminalBackend`
state.title: Restored terminal editors on remotes reattach by saved process ID only

Testing #345466

## Environment

- Windows x64, Code OSS 1.146.0 (Electron 43.8.3).
- Client and remote VS Code agent host built from `ccbfe2802f57d4bb69c478c7790c829ec486f75e`.
- Host type: **Dev Tunnel to a Windows VS Code agent host**, authenticated/private tunnel.
- `workbench.browser.enableRemoteProxy: true`; `workbench.browser.dataStorage: "default"`.
- Isolated Code OSS profile. The dev product override supplies only the public tunnel authentication configuration from Insiders; no product source changes.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In the Agents window, open the new-session composer and select a remote host and folder A. Do **not** send the first message yet.
2. Open the integrated browser from the session activity bar and navigate to a web app running only on that host's loopback interface, for example `http://127.0.0.1:43187/?case=draft`.
3. Verify the page loads and the remote indicator says `Connected via <host>`.
4. In the composer, change the workspace to another folder B on the **same remote host**. This also reproduces by choosing a previously used folder directly from the workspace picker's recent list.
5. Send the first message.

## Expected

The browser tab remains open, preserving its URL while following the draft's new folder/storage affinity. It is still available when the session starts, as specified by the TPI's new-session-composer scenario.

## Actual

Changing the folder immediately removes the browser tab. Only the Files tab remains, and the native browser page is destroyed, not merely hidden behind another editor. Starting the session does not restore it.

Reproduced twice in opposite directions between two folders on the same source-built host. Before the switch, the tab loaded the correct remote HTML, scripts, image, API response, and WebSocket echo; after the switch, its URL was absent from the browser targets. Existing browser tabs belonging to already-started local and other remote sessions remained intact.
state.title: Agents: changing a draft session folder destroys its browser tab (Dev Tunnels)

Since updating VS Code to 1.141.1 (commit 7baac39), the Claude Code extension's panel is blank in a WSL remote window: no buttons, no content. It worked immediately before the update.

**Environment**
- Windows client, remote: WSL Ubuntu 24.04 (`wsl+Ubuntu`)
- Claude Code for VS Code 2.1.296 (linux-x64), installed on the WSL side

**Steps**
1. Open a folder in a WSL remote window.
2. Open the Claude Code panel in the sidebar.

**Expected:** the panel loads its UI.
**Actual:** the panel stays blank. Developer Tools shows the webview's own script and stylesheet rejected with 401:

```
GET https://vscode-remote+wsl-002bubuntu.vscode-resource.vscode-cdn.net/home/andre/.vscode-server/extensions/anthropic.claude-code-2.1.296-linux-x64/webview/index.js net::ERR_ABORTED 401 (Unauthorized)
GET https://vscode-remote+wsl-002bubuntu.vscode-resource.vscode-cdn.net/home/andre/.vscode-server/extensions/anthropic.claude-code-2.1.296-linux-x64/webview/index.css net::ERR_ABORTED 401 (Unauthorized)
```

Both files exist on disk. The extension sets `localResourceRoots` to `<extensionUri>/webview` and `<extensionUri>/resources`, so they fall inside the allowed roots. The 401 matches the access-denied branch of the webview's local-resource loader.

**Where it works and where it doesn't**
- Works: the same extension in a local Windows window.
- Works: the same extension in a Dev Container window.
- Fails: WSL remote window only.

**Already tried, no change**
- Full system reboot
- Several older versions of the extension
- Clearing `%APPDATA%\Code\` `Service Worker`, `Cache`, `CachedData`, `GPUCache`
- Rolling back to VS Code 1.140.0: **fixes it** (see update below)

The extension host log shows the extension activating normally and finding its saved login, so the failure is limited to the panel loading its files.

**Update: confirmed regression in 1.141.1**

Rolling the client back to 1.140.0 (commit 07f806f) fixes it with no other changes. The WSL server updated to the matching build on reconnect, and the Claude Code panel loads normally. Same extension version (2.1.296), same machine and WSL distro.

- 1.140.0 (07f806f): works
- 1.141.1 (7baac39): panel blank, webview resources return 401
state.title: Extension webviews in WSL remote window fail to load their resources (401) after updating to 1.141.1

All webviews (Markdown preview, Claude Code extension panel, etc.) render blank when connected to WSL. Webviews work fine in local Windows folders.

VS Code: 1.141.1 (commit 7baac39ec3), Electron 43.7.7, Chromium 150

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open a folder in WSL via `code .` from the Ubuntu shell (remote authority becomes `wsl+Ubuntu`)
2. Open any .md file and run "Markdown: Open Preview"
3. Preview is blank

Webview DevTools > Network: every webview resource fails with "401 Unauthorized (from service worker)", e.g.
https://vscode-remote+wsl-002bubuntu.vscode-resource.vscode-cdn.net/home/<user>/.vscode-server/bin/7baac39ec3.../extensions/markdown-language-features/media/index.js

The direct vscode-remote-resource request to the server returns 200, so the server and connection token are fine. The resource hostname is lowercased (`wsl+ubuntu`) while the remote authority is `wsl+Ubuntu`, so the comparison against allowed resource roots appears to be case-sensitive and denies access.

Workaround: open with a lowercase authority. All webviews then work:
code --remote wsl+ubuntu /home/<user>/project

Ruled out: extension versions, VS Code caches, GPU acceleration, reinstalling the VS Code server, proxy (--no-proxy-server), symlinked home/.vscode-server.
state.title: Webviews blank over WSL: 401 from service worker when remote authority is "wsl+Ubuntu" (capital letter)

state.body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/341700, which streams a detached background shell's output from the Copilot SDK's `session.rpc.tasks.readOutput` into its tool call's terminal. Review of that PR found three things, none of which block it. The reload and restart gaps are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341645.

**`lastSnapshot` grows without bound for background shells**

- `NonPtyShellTerminalStreams.appendChunk` appends every chunk to `stream.lastSnapshot` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L360)) and nothing trims it. The terminal content itself is kept to a rolling buffer by `AgentHostTerminalManager._trimContent` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts#L832-L834)), 100 KB per [`AGENT_HOST_TERMINAL_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/terminalConstants.ts#L10).
- Once a stream has switched to chunks, `lastSnapshot` has two readers: `append` returns early for a chunked stream ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L278)), and `completeToolCall` compares it once when the tool call completes ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L406)). For a shell that keeps running after its call completed, nothing reads it again.
- Attached background shells have done this since https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339220, because the Copilot SDK streams their `tool.shell_output` chunks until exit. Detached shells are the long-lived ones (dev servers, watchers), and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/341700 feeds their reads through the same path in `appendDetachedShellOutput` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L453-L459)), so a detached watcher that runs for hours keeps all of its output in the Agent Host process, untrimmed, until the chat is disposed.

**The exit code reported before the log drained is lost if the read then fails**

- When the task list, a `shell_completed` notification, or a `read_bash`/`stop_bash` result reports the exit while the log is still being read, `_completeBackgroundShell` remembers the shell as draining and returns without keeping the reported `exitCode` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L591-L596)).
- Normally the read's `exit.exitCode` settles the terminal. If the read fails instead, `stopReadingDetachedShell` finalizes with `undefined` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L486-L491)), so the terminal shows the shell as exited without a code even though one was reported.

**A failed read gives up instead of reading again without a cursor**

- `_readDetachedShellOutput` stops on any error, logs a warning, and leaves the shell to the task list ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L2684-L2689)).
- The `TasksReadOutputRequest.cursor` docs in `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.23-preview.2 say a read fails when the output no longer reaches the cursor, for example because its log was removed, and to read again without a cursor. The terminal then stays at whatever had been read before the failure.

Steps to see the firs
state.title: Background shell streams in Agent Host chats keep all output in lastSnapshot and can lose a detached shell's exit code

state.body:
The Markdown editor sends each edit to the extension host, which writes it to the `TextDocument`. When the document changes in the meantime for another reason, typing that is still on its way is dropped. The webview is reset to the document's text, so recently typed characters disappear.

Examples of such concurrent changes:

- a save participant such as format on save or trimming trailing whitespace while auto save is on
- the same file open in a second editor (another Markdown editor or the text editor) and edited there
- another extension applying a `WorkspaceEdit`

Steps to reproduce:

1. Open the same Markdown file in two Markdown editors side by side.
2. Type alternately in both, quickly.
3. Some characters are lost.

Expected: changes from both sides are merged, and no typed text is lost.

The empty change events on save, which caused #342170, are fixed separately in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344638.
state.title: Markdown editor drops typing when the document changes at the same time

## Summary

When a tool's JSON Schema uses a **top-level combinator** (`oneOf` / `anyOf` / `allOf` / `not` / `if` / `then` / `else`), that constraint **never reaches the `LanguageModelChatProvider`**. It is deleted, and the sub-constraints inside it are downgraded into plain description text.

The model therefore has no way to know the fields are mutually exclusive, fills several of them at once, and the runtime - which still validates against the original schema - rejects every call. This makes a core built-in tool (`write_agent`) **unusable on any BYOK provider**, permanently.

## Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| VS Code | 1.141.0 (commit `2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c`), win32 |
| Copilot Chat extension | 0.69.0 (bundled) |
| Agent host runtime | `@github/copilot-sdk-win32-x64` 1.0.17-unstable.37397886721.gad270aa |
| Bundled CLI runtime (in the Copilot extension) | `@github/copilot` 1.0.73 |
| Model | BYOK, `apiMode: "openai-responses"` registered via a third-party `LanguageModelChatProvider` |

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register a BYOK OpenAI-compatible model and select it in agent mode.
2. Send any message that causes the model to call the built-in `write_agent` tool (i.e. ask it to message a subagent).
3. Observe: the tool call is always rejected, because the model emits `agent_id` + `agent_ids` + `scope` together.

**Control group:** the sibling tool `read_agent` has a single optional selector and `required:["agent_id"]` only - it succeeds **100%** of the time on the same model. Only the tool whose constraint is expressed with `oneOf` fails.

## Evidence A - the source schema is correct

Extracted verbatim from the Copilot SDK/CLI runtime binary (`prebuilds/win32-x64/runtime.node`), identical in both runtimes present on this machine:

```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"agent_id":{"type":"string","description":"The ID of one background agent to send a message to."},"agent_ids":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"minItems":1,"maxItems":16,"uniqueItems":true,"description":"A small explicit set of background agent IDs to send the same message to."},"scope":{"type":"string","enum":["siblings","children"],"description":"Visible agent group to send the same message to. Use only for same-message coordination with all current sibling agents or child/descendant agents."},"message":{"type":"string","description":"The message to send to the selected agent or agents. Steers a running turn or starts the idle agent's next turn."}},"required":["message"],"oneOf":[{"required":["agent_id"],"not":{"anyOf":[{"required":["agent_ids"]},{"required":["scope"]}]}},{"required":["agent_ids"],"not":{"anyOf":[{"required":["agent_id"]},{"required":["scope"]}]}},{"required":["scope"],"not":{"anyOf":[{"required":["agent_id"]},{"required":["agent_ids"]}]}}]}
```

Note `"required":["message"]` and the 3-branch `oneOf` that makes the selector fields mutually exclusive.

## Evidence B - what the `LanguageModelChatProvider` actually receives

Captured in `provideLanguageModelChatResponse(model, messages, options)` from `options.tools`, for the same request (`write_agent`):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "agent_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The ID of one background agent to send a message to."
    },
    "agent_ids": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "{minLength: 1}"
      },
      "description": "A small explicit set of background agent IDs to send the same message to.\n\n{minItems: 1, maxItems: 16, uniqueItems: true}"
    },
    "scope": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["siblings", "children"],
      "description": "Visible agent group to send the same message to. Use only for same-message coordination with all current sibling agents or child/descendant agents."
    },
    "message": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The message to send to the selected agent or agents. Steers a ru
state.title: BYOK: `oneOf` is stripped from tool `inputSchema` and sub-constraints are downgraded into description text, so the model fills mutually exclusive fields

On first launch, the Agents window's new-session composer defaults to **Cloud** instead of **This Computer**, so choosing a local folder fails.

**Steps**

1. In a fresh profile, signed in to GitHub, with the Agents window never opened, click **Try out the new Agents window** on the Welcome page.
2. Look at the environment control above the composer.
3. Finish the tour, then click **Chat** > **Open Folder...** and pick a local folder.

**Expected:** The first draft targets **This Computer** (as in the previous build, `caeec36b`), and the picked folder becomes the workspace.

**Actual:** The environment control shows **Cloud**. After picking the folder, the composer still shows **Chat** and a toast says `Choose a workspace available in Cloud.` with no action. The window log shows the first draft created as `copilot-cloud-agent` at startup, right after `No harness descriptor found for session type local`. Switching to **This Computer** and picking the folder again works.

**Build:** VS Code Insiders 1.145.0-insider (`67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff`), Ubuntu 24.04 arm64.

[image]

Related: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/343502 (same fallback after a reload, fixed), https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/345473 (Cloud's **Open Folder...** always fails).

- Logs: Agent Host debug export captured October 12. Sanitized evidence is included below. The full archive contains credentials/session content and is not attached publicly.

## Follow-up to #340546

WorkIQ and Kusto connector **Sign In** still repeatedly fails in Insiders after the fix in #340547.

The installed build contains the fix: comparing its commit with the merge commit of #340547, `8254ed199b79dec46a5b056c53e1c8a2ed987558`, reports the installed build is 186 commits ahead and zero behind. Installed product metadata predates the captured failures. The exported logs independently identify the Insiders profile, but do not include a definitive build fingerprint, so this verifies the installed build rather than independently identifying the running process's commit.

The earlier PR stops retrying an unchanged token after silent authentication is rejected and restores the Authentication required state. It does not establish that interactive Sign In updates the credential the managed connector actually uses. This report tracks that remaining end-to-end failure, not just the spinner presentation.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open an Agents Window Copilot session containing the WorkIQ and Kusto Copilot connectors.
2. Open Customizations and inspect their MCP server entries. Both require authentication.
3. Use **Sign In** and retry the affected connector.
4. Observe that the connector does not become usable. It returns to `authRequired` with an insufficient-scope challenge despite client logs reporting authentication success.

**Expected:** Sign In obtains the required authorization for the selected account, updates the credential used on subsequent connector requests, and allows tool discovery. A rejected credential produces an actionable failure rather than an unverified success report.

**Actual:** Both connectors remain unable to authenticate. The GitHub connector gateway receives a credential without the required scope. Client-side token forwarding reports success, but subsequent MCP requests still fail.

## Confirmed log evidence

All times in this section are October 12, 2026, Pacific daylight time, UTC-7.

The same session records the failure for both connectors at approximately **10:30:14, 10:34:11, and 10:45:55**.

The affected endpoints are:

- `https://api.github.com/copilot-connectors/api/v1/connectors/kusto/mcp`
- `https://api.github.com/copilot-connectors/api/v1/connectors/workiqmcp/mcp`

Both return:

```text
HTTP 403
WWW-Authenticate challenge:
  error="insufficient_scope"
  scope="write:plugin_gateway_connections"
x-accepted-oauth-scopes: write:plugin_gateway_connections
x-oauth-scopes: read:user, repo, user:email, workflow
body: insufficient OAuth scope
```

Representative ordering:

```text
10:30:13.602  Renderer: MCP authentication succeeded for [Kusto connector]
10:30:13.627  Renderer: MCP authentication succeeded for [WorkIQ connector]
10:30:14.556  SDK: Kusto mcp.oauth_required, reason=upscope, HTTP 403
10:30:14.634  SDK: WorkIQ mcp.oauth_required, reason=upscope, HTTP 403
```

The client forwards `authenticate` requests with `scopes: ["write:plugin_gateway_connections"]`. All 239 matched connector authenticate RPCs across the captured client connection return `{}` without a JSON-RPC error. That count includes other sessions and automatic activity; it is not 239 manual sign-in attempts in the affected session.

Follow-up to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318422. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344955 fixed this for the **Copilot (Agent Host)** harness and the **Agents window**: same-named agents get a source caption (`Extension: …`, `Plugin: …`). In the **Local** harness, the agent picker still shows identical rows.

Found while verifying the fix on VS Code Insiders `1.145.0-insider` (commit `67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff`), Ubuntu 24.04 arm64.

## Repro

1. Install two extensions that each contribute an agent named `Reviewer` through `contributes.chatAgents`. Also enable a plugin (`chat.plugins.enabled` and `chat.pluginLocations`) that has `agents/reviewer.agent.md` with `name: Reviewer`.
2. Open Chat, choose the **Local** harness, and open the agent picker (**Ctrl+.**).

**Expected:** like the Copilot harness, each `Reviewer` shows its source (`Extension: <display name>` or `Plugin: <name>`), and unique names stay plain.

**Actual:** three identical `Reviewer` rows. The only way to tell them apart is the hover tooltip, which shows each agent's authored `description`. After you pick one, the input chip also just reads `Reviewer`.

In the Copilot harness, the same setup shows the captions and runs the correct agent for each selection, including switching mid-session.

Related: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/312256 asks to *deduplicate* same-named org-synced and local agents by precedence. This issue is about *labeling* distinct agents from different sources.

This issue stems from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335655. When Fira Code and font ligatures are used, the font is not considered monospace, even though it is.

We should change `_actualReadFontInfo` so that we measure the width of character sets that typically are joined using font ligatures like `fi`, `ff`, `<=` and `=>` and verify this width is roughly equal to twice the width of one space. Essentially we should verify the font remains monospace even when font ligatures are turned on.

state.body:
- VS Code Version: Code - Insiders 1.142.0-insider (f4dfb91d30e). The code path is unchanged on `main` at 38d9885c158.
- OS Version: macOS 27.0.1 (arm64)

When a message send makes the Agent Host refresh a Copilot chat's session configuration, every canvas open in that chat closes in the Agents window and doesn't come back.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Enable `chat.canvases.enabled` and, in the Agents window, start a new local Copilot session in a new worktree.
2. Have the agent open a canvas (`open_canvas`) in the first turn. It opens as a tab in the side pane.
3. Send a follow-up message in the same chat.

**Expected:** The canvas stays open. At most it's briefly unavailable while its provider reconnects, as with an extension reload.

**Actual:** The canvas tab closes and doesn't reopen. The runtime still has the instance open: `invoke_canvas_action` calls on it keep succeeding, and calling `open_canvas` again with the same `instanceId` brings it back, as a new tab.

`agenthost.log` shows the send restarting the SDK session. The same pattern was observed in two chats:

```
11:01:11.457Z [Copilot:…] Session configuration changed, refreshing session: operation=sendMessage, …, reason=clientPluginsChanged
11:01:11.459Z [Copilot:…] SDK session disconnect RPC started …
11:01:11.514Z [Copilot:…] Preparing SDK session: kind=resume …
```

The Agents window's AHP log shows the host publishing an empty canvas list at the same instant:

```
11:01:11.459Z s2c chat/canvasesChanged   (no canvases)
11:01:11.459Z c2s unsubscribe ahp-canvas:/…
```

### Root cause

1. [`_refreshSessionConfiguration`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/38d9885c15878f05c638755aedf59d1c760df4b3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts#L4922) [destroys the live SDK session](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/38d9885c15878f05c638755aedf59d1c760df4b3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts#L4980) and resumes it whenever the chat's configuration snapshot changed.
2. [`destroySession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/38d9885c15878f05c638755aedf59d1c760df4b3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L4907) calls [`_clearCanvasProjection`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/38d9885c15878f05c638755aedf59d1c760df4b3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3336), which publishes `ChatCanvasesChanged` with no canvases. The Agents window treats this as authoritative membership and [closes the canvas editors](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/38d9885c15878f05c638755aedf59d1c760df4b3/src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/electron-browser/sessionCanvasService.ts#L104).
3. The replacement session's [`initializeSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/38d9885c15878f05c638755aedf59d1c760df4b3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3211) adds every instance in `wrapper.session.openCanvases` to `_ignoredRestoredCanvasInstanceIds`, and projection starts out not ready, so the runtime's rehydration `session.canvas.opened` events are [dropped](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/38d9885c15878f05c638755aedf59d1c760df4b3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L9046). Nothing re-projects the canvas, even though the runtime still has it open.

This follows the [documented contract](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/38d9885c15878f05c638755aedf59d1c760df4b3/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/AGENT_HOST_SESSIONS_PROVIDER.md?plain=1#L130) ("A new SDK residency starts with an empty projected canvas collection and does not restore prior open canvases"), but a configuration refresh of a chat that's in use is currently treated as a new residency.

### Why the refresh happens in this flow

state.body:
Follow-up to #305870.

## The problem in one sentence

In an Agents window **folder session** (Branch mode, no worktree), clicking **Commit** makes the **Create PR** button disappear. If the branch has no upstream yet, which is normal for a new local branch, nothing replaces it: no Create PR and no Sync Changes. There is then no way to push or open a PR from the Agents window.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Take a git repo with a GitHub remote and create a local branch that has never been pushed: `git checkout -b feature/greeting`.
2. In the Agents window, start a new session: pick that folder, set the mode to **Branch** (not New Worktree).
3. Ask the agent to create a file and do not commit. **Create PR** is shown in the title bar, which is the expected behavior.
4. Open the Changes view, switch to the **Uncommitted** tab, and click **Commit**. The commit succeeds in about 2 seconds.

## Actual behavior

Right after the commit, **Create PR** disappears from the title bar and the Changes view shows "No changed files". There is no other PR or push action anywhere. The session cannot move forward from the Agents window.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad7ef55f-c4e2-4ca5-a3ba-f4e01f2d986f

## Expected behavior

There should still be a way to continue after committing. For example, keep offering **Create PR**, since the create-PR operation already pushes the branch itself, or offer a **Publish Branch** / **Push** action when the branch has no upstream.

## Why this happens (from reading the code)

- [`agentHostPullRequestOperationProvider.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostPullRequestOperationProvider.ts) (`_computeOperations`) returns no operations for a folder session as soon as it has outgoing (unpushed) commits: `if (isFolderSession && gitState?.outgoingChanges && gitState.outgoingChanges > 0) return undefined;`. This rule was added in #333133 and applies to every changeset tab, so committing hides Create PR.
- [`agentHostSyncOperationProvider.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostSyncOperationProvider.ts) only offers **Sync Changes** when the branch already has an upstream (`if (!gitState?.upstreamBranchName) return undefined;`). A branch that was never pushed has none.
- Together, a never-pushed branch gets neither action after the commit, which is the dead end above.

I did not check in the UI what happens when the branch already has an upstream. From the code I expect **Sync Changes N↑** to appear, and **Create PR** to come back after syncing.

## Related case: folder session on `main`

On `main`, **Create PR** works while the changes are uncommitted: it creates a new branch, commits, pushes and opens the PR. After clicking **Commit** first, the same rule hides it, and **Sync Changes** (if offered) would push the commit straight to `main`.

## Environment

Code OSS dev build of `main` (1.145.0), macOS. The repo had a GitHub remote URL and no upstream on the branch.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.
state.title: Agents window: no way to open a PR after committing in a folder session

state.body:
- VS Code Version: 1.143.0-insider (commit e9f10b90b508)
- OS Version: Windows 11 with WSL 2 (Ubuntu 24.04)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install VS Code Insiders on Windows and keep the default that adds the `copilot` command to PATH (`{app}\bin\copilot-shim` is on the user PATH).
2. Open a WSL shell outside VS Code, for example Ubuntu in Windows Terminal.
3. Run `code-insiders .`. It works: VS Code opens the folder in WSL.
4. Run `copilot`.

## Expected

`copilot` works in WSL like `code` does. It runs GitHub Copilot CLI in the distro, or offers to install it, through the Linux `copilot` shim that the VS Code Server already ships.

## Actual

```text
$ command -v code-insiders
/mnt/c/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft VS Code Insiders/bin/code-insiders
$ copilot
copilot: command not found
```

WSL appends the Windows PATH, so `/mnt/c/.../Microsoft VS Code Insiders/bin/copilot-shim` is on the WSL PATH. That folder only contains `copilot.exe`, though, so Linux shells don't find a `copilot` command. `code` works because `bin` also contains a POSIX `code` script next to `code.cmd`, which hands off to the VS Code Server in WSL.

## What already works

- The VS Code Server ships the Linux shim. Remote-WSL installed it at `~/.vscode-server-insiders/bin/<commit>/bin/copilot-shim/copilot`, next to the server's `node`.
- Integrated terminals in a WSL window resolve `copilot` once Copilot Chat is active. Copilot Chat appends `<server>/bin/copilot-shim` to the terminal PATH, with `:` as the separator. I verified this end to end with Remote-WSL 0.104.3 and Insiders e9f10b90b508.
- Remote-SSH integrated terminals use the same remote extension host path. A plain SSH session outside VS Code has neither `code` nor `copilot`, so SSH has no equivalent gap.

## Proposal

Ship a POSIX `copilot` launcher next to `copilot.exe` in `bin\copilot-shim`, like `bin\code` next to `code.cmd`:

- **WSL:** run the Linux shim from the distro's VS Code Server, preferring the server for the same commit and falling back to the newest installed one. If no server is installed yet, print how to set it up.
- **Git Bash and Cygwin:** run `copilot.exe`, as those shells do today.

Windows shells keep running `copilot.exe`, because they ignore extensionless files. Setup publishes and removes the launcher together with the shim, so the `CopilotCliCommand` policy and the Copilot CLI choice still decide whether the command exists.

state.body:
- VS Code Version: 1.142.0
- OS Version: macOS 26.7.1

## Summary

On macOS the main process runs with the default libuv threadpool of 4 threads. 2 of them are held for the whole process lifetime by `vscode-policy-watcher` (`PolicyWatcher::Execute` waiting on a semaphore).
All `fs` work the main process does on behalf of every window shares the remaining 2 threads.

When 2 `open()` calls are slow, the pool is exhausted and every window stalls:
- no window can open or save files, or expand folders in the Explorer, until the slow opens return
- closing any window shows "Discarding backups is taking a bit longer..." and the renderer logs `onBeforeShutdown is taking a long time, pending operations: veto.backups`
- everything recovers at the same moment once the slow opens return

That can be the case when file access is slow e.g. on a slow filesystem or also due to security scanners like Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

It also happens with `--disable-extensions`, because opening a window still reads the `package.json` of every installed extension through the main process.

## Steps to Reproduce:

Either  
Open VS Code where e.g. the Extension files are on a slow filesystem

Or  
1. In Terminal.app (not the VS Code terminal, which sets `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`), start a separate instance with a threadpool of 2:
   `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=2 code --user-data-dir /tmp/vsc-ud --extensions-dir /tmp/vsc-ext /tmp`
2. The window never finishes loading. `main.log` stops after `[shared storage] Fallback application storage initialized`.
3. `sample <main pid> 2`: both `libuv-worker` threads sit in `PolicyWatcher::Execute` (`semaphore_wait_trap`).
4. With `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=3` the same command starts normally.

## Expected

A slow `open()` for one window's request delays only that request. Other windows keep working, and closing a window does not wait on unrelated file I/O.

## Actual

One slow `open()` per free thread blocks file access for all windows, because the shared pool has only 2 usable threads.

## Maybe Related

- #321902
- #327479
- #337272

## Possible fixes

- Run the policy watchers on a dedicated thread instead of a libuv pool worker (`Napi::AsyncProgressQueueWorker` occupies a pool thread for its whole lifetime).
- Set a larger `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE` for the main process.
- Avoid re-reading every installed extension's `package.json` through the main process on each window open.

## Workaround

Start VS Code with ENV `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=32`
state.title: Main process policy watchers permanently hold 2 of 4 libuv threads on macOS. Slow open() stalls file access in all windows

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Enable the Customizations Marketplace and its configured sources.
2. Run **Chat: Open Customizations** and open **Browse**.
3. Wait for marketplace content from the configured feeds to load.

**Actual:** Browse can take approximately 17 seconds to populate. The connectors endpoint appears to be a significant contributor. During this time, the UI does not explain which sources are still loading or how much work remains.

**Expected:** Browse should show useful content promptly, avoid blocking all results on a slow source, and communicate incremental progress such as sources explored or loaded. Reopening Browse should avoid repeating unchanged network work when cached data is safe to reuse.

## Investigation

- Add privacy-safe telemetry for each source request and total Browse loading time, including success/failure, duration, timeout, and cache hit/miss. Do not collect query contents, feed contents, URLs, or other user data.
- Determine whether sources can load and render independently so one slow endpoint does not block other results.
- Explore in-memory and persistent caching for marketplace responses, including TTL and invalidation when source configuration, authentication, policy, or installed state changes.
- Consider stale-while-revalidate behavior so cached content can render immediately while sources refresh in the background.
- Add meaningful progress feedback, for example sources explored/loaded out of the total, while preserving source-specific errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A slow source does not prevent already available source results from rendering.
- The UI communicates applicable loading progress rather than remaining static for the entire request.
- Repeat visits reuse valid cached results and refresh according to a documented invalidation strategy.
- Telemetry can identify which source category contributes to latency without collecting content or sensitive endpoint data.
- Targeted tests cover incremental loading, cache reuse/invalidation, slow or failed sources, and progress state.

state.body:
The multi-diff editor (seen in the Agents window **Changes** view) sometimes renders broken: the file header disappears, the diff is cut off partway down the editor, and the rest of the editor is blank. Scrolling the multi-diff editor fixes it.

**Root cause:** the browser natively scrolls the multi-diff editor's `overflow: hidden` `.scrollContent` element. The virtualized layout doesn't expect that and nothing resets it, so every rendered item is shifted up by that hidden offset.

## Version

```

```

## Symptoms

[image]

- The sticky file header (`code-no-timeout-polling-loop.ts … +153 -0`) is gone; the diff starts mid-function at line 44.
- The diff ends about halfway down the editor and the area below is empty.
- The original side shows only the "no content" hatch pattern.

## Evidence

I attached a debugger to the live renderer of the broken window and inspected the DOM.

**1. `.scrollContent` had a non-zero native scroll offset.** It was the only element inside the multi-diff editor with one:

```
DIV.scrollContent  scrollTop=465.6  scrollHeight=9610  clientHeight=858
```

This element has `overflow: hidden`, and its scroll position is owned by the `SmoothScrollableElement` in `CompressedVirtualizedScrollView`. Its native `scrollTop` is expected to be `0`.

**2. The rendered geometry is shifted by exactly that offset.** The editor is at `y=117` and the visible `.multiDiffEntry` is laid out correctly by the virtualized layout (`top: 858.2px` inside a `translateY(-858.2px)` container). But the header renders at `y=-348`: 117 − 465.6 ≈ −348. The header and the top 465.6px of the item are above the viewport, and the bottom 465.6px of the viewport has no content.

| element | style (from layout) | actual `getBoundingClientRect().y` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.multiDiffEditor` | – | 117 |
| `.multiDiffEntry` (visible) | `top: 858.2px` within `translateY(-858.2px)` | **−348** (expected 117) |
| `.header` | `translateY(0px)` | **−348** (expected 117) |

**3. Resetting the native scroll offset immediately fixes rendering.** Running `document.querySelector('.multiDiffEditor .scrollContent').scrollTop = 0` in the live window, without changing anything else, gives:

[image]

**4. The trigger is focus and caret movement inside an embedded diff editor.** I added a capturing `scroll` listener and drove the window with clicks and cursor keys inside a diff. It recorded repeated native scrolls of `.scrollContent` to `16.2`, `36`, and `0` while `document.activeElement` was the editor's `.native-edit-context`. 36px is the file header height. When the editor's input element (EditContext) is focused or moved to follow the cursor, Chromium scrolls the nearest scrollable ancestor to keep it in view. That ancestor is `.scrollContent`, because `overflow: hidden` still allows programmatic scrolling. The window remained in the broken state after one of these runs. It doesn't reproduce on demand: it depends on where the caret is relative to the outer viewport.

## Root cause

[`CompressedVirtualizedScrollView`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c44c5332b31c31eca0519ff6e7c5ebb9da0711e6/src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/compressedVirtualizedScrollView.ts#L96) renders items into `div.scrollContent` and positions them itself from the `SmoothScrollableElement` scroll position. Nothing undoes a native scroll of `.scrollContent`, so once the browser scrolls it, the browser's offset is added on top of the virtual one and stays there.

`ListView` already guards against this ([listView.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c44c5332b31c31eca0519ff6e7c5ebb9da0711e6/src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts#L454-L461)): it listens for native `scroll` on its scrollable DOM node, resets `scrollTop` to 0, and moves the offset into its virtual scroll position. The multi-diff editor has never had an equivalent guard, including before the virtualized-scroll refactor (33494d30170 / 10de1b93436).

## Suggested fix

Add the same guard to `Compresse

state.body:
### Environment

- VS Code: 1.141.1
- Commit: 7baac39ec3ca969dab74ac12c097f6a486e46593
- Windows desktop client connected to WSL Ubuntu
- Remote - WSL extension: 0.104.3
- Affected extension: OpenAI Codex (`openai.chatgpt`)
- Codex versions tested in WSL: 26.1007.21434 and 26.930.31730

### Description

The Codex Webview fails to load when I open VS Code from an Ubuntu terminal using `code .`.

This workflow worked before October 13, 2026. Local updater logs show that VS Code completed an update on that day. I suspect an update regression, although I have not tested the previous VS Code version.

Both Codex versions listed above exhibit the failure.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Windows VS Code with the Remote - WSL extension and a WSL distribution named `Ubuntu`.
2. Install the Codex extension in WSL.
3. From an Ubuntu terminal, open a project with:
   ```bash
   code .
   ```
4. Open the Codex sidebar.
5. The Webview fails to initialize.

### Expected behavior

The Codex sidebar loads normally when VS Code is launched using `code .` from WSL.

### Actual behavior

Webview JavaScript and CSS requests return HTTP 401. The Windows renderer log reports:

```text
Webview.loadLocalResource - trying to load resource.
requestUri=vscode-remote://wsl%2Bubuntu/home/zlyt/.vscode-server/extensions/openai.chatgpt-26.1007.21434-linux-x64/webview/assets/index-6d5eb9bd4867.js,
resourceToLoad=undefined

Webview.loadLocalResource - access denied.
requestUri=vscode-remote://wsl%2Bubuntu/home/zlyt/.vscode-server/extensions/openai.chatgpt-26.1007.21434-linux-x64/webview/assets/index-6d5eb9bd4867.js,
resourceToLoad=undefined
```

The WSL extension log shows that the Codex app-server initializes successfully, followed by:

```text
Webview renderer did not become ready
elapsedMs=30000
extensionVersion=26.1007.21434
reason=renderer_ready_timeout
receivedWebviewMessage=false
role=sidebar
stage=renderer
timeoutMs=30000
```

### Investigation

The WSL launch script constructs the connection authority using:

```sh
AUTHORITY="wsl+$WSL_DISTRO_NAME"
```

Here, `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` is `Ubuntu`, so the connection authority is `wsl+Ubuntu`. However, the failing Webview resource requests use `wsl+ubuntu`.

In the installed VS Code bundle, `loadResource()` uses a strict comparison between the connection's `remoteAuthority` and the resource URI's `authority` before obtaining the remote OS.

When these differ in casing, `remoteOS` remains undefined. The resource resolver then returns early, before checking the resource roots or reading the file. This produces `AccessDenied`, which is mapped to HTTP 401.

An isolated check using the installed OS-selection and resource-loading functions reproduced this behavior. The URI and filesystem services in that check were test doubles, not a live Webview.

The current Codex Webview assets exist and are readable, and its extension code sets `localResourceRoots` and uses `asWebviewUri()`.

### Confirmed workaround

Opening a new window with an explicitly lowercase authority restores the Codex UI:

```bash
code --new-window --remote wsl+ubuntu .
```

This suggests that inconsistent authority casing is responsible for the resource-loading failure.

Could you investigate whether the remote OS lookup should use a normalized or case-insensitive authority comparison?
state.title: WSL Webview resources return 401 due to remoteAuthority casing mismatch (wsl+Ubuntu vs wsl+ubuntu)

- VS Code Version: 1.144.0-insider (7cc5e7382b284f2156375fcedc388b44a07c0487)
- OS Version: macOS 26.7.1 (Apple silicon)

When the sticky scroll overlay's WebGL context is lost and not restored, the overlay keeps the lost canvas: a white bar with Chromium's sad-face placeholder where the command should be. The terminal itself falls back to the DOM renderer in the same situation after 3 seconds. The overlay never does, so it stays broken until the window is reloaded or `terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration` is toggled.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Set `"terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration": "on"`, open a terminal with shell integration (the default), and run `seq 1 200` so sticky scroll shows `seq 1 200`.
2. Run **Developer: Toggle Developer Tools** and evaluate:
   ```js
   document.querySelector('.terminal-sticky-scroll .xterm-screen canvas:not([class])').getContext('webgl2').getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context').loseContext()
   ```
3. Wait more than 3 seconds, then run `seq 1 100`.

**Expected:** like the terminal, the overlay falls back to the DOM renderer and shows `seq 1 100`.
**Actual:** 13 seconds later, after new commands, the overlay is still a white bar (screenshot).

[image]

A real GPU process loss gives the same result when Chromium doesn't restore WebGL contexts, which happened after repeated GPU process restarts. Both terminals fell back to the DOM renderer and rendered correctly, while both sticky scroll overlays kept the sad face (screenshot).

[image]

### Cause

`TerminalStickyScrollOverlay._refreshGpuAcceleration` ([terminalStickyScrollOverlay.ts#L510-L526](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/fb04e9e3d8e4bc56375e4795d7fdc8ff4293f2b3/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/stickyScroll/browser/terminalStickyScrollOverlay.ts#L510-L526)) loads a `WebglAddon` but never subscribes to `onContextLoss`. `XtermTerminal._enableWebglRenderer` does subscribe, and disposes the addon ([xtermTerminal.ts#L956-L961](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/fb04e9e3d8e4bc56375e4795d7fdc8ff4293f2b3/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/xterm/xtermTerminal.ts#L956-L961)).

History: WebGL for sticky scroll was added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/218941; the terminal's DOM fallback is from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/120400.

### Possible fix

Subscribe to `onContextLoss` in `_refreshGpuAcceleration` and clear `_webglAddon`.

`_syncOptions` calls `_refreshGpuAcceleration` again on every terminal resize, configuration change and theme change ([terminalStickyScrollOverlay.ts#L478-L487](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/fb04e9e3d8e4bc56375e4795d7fdc8ff4293f2b3/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/stickyScroll/browser/terminalStickyScrollOverlay.ts#L478-L487)), so it would recreate the addon immediately. Loading the addon throws while WebGL2 is unavailable. Before re-enabling, either remember the loss or follow the terminal's own renderer.

---

Since the Electron 43 update (#332935), the workbench takes about twice as long to load in dev builds. The update replaced the `vscode-file://` handler in [`protocolMainService.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/protocol/electron-main/protocolMainService.ts): `registerFileProtocol` (Chromium serves the file) became `protocol.handle` + `net.fetch(file://…)` (each response is fetched and returned through the main process). Dev builds load thousands of separate module files through this handler on every launch.

This is the main cause of the Linux Electron smoke tests hitting their 20-minute timeout (#341382).

## Evidence

**CI** (Linux / Electron-Smoke, about 110 successful PR runs from Sep 8 to Oct 13, timed from `smoke-test-runner.log`). Process launch, first window and app exit times did not change. Only the wait from the first window to the `.monaco-workbench` element increased, per launch:

| Runner class | Before Electron 43 (wait / step) | After Electron 43 (wait / step) |
|---|---|---|
| Slow | ~7.2s / 740–824s | ~12.2s / 1080–1200s |
| Fast | ~4.7s / 590–650s | ~8.4s / 810–1000s |

Controlled comparison on the same `main` base and the same slow runner class: the Electron 43 PR's own run ([35055495194](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/35055495194)) took 12.2s per launch and 1019s for the step. Runs without Electron 43 an hour later ([35056430179](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/35056430179), [35056485997](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/35056485997)) took 6.3s per launch and 756–773s for the step.

**Local A/B** (macOS, dev build, Electron 43.7.7, alternating runs of the Launch / Multiroot / Quick Open smoke suites). Only the `vscode-file://` handler differs; the number is the wait for `.monaco-workbench`:

| `vscode-file://` handler | Wait |
|---|---|
| `protocol.handle` + `net.fetch` (current) | 3.0–3.2s |
| `registerFileProtocol` (before Electron 43) | 1.5–1.9s |
| `protocol.handle` returning a `Response` built from `fs.readFile` | 2.0–2.2s |

## Open questions

- Should we go back to the deprecated `registerFileProtocol` for `vscode-file://` for now? It still exists in Electron 43 with no removal scheduled. That change is drafted locally for #341382.
- Is there a faster way to use `protocol.handle` for this? Upstream electron/electron#42612 ("protocol.handle is very slow") was closed as completed on 2026-09-25 with no linked fix, so it's unclear whether any fix is in our Electron version.
- Are packaged builds affected? They load far fewer, larger files, so the effect on users' startup is unmeasured. It may be worth checking startup telemetry from before and after the Electron 43 update.
state.title: Workbench loads ~2x slower in dev builds since Electron 43 (vscode-file:// handler moved to protocol.handle + net.fetch)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Use Copilot canvas customizations, including a user-scoped `brainstorm-board` provider, and open the customization/canvas UI.
2. Leave conversations idle and observe intermittent canvas availability flicker. Separately, open canvases sometimes refresh during longer runs. This is intermittent; no minimal deterministic reproduction yet.

Expected: Canvas definitions remain stable while idle; background discovery should not temporarily remove available canvases or unnecessarily restart providers.

### Evidence from the idle occurrence

Analysis of the final minutes of an Agent Host debug export on October 19, 2026, approximately 18:10–18:13:50 PDT:

- No `chat/turnStarted` or `chat/turnComplete` actions in that window's captured client AHP stream.
- 224 `chat/canvasesChanged` notifications, all without an open-canvas membership list, and 1,800 MCP `notifications/tools/list_changed` notifications.
- Retained host logs covering 18:12:15–18:13:48 contain 125 repetitions of `brainstorm-board canvas ready` across nine SDK sessions (13–14 per session).
- SDK logs show repeated warm attachments and extension rediscovery; there is also repeated plugin-lockfile filesystem activity. These are correlated signals, not proof of the initiating trigger.

### Suspected lifecycle/UI interaction

`CopilotAgentSession` forwards `session.canvas.registry_changed` by republishing `chat/canvasesChanged`. `SessionCanvasRegistryService` refreshes definitions on each emission. `CanvasDefinitionStore` retains definitions while a request is pending or fails, but accepts a successful transiently empty listing. Provider unregister/re-register churn can therefore make available canvas entries disappear and return.

For an open canvas, `CanvasEditor` detaches when the source becomes unavailable and loads again when it returns with a changed URL. However, this idle capture contains no `canvas/stateChanged` events on the captured client connection, so an actual open-panel URL change is not established by this occurrence.

Please investigate unnecessary background provider reinitialization and whether registry refreshes need atomic/readiness-aware publication. The caller initiating the repeated lifecycle work is not yet identified; `brainstorm-board` may be a witness rather than the cause.

The debug archive contains private data and is intentionally not attached publicly; Harald has the original export.

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: bundled (VS Code 1.141.0)
- VS Code Version: 1.141.0
- OS Version: Windows 11 (also present on a second machine with the same version)
- Feature: agent sessions running in the local agent host process (the mode picker option "Copilot (runs the Copilot SDK agent in a local agent host process)")
- Selected model: any BYOK model via a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (verified through a local logging proxy)
- Logs: outgoing request timings captured at a local OpenAI-compatible proxy (details below)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a BYOK provider with an OpenAI-compatible base URL.
2. In the chat mode picker, choose the agent host option ("Copilot (runs the Copilot SDK agent in a local agent host process)") rather than "Local".
3. Send a prompt that produces a longer answer (thinking + body).
4. Observe: nothing renders incrementally. The full content (reasoning and body) appears at once when the turn completes.
5. Press Stop while the turn is running: the request to the provider **keeps running** (visible at the proxy / provider logs) until it completes on its own.
6. A/B control: in the same window, switch the mode picker to "Local" and repeat — streaming renders incrementally and Stop terminates the provider request immediately.

## Actual result

- No incremental display of reasoning/body — the whole response is emitted at completion time.
- Cancel does not propagate to the provider; the upstream request runs to completion (billing/tokens still consumed).
- Tool-call progress is also not shown live (tool invocations appear only after the turn finishes) — possibly the same root cause, listed here as a suspected co-symptom.

## Expected result

The agent-host path should stream incrementally like the "Local" path, and Stop should cancel the in-flight provider request.

## Root cause hypothesis (source-level, from reading current main)

The BYOK LM bridge appears to be buffered by design:

- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostClientByokLmChannel.ts` — its doc comment states `chat()` "ships the request to the renderer and **resolves with the buffered completion** the renderer produced from the LM API".
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/byokLmProxyService.ts` — `bridgeResultToResponsesSseFrames` synthesizes SSE frames from the buffered result after completion, which matches the "everything at once" rendering and the missing live tool-call progress.
- Cancellation seemingly does not cross the reverse-RPC bridge back to the renderer's LM API request.

For machine-driven agent turns this is tolerable, but for interactive use the mode picker makes it easy to land in this path for regular chat, and the experience regression vs. the "Local" path is severe (no live tokens, no effective Stop, provider cost keeps accruing after cancel).

## Relationship to recent work

#339830 (forwarding tool-result images across this same BYOK bridge) recently landed — great to see this path under active maintenance. Streaming and cancellation feel like the next gaps on the same bridge.

## Workaround

Switch the chat mode picker back to "Local" for interactive use.
state.title: Agent-host sessions with BYOK models: responses are buffered until completion — no incremental streaming, cancel does not reach the provider

- OS Version: macOS 27.2 (the underlying logic is platform-independent)

## Description

Eligible chat tips in the Agents Window New Session view do not remain visible after the workbench finishes restoring. A tip can briefly flash during initialization, then disappear once foreground-chat counting settles. Returning from another foreground chat to New Session also fails to reset tip rotation, so previously hidden tips remain hidden.

This affects standard catalog tips and contextual provider tips, including connector recommendations. It does not bypass `chat.tips.enabled`: the problem occurs only for users who have tips enabled and are otherwise eligible.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure `chat.tips.enabled` is enabled.
2. Start at least two Agents Window sessions so the first-run tip suppression threshold has been reached.
3. Open the Agents Window New Session view with no other foreground chat surface.
4. Wait for the workbench to finish restoring.
5. Observe an otherwise eligible tip. For a deterministic contextual-tip repro when connector recommendations are enabled, enter a recognized URL such as `https://www.notion.so/example` in the New Session prompt.
6. Optionally open another foreground chat and return to New Session.

## Actual

The tip may flash during initialization, but it is removed once the shared foreground-session count becomes `1`. Returning from multiple foreground chats (`2`) to the sole New Session composer (`1`) does not reset the tip session.

## Expected

When New Session is the sole foreground chat surface and all normal tip gates pass, the tip remains visible and usable. Returning from another foreground chat resets tip rotation so an eligible tip can be selected again.

## Root Cause

The New Session composer owns one visible internal chat widget, so its settled foreground-session count is `1`. The presenter treated `0` as the sole-composer state for both eligibility and session reset. Component fixtures also forced the count to `0`, masking the production regression.

## Problem

Team-assigned plugins can install successfully, but VS Code's displayed enablement state can disagree with the SDK/runtime's effective state.

The [investigation](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/343845#issuecomment-6374814166) found a Team-default plugin whose skills were enabled in runtime session inventory while Agent Customizations and `/plugin list` showed it as disabled. VS Code also forwarded `enabled: false` as a client customization without an explicit user-disable decision.

The persisted installation flag is not sufficient to determine effective enablement. The runtime deliberately installs Team-default plugins with that flag set to false and applies the default during session activation, without turning it into a permanent personal opt-in.

## Expected behavior

- The SDK/runtime is the source of truth for Copilot plugin enablement. VS Code reflects its resolved state rather than maintaining a conflicting enablement state.
- Enable and disable actions use the SDK and preserve the user's explicit choice across new sessions and restarts.
- A Team default applies when there is no explicit user choice, subject to higher-level policy. It must not be persisted as a personal opt-in.
- VS Code does not forward a disabled override merely because the persisted installation flag is false.
- Agent Customizations, `/plugin list`, and actual contribution availability agree. The experience also needs to handle opening Customizations before the first user chat, including prewarmed sessions.

## Verification

1. With no existing personal enable/disable choice, receive a Team-default plugin. Verify it appears enabled and an included skill or agent actually works.
2. Disable it in VS Code. Verify it is unavailable in a new session and remains disabled after restart.
3. Enable it again. Verify its contributions return and unrelated plugins retain their state.

The investigation comment's API options describe earlier exploration, not a settled implementation requirement. This issue tracks VS Code's alignment with SDK/runtime enablement, not marketplace visibility.

### Webviews render blank in WSL remote windows after updating to 1.141.1 (resources return 401)

**Summary**
Since the auto-update to VS Code 1.141.1, every webview in a WSL remote window renders
completely blank (e.g. Markdown Preview and the Claude Code extension panel). The webview's
own resources (`index.js`, `index.css`) fail to load with HTTP 401. Downgrading to 1.140
fixes the issue immediately with no other changes.

**Environment**
- VS Code: 1.141.1 (stable, commit 7baac39ec3ca969dab74ac12c097f6a486e46593, User Installer)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300
- Remote: WSL (Ubuntu), Remote - WSL extension 0.104.3
- Last working version: 1.140

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a folder in WSL (Ubuntu) with VS Code 1.141.1.
2. Open any `.md` file and run "Markdown: Open Preview" (Ctrl+Shift+V),
   or open any extension webview (e.g. Claude Code panel).

**Expected**
The webview renders its content.

**Actual**
The webview tab/panel stays empty. Webview DevTools console shows:

    index.css:1 Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 ()

The extensions themselves activate normally (extension host logs show no errors related

state.body:
In an Agent Host (Copilot CLI) session, calling the `create_pull_request` tool always reports `Failed to create pull request: Callback URL is required`. This happens even though the tool the model loaded is the one forwarded from the GitHub Pull Requests extension (`github-pull-request_create_pull_request`, reference name `create_pull_request`).

The logs show that two handlers run for the same tool call ID:

1. The window runs the GitHub Pull Requests extension's tool and sends a `chat/toolCallComplete` with that tool's own result.
2. The Copilot runtime also runs its **built-in** `create_pull_request` tool, which belongs to the cloud coding agent and needs a cloud-agent callback URL. Its failure is the result the model receives.

The extension's result never reaches the model.

### Versions

- VS Code Insiders 1.142.0-insider (`363a43fb9eb3`)
- GitHub Copilot Chat 0.70.2026101201 (bundled `@github/copilot` 1.0.73)
- GitHub Pull Requests 0.169.2026101204

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start an Agent Host Copilot session in a worktree for a GitHub repo, and push a branch.
2. Ask the agent to open a PR so that it calls `create_pull_request`.
3. The tool fails with `Failed to create pull request: Callback URL is required`.

### Logs (same tool call `toolu_01UoRDXLuv4Tmqh7U3Ej6sXq`)

`renderer.log`: the extension tool runs in the window. In this run it also failed, for an unrelated reason covered below.

```
15:03:45.247 [info] [AgentHost] Running client tool: create_pull_request (callId=toolu_01UoRDXLuv4Tmqh7U3Ej6sXq, withContext=true)
15:03:45.248 [error] [LanguageModelToolsService#invokeTool] Error from tool github-pull-request_create_pull_request ...
    No repository found for microsoft/vscode. Make sure to have the repository open.
15:03:45.249 [warning] [AgentHost] Client tool failed: create_pull_request No repository found for microsoft/vscode. Make sure to have the repository open.
```

AHP transport log: the client's completion is accepted, then a second completion from the runtime arrives about 30 ms later. The model sees the second one.

```
19:03:45.249Z c2s chat/toolCallComplete  error: "No repository found for microsoft/vscode. Make sure to have the repository open."
19:03:45.279Z s2c chat/toolCallComplete  text:  "Failed to create pull request: Callback URL is required"
```

`agenthost.log`:

```
15:03:45.245 [info] [Copilot:<session>] Tool started: create_pull_request
15:03:45.249 [info] [AgentSideEffects] Forwarding client tool completion: source=client-dispatch, ...
15:03:45.278 [info] [Copilot:<session>] Tool completed: toolu_01UoRDXLuv4Tmqh7U3Ej6sXq
```

### Likely cause

[`_createClientSdkTools`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5feeff21bb532301a539383f49289c8d34a33d14/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L2917) forwards client tools under their reference name. It only sets `overridesBuiltInTool` for tools listed in [`CLIENT_TOOL_SDK_POLICIES`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5feeff21bb532301a539383f49289c8d34a33d14/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L143), and today that's only semantic search. So the forwarded `create_pull_request` has the same name as the runtime's built-in tool, and the runtime appears to execute its built-in tool. The SDK docs say a name clash without `overridesBuiltInTool` should be an error, but here the clash seems to go unreported.

### Impact

- `create_pull_request` can't succeed from a local Agent Host session; the model always gets the error above.
- If the extension tool **does** succeed, the PR gets created while the agent is told it failed. The agent then retries or falls back to `gh pr create`, which risks duplicate attempts and extra turns. I see the agent fall back to `gh` regularly.

### Possible fixes

- Set `overridesBuiltInTool` when forwarding a client tool whose name matches a runtime built-in, at least for `create_pull_request`.
- Or exclude the runtime's built-in `create_pull_request` in local Agent
state.title: Agent Host: create_pull_request runs the runtime's built-in tool instead of the GitHub Pull Requests extension's tool

## Summary

`remote.portsAttributes` accepts port ranges, but a matching range rule with `requireLocalPort: true` does not show the documented warning when forwarding uses a different local port. An exact numeric port rule with the same flag correctly shows the warning.

The range still applies its `label`, so the failure is not that the rule fails to match. `requireLocalPort` is dropped while resolving the attributes.

## Environment and verification scope

- VS Code: **1.119.0-insider**, commit `717aa443fdb80afacf21f6050ba976f890b8ea55`, arm64.
- OS: **macOS 26.2**, build `25C56`.
- Installed user extensions disabled; a local extension development host supplied the reproduction fixture.
- VS Code product code was unmodified.
- Source analysis used upstream `main` at `4f012f7e4eecac06ab2ecc60d5c17ca686fb9c2a`.

**Reproduced in the running VS Code desktop app:** range rule with `true`, exact-port rule with `true`, and exact-port rule with `false`.

**Checked only in an isolated source-class harness:** host-and-port and process-command regex rules also lose `requireLocalPort: true`. Their missing-dialog behavior was **not** reproduced in the desktop app.

The desktop reproduction uses a controlled local tunnel provider, not a Remote SSH or Dev Containers connection. The fixture creates real loopback TCP forwarding through `workspace.openTunnel`, exercising VS Code's forwarding model, configuration resolution, Ports view, and native dialog service. It does not replace those VS Code components.

## Reproduction steps

[Download the self-contained source fixture](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33943581/require-local-port-repro.zip). It contains the extension source, initial workspace settings, and README; no dependency installation is needed.

1. Extract the archive. Ensure loopback ports **45321** and **45322** are free. From the extracted directory, launch:

   ```sh
   code-insiders --new-window --profile "Require Local Port Repro" --disable-extensions \
     --extensionDevelopmentPath="$PWD/extension" \
     --enable-proposed-api local-repro.require-local-port-repro \
     --skip-welcome --skip-release-notes "$PWD/workspace"
   ```

   On macOS, if the CLI is not on PATH, use the installed application's `Contents/Resources/app/bin/code`.

2. Wait **more than ten seconds** after startup. VS Code's mismatch-dialog cooldown otherwise suppresses even the positive control.

3. Run **Repro: Range Rule** from the Command Palette. It configures:

   ```json
   "remote.portsAttributes": {
     "45300-45400": {
       "label": "Repro range",
       "requireLocalPort": true
     }
   },
   "remote.otherPortsAttributes": {}
   ```

   The fixture opens remote port 45321, requesting local port 45322. A fixture server already occupies 45322. The provider attempts it, receives `EADDRINUSE`, chooses another local port, and forwards to the HTTP application.

4. Open the Ports view. The row has label **Repro range**, confirming the range matched. The local port differs from 45322, but **no mismatch warning appears**.

5. Run **Repro: Exact Port Rule**. It closes the previous tunnel and replaces the range with the exact key `"45321"`, keeping `requireLocalPort: true`. The same conflict now produces the expected mismatch warning.

6. Dismiss the warning, wait more than ten seconds, then run **Repro: Exact Port False Control**. It uses exact key `"45321"` with `requireLocalPort: false`; forwarding succeeds without a warning, as expected.

7. Close the development host to stop the fixture servers and tunnels.

The fixture also includes optional host-and-port and fallback commands; those were **not completed in the recorded desktop run**.

## Expected and actual results

A matched range with `requireLocalPort: true` should show the same warning as a matched exact-port rule when the requested local port cannot be used. This setting requests a warning; it does not prohibit forwarding to another port.

| Case | Actual local port in recorded
