Testing #345460

In a Copilot (Agent Host) session, **Allow Edits in \<folder\> in this Session** and **Allow Edits to \<file\> in this Session** have no effect when the file's path goes through a symlink. The **Allow Reading…** options behave the same. On macOS this includes everything under `/tmp` and `/var/folders`.

### Steps

1. Copilot harness, **Manual permissions**.
2. `mkdir -p /tmp/outside-repo && git -C /tmp/outside-repo init`, then add `target.txt` and `same-folder.txt`.
3. Ask the agent to edit `/tmp/outside-repo/target.txt` and pick **Allow Edits in outside-repo in this Session**.
4. Ask it to edit `/tmp/outside-repo/same-folder.txt`.

**Expected:** no prompt.
**Actual:** **Write file?** prompts again. The same steps in a folder under `~` work.

The rule is built from the literal path (`Edit(//tmp/outside-repo/**)`, [sessionPermissions.ts#L935-L958](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionPermissions.ts#L935-L958)). Approval checks both the literal path and its real path (`/private/tmp/…`, [L822-L828](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionPermissions.ts#L822-L828)) and requires every candidate to match ([L293](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionPermissions.ts#L293)). One option is to also add a rule for the folder's real path. A symlink inside the approved folder that points outside it should keep prompting, as it does today.

VS Code Insiders 1.145.0-insider (`67710841ad`), macOS 26.7.1 arm64.

state.body:
## Problem

Sandbox-related minimum client version requirements should not apply when sandbox is not enabled in managed settings. The presence of a sandbox configuration object alone should not require a newer client.

cc @rwoll 

Example `copilot/managed-settings.json`:

```json
{
  "sandbox": {
    "overridable": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Requested behavior

Enforce the sandbox-related minimum client version only when the effective managed sandbox policy explicitly sets `enabled` to boolean `true`.

- When `enabled: false` is set, do not enforce the sandbox minimum version.
- When explicit effective `enabled: true` is absent—including an omitted `enabled` field, empty sandbox object, or absent sandbox key—do not enforce the sandbox minimum version.
- When sandbox is explicitly enabled, preserve existing minimum-version enforcement.
- Preserve minimum-version requirements independently imposed by other policies.

Use the effective enabled state after applicable policy composition and overrides, rather than the presence of the sandbox object or other sandbox subkeys.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disabled sandbox does not trigger a sandbox-derived minimum-version rejection.
- [ ] Missing `enabled`, an empty sandbox object, and an absent sandbox key do not trigger a sandbox-derived minimum-version rejection.
- [ ] Explicitly enabled sandbox continues to enforce its minimum version.
- [ ] Policy composition and overrides use the final effective sandbox enabled state.
- [ ] Unrelated applicable minimum-version requirements remain enforced.
- [ ] Policy refresh from enabled to disabled removes any stale sandbox-only version requirement.

## Related work

- ACP tracking issue: https://github.com/github/agent-control-plane/issues/1865
- Runtime counterpart: https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/issues/26557
- GitHub App implementation issue: https://github.com/github/github-app/issues/16570
- [Slack discussion](https://github-grid.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0AUT2UKPB3/p1791985099678439?thread_ts=1791923316.205789&cid=C0AUT2UKPB3)

✏️ with :heart: :zap: by Copilot for @gpadak
state.title: Do not enforce minimum client version when sandbox is not enabled

state.body:
When the connection to a remote agent host is down and VS Code has stopped reconnecting, sending the first message in a new chat for that host still creates a chat session on the client only. The host never creates it. After a reload, that chat's editor can't be restored and shows *"The editor could not be opened due to an unexpected error"*. **Try Again** keeps failing, and the prompt is lost.

## What happened (reconstructed from the renderer log)

1. The WebSocket connection to the remote agent host closed. `RemoteAgentHostProtocol` retried in rounds (`Automatic reconnect to <host> gave up after 10 attempts.`, followed by `Connection closed` and another round). After about 20 minutes, the rounds stopped. The window then stayed disconnected from that host for about 12 hours, with no further reconnect attempts in the log.
2. In that state, I opened a new chat for that host and sent a message:
   ```
   [info]  ChatService#materializeUntitledSession: Materialized untitled session <host>-copilotcli:/untitled-<uuid> into real session <host>-copilotcli:/<id>
   [info]  [AgentHost] _invokeAgent called for resource: <host>-copilotcli:/<id>
   [error] Error while handling chat request: Automatic reconnect gave up after 10 attempts.: Error: Automatic reconnect gave up after 10 attempts.
   ```
   The request failed immediately, but the editor kept the materialized resource `/<id>`. The same failure had already happened once with an earlier new chat.
3. Later, the window reconnected to the host and was reloaded. Restoring that chat editor fails, and so does every **Try Again**:
   ```
   [error] ChatService#loadRemoteSession: failed to restore <host>-copilotcli:/<id> Session identity was not advertised by its agent host: <host>-copilotcli:/<id>
   [error] Error: Failed to get model for chat editor. resource: <host>-copilotcli:/<id>
   ```
   The error comes from `_discoverSessionIdentity` in [agentHostSessionHandler.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c5f99e81a5d0ce82a55615da27c322bbe48ad00e/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts). It refreshes identities through `connection.listSessions()`, and the ID isn't listed. I confirmed with an AHP `listSessions` call directly against the host: neither a session nor a chat with that ID exists. The host never received the session.

## Problems

1. **No recovery after reconnect gives up.** Once automatic reconnect stops, the host connection stays dead indefinitely, but the UI still lets you start chats and send messages to that host. The failure only appears after sending.
2. **The untitled session is materialized before the host confirms it.** If creating the session or sending the first message fails, the editor keeps a resource that will never exist on the host. That leaves an editor that can't be restored, and the user's prompt is lost.

## Expected

- Keep reconnecting periodically (or on window focus or network change), or clearly show that the host is disconnected and block sending until it is reachable again.
- If the first request fails before the host creates the session, keep or revert the chat as untitled and keep the prompt, so the user can resend it once the host is back.
- When a restored chat refers to a session the host doesn't know, show a specific message instead of the generic "editor could not be opened" error.
state.title: Agent host: chat created while the remote host connection is down cannot be restored (Session identity was not advertised)

state.body:
## Describe the bug

In the Agents Window's "modern" editor header (desktop tabs layout), the **Branch Changes dropdown** (e.g. `main · 3 Files +42 -7 ⌄`) appears to have an uneven top/bottom margin inside its pill: the content sits visually closer to one edge than the other, instead of being perfectly vertically centered like the surrounding tabs.

Related complaints from the same screenshot/thread (filed here for traceability, not necessarily the same root cause):
- The left-most tab can get clipped/cut off.
- Tab titles can be hidden/truncated by the close ("x") button before the title has a chance to ellipsize.
- It's unclear why the changes-count/diff-stat badge (`+42 -7`) is fused into the same clickable pill as the branch/changeset picker, rather than being a separate, non-interactive element.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Agents Window with the desktop tabs/editor-header layout enabled.
2. Open a session with pending changes so the "Branch Changes" dropdown shows a file-count + added/removed stats summary (i.e. `changes-picker-action-with-summary`).
3. Compare the vertical space above vs. below the pill's content versus its container.

## Code pointers

- `ChangesPickerActionItem` (the dropdown's action view item) — `src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/browser/changesView.ts`
- Desktop header host: `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorHeaderControl.ts` (`.editor-group-header`, `.editor-group-header-actions`, `.editor-group-header-primary-actions`, `DEFAULT_HEIGHT`/`COMPACT_HEIGHT`)
- Desktop header CSS: `src/vs/sessions/contrib/editor/browser/media/editorHeader.css`
- Pill styling: `src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/browser/media/sessionChangesEditor.css` (`.changes-picker-action-rich`, `.changes-picker-action-with-summary .action-label`)
- Animated stats badge: `src/vs/workbench/browser/animatedCounterWidget.ts` / `changesStatsWidget.ts`

While the explicit padding values declared along this chain are symmetric (e.g. `.editor-group-header { padding: var(--vscode-spacing-size20) var(--vscode-spacing-size40) var(--vscode-spacing-size20) var(--vscode-spacing-size80); }` and `.changes-picker-action-with-summary .action-label { padding: var(--vscode-spacing-size20) var(--vscode-spacing-size60); }`), the button is vertically centered through ~5 nested levels (`.monaco-toolbar` → `.monaco-action-bar` → `.actions-container` → `.monaco-dropdown` → `.dropdown-label`) that rely on `height: 100%`, but none of their ancestors up to `.editor-group-header` actually has a definite (non-`auto`) height — only a `min-height`. Per spec, a percentage height needs a definite containing-block height to resolve; here it does not, so each level's height instead hugs content and gets independently (re-)centered via `align-items: center`/CSS grid, which is a common source of compounding 1px sub-pixel rounding drift. There is also an inherited/uncontrolled `line-height` on the picker's text spans, which combined with flexbox centering is a classic cause of 1px visual top/bottom offset ("half-leading" rounding).

Separately (not necessarily the cause of this specific bug, but a related cascade issue found while investigating), `.session-changes-editor-header-left .action-label > .codicon` sets an explicit `width: 12px; height: 12px;` box for the chevron/icon, but the later, equal-specificity rule `.changes-picker-action-rich .action-label > .codicon` resets it back to `width: auto; height: auto;`, so the fixed icon box is silently lost for this specific picker.

## Suggested fix

See follow-up comment / Slack thread — proposal is to (1) give the header row an explicit, definite height (matching `EditorHeaderControl.DEFAULT_HEIGHT`/`COMPACT_HEIGHT`) instead of only `min-height`, so the nested `height: 100%` chain resolves deterministically instead of drifting; (2) set an explicit, unitless `line-height` on `.changes-picker-action-rich .action-label` and descendants to remove half-leading rounding ambiguity; (3) restore the fixed icon box i

## Issue Subcategory
Visible and programmatic descriptions do not align

## User Experience
Screen reader users may receive different or less descriptive information than is available visually, causing them to miss instructions or context needed to understand or use the element.

Open VS code > Extensions > Observe the issue

When navigating to the expand/collapse controls for Installed, Recommended, Enabled, and Disabled extension sections using a screen reader, the screen reader announces the section/control name and expanded or collapsed state, but does not announce the corresponding number of extensions displayed visually next to the section name.

The screen reader should announce the section name, extension count, and expanded/collapsed state so that the information available visually is also available to screen-reader users.

Ensure the visible and programmatic descriptions convey equivalent information. If they intentionally differ, programmatically associate the element with any additional visible content. Use `aria-describedby` for concise text or `aria-details` for extended or structured content.

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not captured.
- VS Code Version: Insiders, commit `087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41`, built 2026-10-20.
- OS Version: macOS, exact version not captured.
- Feature: Agents window > Customizations > Migration.
- Selected model: Not applicable.
- Logs: Agent Host debug export analyzed locally. The bundle is not attached because it contains sensitive session data.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open Customizations > Migration with user prompt files eligible for migration.
2. Open a prompt's context menu, choose Delete, and confirm.
3. Check the migration list. The deleted prompt can remain listed and still offer Delete.

Expected: Deleting a prompt removes its row and updates the migration counts.

Actual: The file is removed from disk, but the list can retain the row, making deletion appear unsuccessful. Repeating Delete can show another confirmation for the same prompt.

### Observed evidence

On October 20, local log timestamps show:

- 08:42:01: Delete confirmation for one prompt, followed by migration recomputation and a user-data filesystem change.
- 08:42:10: Delete confirmation for another prompt, followed by another filesystem change and multiple migration recomputations.
- 08:42:15 and 08:42:22: Delete confirmations appear again for the second prompt.

Both prompt files were absent on disk when checked after the capture. No matching filesystem-delete error appears in the renderer logs.

### RCA

A cancellation race was reproduced using the current source methods with controlled discovery timing. The relevant source matches the reported Insiders commit.

- [deleteCustomizationFile](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L2338) deletes the file and refreshes Migration. An immediate refresh can still read pre-delete discovery results before watcher invalidation.
- [refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L1357) cancels the previous refresh when another invalidation arrives.
- [listPromptFiles](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsServiceImpl.ts#L377) shares an in-flight promise tied to its first caller's cancellation token. The replacement refresh can inherit that cancelled scan even though its own token remains live.
- [computeCustomizationMigrationInfo](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L1475) ignores the resulting cancellation, leaving the previous rows without an error state or retry.

The controlled reproduction verified that both computations exit without applying updated candidates, while the replacement request's token is not cancelled. The logs are consistent with this race but do not record discovery cancellation directly, so attribution of this specific occurrence remains likely rather than conclusive. No live UI reproduction or fix validation was performed.

- VS Code Version: 1.143.0-insider (e9f10b90b50805aa31d65f3d35cf53c264d7235f)
- OS Version: macOS 27.0.1

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Have an idle local Copilot SDK session in the Agents window.
2. Have an AHP client subscribe to the cold session's channel to inspect its state/history, without sending a message or continuing a turn.
3. Observe its relative update label and, when sorting by update time, its position in the session list.

**Actual:** Old, untouched sessions become recently updated, e.g. "1 min ago". Background restore/resume, runtime warnings, and shutdown can advance the timestamp despite no conversation activity.

**Expected:** The relative update label should reflect meaningful conversation activity, not passive inspection or provider lifecycle bookkeeping.

### Local evidence

On October 16, a session whose last user message and assistant turn were on August 8 received background AHP subscriptions at 10:10 and 10:11 PDT. Agent Host restored it, the SDK appended `session.resume` and remote-availability warnings, and later idle eviction appended `session.shutdown`. No new user message or assistant turn was recorded. There were 23 distinct SDK sessions resumed during 10:11, matching the observation that several untouched sessions became recent together.

### Suspected mechanism

- `AgentService.subscribe()` restores cold sessions; Copilot history loading resolves/resumes an SDK session.
- SDK session listing derives `modifiedTime` from the `events.jsonl` filesystem modification time, which also advances for lifecycle/warning records.
- VS Code forwards that value into the session adapter's `updatedAt` and `lastTurnEnd`.

This makes passive reads appear as user activity. The originating client feature for the observed batch has not yet been identified; attribution to a particular third-party client is not established.

Related but distinct: #306025 concerns creation-time versus update-time display, not lifecycle writes manufacturing fresh update times.

Switching between chats in the Agents window is slow when the chats live on remote agent hosts (here: hosts reached through a Hub relay). Opening a chat for the first time in a window takes a median of 2.7s and up to ~26s; reopening an already-loaded chat takes ~0.4s. During a switch the renderer is also blocked for several hundred milliseconds to a few seconds at a time, so the whole window feels sluggish.

The investigation below was done on a live Agents window (VS Code Insiders, commit [`131aec7f`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/131aec7f1ee4f0d0e8ed204704850cc8e31dd9d0)) with ~400 sessions across four remote agent hosts, using CPU profiles, the existing chat-open performance marks, a temporary WebSocket send/receive probe in the renderer, and a non-pausing conditional breakpoint. Source links point to that commit.

## Measurements

From `[ChatOpen] agentsWindow … total=…ms modelWasLoaded=…` lines in one day of renderer logs:

| Case | n | p50 | p90 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chat model not loaded yet | 45 | 2,651 ms | 23,313 ms | 26,523 ms |
| Chat model already loaded | 15 | 392 ms | 724 ms | 724 ms |

Per-phase marks (`…open/<milestone>`, recorded by `ChatOpenDiagnosticsService`) for opens I triggered:

| Host | contentRequested → contentReceived | contentReceived → loaded |
|---|---|---|
| Devbox | 4,686 ms | ~500 ms |
| Tablet | 6,217 ms | ~135 ms |
| PC2 | 7,420 ms | 755 ms |
| Devbox | 7,480 ms | 1,818 ms |
| Devbox | **18,117 ms** | 2,708 ms (replay alone 1.7 s) |

The dominant cost is `contentRequested → contentReceived`, i.e. [`chatSessionService.getOrCreateChatSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/131aec7f1ee4f0d0e8ed204704850cc8e31dd9d0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts#L951-L972) waiting for the host's subscribe snapshot. Rendering adds 0.3–2.7 s on top.

## Contributing causes

### 1. Customization scope is rebuilt on most switches and floods the host connection

[`_syncActiveClient`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/131aec7f1ee4f0d0e8ed204704850cc8e31dd9d0/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L5037-L5065) replaces `_activeSessionScope` whenever the newly active session has different working directories. That disposes the previous refcounted `AgentCustomizationScope` and acquires a new one. Since every worktree session has its own working directory, almost every switch creates a new scope, whose constructor runs a full [`resolveCustomizationRefs` + `resolveLocalCustomAgents`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/131aec7f1ee4f0d0e8ed204704850cc8e31dd9d0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostActiveClientService.ts#L136-L180) pass.

Observed effects:

- A conditional breakpoint on [`PromptFilesLocator.toAbsoluteLocations`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/131aec7f1ee4f0d0e8ed204704850cc8e31dd9d0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/utils/promptFilesLocator.ts#L599) counted ~4,000 hits across two chat opens, all from `agentHostActiveClientService` → `agentHostLocalCustomizations` → `promptsService.listPromptFilesForStorage`. Zero hits while idle.
- The renderer log contains 25,774 `Glob patterns (* and **) detected in instruction file location` lines in one day, arriving in bursts of ~242 per switch.
- During one open against PC2, the renderer sent **1,378–1,891 `resourceList` requests within ~5 s** over the same WebSocket as the chat subscribe. Subscribe responses in that window had round-trip times of up to 2.6–2.9 s.
- After resolution, a ~52 KB `session/activeClientSet` action is sent again on every switch (via `_dispatchActiveClientWhenResolved`).
- Many `Resource not found` warnings for non-existent `.mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, `.vscode/tasks.json`, `.github/copilot/settings…` on remote roots are part of the same rediscovery.

Suggestion: keep recently used scopes alive (an LRU or a grace pe

state.body:
**Use case**
In organizations on Copilot Business/Enterprise, admins decide which models are available, and users only get that subset. Dictation cleanup, however, can only use one hard-coded "good" model (`gpt-5.6-luna`). If that model is not offered to an organization, every user there silently falls back to `copilot-utility-small`. There is no way to choose another model that the organization *does* allow and that the same user already uses in chat every day.

**What happened to us**
Between 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-28, dictation cleanup stopped using Luna, although `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` is still `gpt-5.6-luna`. `gpt-5.6-luna` is no longer offered to my account/organization (Copilot Business). Our model list now contains `gpt-6-luna` instead. I cannot tell whether the model was retired globally or is just not enabled for our organization. Either way, the result for the user is the same.

```
[chat-stt] selecting language model cleanup model (vendor=copilot, id=gpt-5.6-luna)
[chat-stt] gpt-5.6-luna cleanup model unavailable; falling back to copilot-utility-small
[chat-stt] applied language model cleanup (model=copilot-utility-small, ...)
```

**Why settings cannot fix it:** `gpt-5.6-luna` is hard-coded in three places:
- the setting enum (`auto | copilot-utility-small | gpt-5.6-luna`)
- `LLM_CLEANUP_LUNA_MODEL_ID` in `chatSpeechToTextService.ts`
- the Copilot alias `copilot-dictation-cleanup-luna`, which resolves the CAPI family `gpt-5.6-luna`

Any other value is silently replaced with `copilot-utility-small`.

**Request:** allow `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` to take the ID of any chat model that is user-selectable for the current user, i.e. what their organization has enabled, for example `gpt-6-luna`. From #332969 I understand that the dedicated cleanup aliases are intentionally core-only. This request leaves them as they are. It only asks to accept models the user is already allowed to use in chat. This would also respect organization model policies by design, and model retirements would no longer need a code change.

**Nice to have:** when the configured model is unavailable, show a visible hint, not only an info line in the log.

**Environment:** VS Code 1.139.1 (04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1), built-in Copilot extension 0.67.0, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Copilot Business, `dictation.model` = Nemotron (local), `agents.voice.language` = `de`.
state.title: Dictation cleanup: allow any chat model available to the user/organization instead of a hard-coded model ID

state.body:
## Summary

Extensions can move an editor into a new window with
`workbench.action.moveEditorToNewWindow`, but cannot choose the window's size,
cannot make it compact or always-on-top at creation, and cannot open an editor
directly into a new window. The workbench supports all of this internally:
`_workbench.openWith(resource, editorId, [AUX_WINDOW_GROUP, { auxiliary: { bounds, compact, alwaysOnTop } }])`
does exactly that today. The public `vscode.openWith` cannot reach it.

## Use case

[porthole](https://github.com/jlumbroso/porthole), an extension that pops an HTML page into a small, compact, pinned
window beside your code. It calls the internal command above because nothing
public does the job, falling back to public commands when the internal call
fails. The fallback opens at the default 1024×768, shows the page in the main
window first, and runs compact and pin as separate steps that depend on focus
having moved.

## What exists today (source at tag 1.141.0, paths under `src/vs/`)

- `_workbench.openWith` passes options through and sends the column to
  `columnToEditorGroup`
  (`workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorCommands.ts` L544), which lets the
  special group `-3`, `AUX_WINDOW_GROUP`, through
  (`workbench/services/editor/common/editorGroupColumn.ts` L19;
  `workbench/services/editor/common/editorService.ts` L34).
- For that group, a floating window is created from `options.auxiliary`
  (`workbench/services/editor/common/editorGroupFinder.ts` L139), whose fields
  are `bounds`, `compact` and `alwaysOnTop`
  (`platform/editor/common/editor.ts` L320).
- The public `vscode.openWith` maps every column except positive ones and
  `Beside` to the active group
  (`workbench/api/common/extHostTypeConverters.ts` L336;
  `workbench/api/common/extHostApiCommands.ts` L443), so `-3` never arrives.
- Floating windows already persist their bounds, compact state and pin across
  restarts (`workbench/services/auxiliaryWindow/browser/auxiliaryWindowService.ts` L239).

## Proposal

A `ViewColumn`-like target for a new window in `TextDocumentShowOptions` and
`vscode.openWith`, for example:

```ts
await vscode.commands.executeCommand('vscode.openWith', uri, viewType, {
  viewColumn: vscode.ViewColumn.NewWindow,
  window: { width: 420, height: 640, compact: true, alwaysOnTop: true },
});
```

Optionally, a way to resize an existing floating window
(`AuxiliaryWindow.setBounds` exists in the renderer, but no command exposes
it), which would remove the need to re-open a page to resize it.

## Evidence it works

On VS Code 1.141.0, macOS, the internal call opened the window at the
requested size, compact and pinned, in 20 runs out of 20 across a spike and a
hands-on test (new window reported within 84–236 ms).

---
*From porthole's design brief (Claude Opus 5.5, 2026-10-12) and its spike;
the call chain re-checked in source by Surveyor 5.1 (Claude Fable 5.1);
drafted by Glazier 5.5 (Claude Opus 5.5).*
state.title: API: let extensions open an editor in a new floating window, with size, compact and always-on-top

state.body:
GitHub sessions only expire today when they're brokered through Microsoft Entra (#335183). Those sessions report `expiresAfter` and renew themselves before they run out. Ordinary GitHub OAuth sessions are stored in the keychain with no known expiry, and nothing ever renews them.

The GitHub Authentication extension should support expiring GitHub tokens for those sessions too, by requesting the `offline_access` scope. With `offline_access`, sign-in returns an access token that expires plus a refresh token. The extension would:

- store the refresh token next to the session
- report the access token's remaining lifetime through `expiresAfter`
- renew the access token before it expires, the same way Entra-brokered sessions renew today

The renewal path in `extensions/github-authentication/src/github.ts` (`stillGood`) only handles transient Entra-brokered sessions. It will need to give persisted sessions their own expiry and branch on how a given session renews.

Related: #335183, #335184
state.title: Support expiring GitHub tokens with the offline_access scope

## Problem

Tools running extension builds need a reliable indication of when compilation starts and when its outputs are ready. Inferring this from human-readable logs is fragile, especially for overlapping builds and asynchronous postprocessing.

## Proposed behavior

Add opt-in versioned JSON event records for extension TypeScript watch compilations and shared esbuild runners. `VSCODE_BUILD_EVENTS=1` enables records with `type: "vscode.build"`, `version: 1`, and either `event: "start"` or `event: "finish"` with a boolean `success`.

Each event occupies one stdout line alongside existing human-readable logs. Consumers can ignore additional metadata fields, allowing the format to evolve. Overlapping builds must retain any failure until the aggregate cycle finishes, and asynchronous pre/postprocessing must complete before success is reported. Existing output stays unchanged when events are disabled.

Implementation: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/343297

Parent story: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/343273
state.title: Expose opt-in machine-readable extension build lifecycle events

The Agents Window Worktree Cleanup editor should avoid repeating disk-usage measurement when valid results already exist.

Expected behavior:

- The first manual open measures session worktrees when no valid measurement is available.
- Concurrent opens and reopening while measurement is in progress join the same provider work and progress operation.
- Completed results are reused for one hour while the session/worktree set is unchanged.
- Changing the inactivity period recomputes eligibility without remeasuring sizes.
- After confirmed cleanup, archived sessions disappear while unchanged remaining measurements are reused.
- Automatic cleanup suggestion scans share the same cache and in-flight measurement with manual editor loads.
- Suggestion invalidation reevaluates thresholds without discarding otherwise valid disk measurements.
- A full window/application reload starts with a new in-memory cache and measures again when results are first needed.

This prevents duplicate provider calls and avoids showing repeated measurement progress for unchanged worktrees.

# Improve editor tab scrollbar placement

## Problem

When multiple editor tabs are open, the horizontal scrollbar appears along the top edge of the tab bar, visually overlapping the area occupied by the tab headers.

This makes the tab bar look less clean and reduces the visual separation between the scrollbar and the tabs themselves.

## Current behavior

When the number of open tabs exceeds the available width, the scrollbar is displayed directly above the tab headers, as shown in the attached VS Code screenshot.

Although the scrollbar serves its purpose, its placement introduces an additional visual element into an already dense navigation area.

## Why this matters

- **Visual hierarchy:** The scrollbar competes with the tab headers for visual attention.
- **Visual consistency:** The line disrupts the clean appearance of the tab bar, particularly when tabs have distinct backgrounds, borders, or rounded corners.
- **Interaction clarity:** Placing the scrollbar so close to the tab headers may make the two controls feel visually connected, potentially causing confusion when interacting with them.
- **Overall polish:** The tab bar feels less cohesive when many files are open, which is a common workflow for developers.

## Proposed improvement

Consider placing the scrollbar in a dedicated area that does not visually overlap or interfere with the tab headers.

Alternatively, explore a tab-scrolling design that keeps the scrollbar visually separate from the tab bar.

The goal is not to remove tab scrolling, but to preserve the visual integrity of the tabs while maintaining convenient navigation between open editors.

## Reference

The attached JetBrains IDE screenshot illustrates an alternative approach to tab navigation, where the tab headers retain a clearer visual separation from the scrolling mechanism.

This is intended as a UX reference rather than a request to replicate the exact implementation.

## Expected result

- Tab headers retain their visual integrity and clear boundaries.
- The scrollbar does not visually interfere with tab labels or tab shapes.
- Scrolling between open tabs remains intuitive and accessible.
- The overall tab bar feels cleaner and more visually consistent.

## Screenshots

[image]

state.body:
## Problem

Model selection is configured through a growing set of independent, flat settings. Each has its own ID format, its own meaning for "empty", and its own picker UX. Three recent developments make this worse:

1. **The runtime prompt advertises `/subagents`, which VS Code doesn't expose.** In the Copilot runtime's `task` tool schema, the `model`, `reasoning_effort`, and `context_tier` descriptions all say: *"The runtime resolves `/subagents` preferences when these fields are omitted; do not copy them merely because they appear in `<subagent_model_preferences>`."* `/subagents` is a CLI command, and VS Code intentionally hides it (it is in `HIDDEN_RUNTIME_COMMANDS` in `copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.ts`). So the model is told about a preference surface that VS Code users can't reach, while VS Code has its own unrelated per-subagent settings (below). The same schema also injects a flat `model` enum containing every available model (22 in the e2e snapshots, and 50+ in a real session with BYOK and OpenRouter models), plus prose lists of which models support each reasoning effort and long context.
2. **Many settings use very long flat lists.** Several settings build a dynamic enum of every user-selectable chat model (`DefaultModelContribution`). With BYOK, OpenRouter, and on-device models, each of these becomes a long, flat, unsearchable dropdown (#317420). The Settings editor repeats it once per setting, and each copy has to be repopulated whenever models change. Other settings are free-form strings with no discovery or validation (#319191).
3. **Non-chat models are arriving.** Image generation is a boolean (`chat.copilot.imageGeneration.enabled`) with the model hard-coded to GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, so users can't choose an image model. Speech, voice, embeddings, completions, NES, and on-device models each have separate settings too. `ILanguageModelsService` is centered on chat models, and nothing shared describes "the model for capability X".

We need one unified way to configure all of these.

## Inventory of current cases

### Main conversation

| Setting | Owner | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat.defaultModel` | workbench | free string (`auto`, family alias such as `opus`, or full id) | Policy-backed (`ChatDefaultModel`, managed `model` / `permissions.model`) |
| `inlineChat.defaultModel` | workbench | dynamic enum of all tool-calling models | `Name (vendor)` format |
| Per-session model picker | workbench | state, not a setting | |

### Agents and subagents

| Setting / surface | Owner | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat.planAgent.defaultModel` | workbench | dynamic enum | `Name (vendor)` format |
| `chat.exploreAgent.defaultModel` | workbench | dynamic enum | `Name (vendor)` format |
| `github.copilot.chat.exploreAgent.model` | Copilot extension | free string | Duplicates the workbench setting above |
| `github.copilot.chat.askAgent.model` | Copilot extension | free string | |
| `github.copilot.chat.implementAgent.model` | Copilot extension | free string | |
| `github.copilot.chat.searchSubagent.model` | Copilot extension | free string | Extension harness |
| `chat.copilot.searchSubagent.model` | agent host | free string (CAPI model id) | Agent host harness; restarts the SDK client |
| `github.copilot.chat.executionSubagent.model` | Copilot extension | free string, default `gpt-5.6-luna` | Description and defaults are inconsistent (#341517) |
| `chat.agentHost.copilot.executionSubagent.model` | agent host | free string (runtime model id), default `gpt-5.6-luna` | Empty means "inherit parent"; restarts the runtime |
| `.agent.md` `model:` frontmatter | prompt files | `Name (vendor)` | Doesn't map to `task` tool ids (#340844) |
| `task` tool `model` / `reasoning_effort` / `context_tier` | Copilot runtime | chosen by the model; flat enum | Points to `/subagents` and `<subagent_model_preferences>` |
| CLI `/subagents` preferences | Copilot runtime | CLI config | Not reachable from VS Code |

state.body:
### Problem Statement & Use Case
We are migrating complex developer tooling from Eclipse RCP to VS Code extensions. We have encountered a major layout and workflow blocker regarding advanced user input and data validation.

In Eclipse RCP, the `Dialog` architecture allows launching modal frames to handle heavy data orchestration (e.g., database schema mapping, multi-row environment setups, and complex multi-field forms) without breaking the user's active editor split layouts.

Currently, VS Code offers no viable alternative for dense, non-linear data collection:
* `showInformationMessage(..., { modal: true })`: Highly restrictive. It only displays static strings and buttons; it cannot collect complex user input.
* `showQuickPick` / Multi-step InputBox: Built for linear selection. It completely fails when workflows require structural matrices, multi-column tables, cross-field validation, or complex form controls.
* `WebviewPanel` (Editor Tabs): Opening a full-sized tab for a transient 10-second task disorients the user's layout, breaks active editor splits, and introduces a messy tab lifecycle management overhead.

### Proposed Solution
We propose an API extension such as `vscode.window.createExtensionDialog`—that allows extensions to spawn a temporary modal overlay surface over the workbench:

* **True Modality:** Blocks interaction with the underlying workbench layout until explicitly submitted or cancelled to guarantee data sequence integrity.
* **Floating & Centered:** Container floats centered over the active VS Code window (similar to native OS message boxes).
* **Webview Driven:** Powered by standard sandboxed Webview HTML/JS, allowing developers to build custom data grids, checkboxes, validation logic, and input fields safely.
* **Transient Lifecycle:** Exists entirely outside the editor tab bar, managed explicitly by the extension backend or user actions (`Esc` / Close buttons).
state.title: API Proposal: Support Custom Native Floating Modal Dialogs for Complex Data Workflows

Depends on: https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/issues/2761

In Agent Host Copilot chats, a detached background shell (`detach: true`) shows no output in VS Code. Neither its tool card nor its **Background Shells** details has a live terminal, because the Copilot SDK sends `tool.shell_output` only for attached shells. Detached shells are the ones that keep running after the response, like dev servers and watchers, so that's exactly when their output (ports, compile errors, crashes) matters.

Once the Copilot SDK ships the experimental `session.rpc.tasks.readOutput`, stream a detached shell's output like an attached shell's:

- For each running detached shell, call `readOutput({ id, cursor, waitMs: 30_000 })` in a loop, append each result's `text` to the shell's terminal, and pass the returned `cursor` to the next call.
- When a result includes `exit`, show the shell's final status and exit code, and stop reading.
- Stop reading when the shell is stopped or the session is disposed.
- When the Agent Host resumes a session after a restart, call `session.rpc.tasks.refresh()` first so the restored shells are listed, then read each one again. Reading without a cursor replays its output from the start.

A local prototype streamed a detached shell's output live into its **Background Shells** details. These still need work:

- [x] Keep the inline terminal in the shell's tool card updating after the response completes. In the prototype, it stopped updating at the end of the response and caught up only when the shell exited, while the **Background Shells** details kept streaming.

### Future TODOs

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/342448
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/342449

- VS Code Version: 1.106.x (Insiders stable line, October 2026)
- OS: macOS

**Repro (any extension that registers models via the `chatProvider` proposed API):**

1. An extension registers a language model provider (`registerLanguageModelProvider`, proposed `chatProvider`).
2. The user picks one of its models in the chat panel and sends a chat request.
3. The provider's response stream yields `LanguageModelTextPart`s (and a `LanguageModelDataPart` with mimeType `"usage"` carrying `{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens}`).
4. The chat panel's context-usage widget (the bar showing "X% of context used" / tokens used of the model's window) stays hidden/empty — no per-response token usage is ever displayed.

**Expected:** there should be a supported way for a language-model provider to report the actual token usage (prompt/completion) it observed, so the chat context-usage widget can display it — the same way chat participants can today.

## What the current build actually does (evidence from the shipped bundle)

1. **The widget reads `IChatResponseModel.usage` only.** `ChatContextUsageWidget#updateFromResponse` computes `promptTokens + completionTokens` over the model's `totalContextWindow`, and hides when `usage` is unset.

2. **`IChatResponseModel.setUsage` has exactly three feeders:**
   - `acceptResponseProgress` when the progress chunk is `kind === "usage"`;
   - the agent-host progress-chunk handler, same `kind === "usage"` shape;
   - the session-restore path (persisted `promptTokens`/`completionTokens` fields).

3. **The only extension-host producer of a `kind:"usage"` progress chunk is `ChatResponseStream.usage(...)`** — i.e. a *chat participant* response stream, gated on the `chatParticipantAdditions` proposed API. A *language-model provider* has no equivalent: there is no `usage`-shaped progress, no field on `LanguageModelChatResponse`, and nothing in the `chatProvider` proposal that carries usage. (Grep of the shipped `vscode.proposed.chatProvider.d.ts` and the stable `@types/vscode` d.ts: zero usage-surface hits.)

4. **The only consumer that decodes a `LanguageModelDataPart` with mimeType `"usage"` is the agent-host BYOK path** (`AgentHostByokLmHandler`, service `agentHostByokLmHandler`, channel `agentHostClientByokLm`). It parses exactly `{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens}` out of the data part, returns it over the agent-host protocol to the node side, where the BYOK loopback proxy folds it into the Responses-API `response.completed` usage — which then reaches `setUsage` and the widget. So for agent-host sessions with BYOK models, an in-band usage data part works end-to-end.

5. **On the plain panel path, that data part is silently dropped.** The default chat agent consumes the provider stream, but its handling of `LanguageModelDataPart`s only covers `stateful_marker`, `cache_control`, images, and PDFs (history filtering / request re-serialization). mimeType `"usage"` is never decoded there — and the default agent's own token accounting comes from parsing usage out of *its own* raw API responses, which a third-party provider's stream never contains.

## Net effect

- Third-party `chatProvider` extensions (this is how e.g. internal gateway-backed model providers register) can never feed the context-usage widget on the normal panel path — the widget silently shows nothing.
- The agent-host BYOK path already demonstrates the intended in-band contract (a `mimeType:"usage"` data part with the `{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens}` payload), so the decode-side machinery exists; it is just not wired for the plain panel/participant path.

## Asks

Either would resolve this:

1. **Provider-side surface:** let `LanguageModelChatResponse` (or a `chatProvider`-proposal extension of it) carry usage — e.g. accept a `LanguageModelDataPart` with mimeType `"usage"` on the provider stream and populate `IChatRe
state.title: Chat context-usage widget cannot be fed by third-party language-model providers (no usage surface on the provider path)

## Feature Request

Improve initial Voice Mode startup when using an OpenAI GPT Live model, and reuse safe setup work across repeated starts.

## Motivation

@meganrogge reported that GPT Live Voice Mode took approximately **9 seconds end-to-end** to start before the improvement. This is a rough user-observed baseline, not an instrumented benchmark.

Startup currently repeats OpenAI model discovery during availability checking and session creation, with an additional model-availability request in between. These serial network requests delay microphone acquisition and connection setup.

## Requested Behavior

- Reduce redundant model-discovery and availability requests during startup.
- Briefly cache successful discovery/availability results in memory, scoped to the current API key and voice model.
- Preserve fresh credential and BYOK policy checks, cancellation, explicit refreshes, cache expiry, and failure retries.
- Do not persist credentials or model caches to disk, keep the microphone open between sessions, or reuse live sessions.

## Implementation and Validation

Addressed by #343553, which adds one-minute caches for silent OpenAI model discovery and successful GPT Live availability checks.

A separate, small instrumented macOS sample measured click-to-WebRTC-connected repeated-start medians of **4.009 seconds before** and **2.297 seconds after**. Those measurements use a narrower timing definition and do not replace the approximately 9-second user-observed end-to-end baseline.
state.title: Improve GPT Live Voice Mode startup latency

The Agents window sessions list is hard to scan. Custom groups, workspace sections, Pinned, and Chats all render as the same grey text, so with a lot of sessions it reads as a wall of grey and groups don't stand out.

To work around this today, I create empty custom groups named `===================== ENG`, `===== PRIV`, and `===== MISC` as visual dividers between engineering, personal, and miscellaneous work.

Browsers already solve both problems:
- **Colored tab groups:** a solid colored header, and a colored rail on the tabs inside. A collapsed group is a small color pill.
- **Workspaces:** separate sets of groups and tabs (for example, personal vs. two work contexts) that you switch between with an icon strip.

| Area | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **Colored groups** | Every custom group has a color: a named palette color (grey, blue, red, yellow, green, pink, purple, cyan, orange) or a custom hex. New groups get the next unused color. The default **Rail** style shows a colored header pill, plus a colored rail next to the group's sessions. |
| **Readable labels** | The label color on a colored header is picked automatically (light or dark, whichever has the higher WCAG contrast), and can be forced to light or dark. |
| **Collapsed groups** | A collapsed group is a compact pill with a session count and its most urgent status: needs input, then in progress, then unread. |
| **Workspace and built-in sections** | Workspace sections, **Pinned**, and **Chats** can optionally be colored too. Uncolored sections look the same as today. Pinned and Chats can only be recolored: they keep their names and their place in the list. |

You switch collections with an icon strip or the Sessions header menu; each collection remembers its last open session. To move sessions, groups, or workspaces to another collection, drag them onto its icon or use **Move to Collection**. With a single collection, the list works as it does today. state.body:
Extensions can add directories to `PATH` for the integrated terminal with `ExtensionContext.environmentVariableCollection`. Copilot Chat's terminal tool picks these up, but Copilot agent host sessions do not: their shells are spawned by the agent host process, which never sees extension environment collections.

So a tool an extension ships (for example the `dbgjs` CLI bundled with the dbgjs extension) can't be called by its name in agent host sessions. The only workaround is an extension tool that returns the absolute executable path, which leads to long, versioned commands into the extensions folder. Permission checks such as assisted auto-approve rightly treat those as suspicious and ask for confirmation.

**Proposal:** let an extension mark individual `PATH` entries of its environment variable collection as intended for agent terminals:

```ts
context.environmentVariableCollection.prepend('PATH', binDir + path.delimiter, {
	applyAtProcessCreation: true,
	applyToAgentTerminals: true, // proposed: terminalAgentEnvironment
});
```

The local agent host then adds these directories to `PATH` of the shells its agents run commands in, so the agent can run `dbgjs ...` directly. Changes apply to new commands without restarting VS Code or the agent host.

The opt-in is deliberately narrow: only global `PATH` prepend/append entries that are absolute directories qualify, and only from the local extension host to the local agent host. Other environment mutations (askpass variables, Python activation, ...) are not forwarded.
state.title: Let extensions add PATH entries to Copilot agent host terminals

## Summary

Compact mode for floating windows (since 1.100) removes tabs, breadcrumbs and
the status bar, so a floating window can show just one editor. For the
integrated browser, the browser's own toolbar (back, forward, reload, address,
actions) still takes about 40 px at the top. There is no setting, context key
or option to hide it.

## Use case

A small always-on-top window showing a page you work alongside: task
instructions, a checklist, a dashboard. At 420×640 the title bar and the
toolbar together take about 73 px, more than a tenth of the window. The page
is a local file the user opened on purpose; navigation controls are rarely
needed there.

## What exists today (source at tag 1.141.0, paths under `src/vs/`)

- The navigation bar is a toolbar widget that the browser editor mounts
  unconditionally (`workbench/contrib/browserView/electron-browser/browserEditor.ts`
  L505–509). The widget contract (L264–269) has only `location`, `element` and
  `order`, with no visibility predicate. The navigation feature returns the
  widget with no condition (`features/browserNavigationFeatures.ts` L271).
- Nothing in the browser contribution reads the compact flag or the
  auxiliary-window context keys.
- `workbench.browser.showInTitleBar` controls the globe button in the window's
  title bar (`features/browserTabManagementFeatures.ts` L908–917), not this bar.
- Individual items can be hidden from the toolbar's overflow menu. #320016
  (closed, shipped in 1.124) made more items customizable, but the strip
  itself stays.

## Proposal

Either of:

1. **Hide the toolbar when the browser editor is the only editor in a compact
   auxiliary window**, revealed on hover or with a keybinding (for example,
   focusing the address bar with Cmd+L brings it back).
2. **A setting**, `workbench.browser.toolbar.visible`: `always` (default),
   `notInCompactWindows`, `hover`.

---
*Observed 2026-10-12 in Jérémie Lumbroso's screenshots while building [porthole](https://github.com/jlumbroso/porthole), an extension that pops an HTML page into such a window; traced in
source by Surveyor 5.1 (Claude Fable 5.1), and confirmed independently from
the documentation by a second report; drafted by Glazier 5.5 (Claude Opus 5.5).*

state.body:
## Feature request

Support explicit spoken approval and rejection phrases in all 25 speech-recognition languages supported by Voice Mode, including languages selected through Automatic mode.

Currently, GPT Live's client-side approval routing is English-only. For example, with `agents.voice.language` set to `de`, saying “verwerfen” does not resolve the pending confirmation even if the voice agent says it rejected the action. See #342526.

## Proposed behavior

- Recognize complete, deterministic approval/rejection phrases in the selected voice language, retaining English commands as a fallback.
- Cover Arabic, Czech, Danish, German, English, Spanish, Finnish, French, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian Bokmål, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese, and Chinese, including simplified/traditional Chinese variants.
- Do not infer consent from substrings, qualified answers, negations, or ambiguous replies; prompt for an explicit reply or manual interaction instead.
- Preserve pending-confirmation identity checks, stale-response rejection, duplicate protection, and acknowledgement only after the client reports success.
- Read pending prompts and provide appropriate response guidance. For question forms, invite a voice reply or use of the controls in chat rather than requiring English, including for follow-up questions.
- Apply voice-language changes immediately without reconnecting.

This should not require an additional language-model request to classify a confirmation reply.

## Question reply language

When the agent supplies a question and choices in the user's language, the user can answer by voice in that language using an exact displayed choice label, a choice number, or free text where the question permits it. For example, a German question with “Westen” and “Osten” accepts “Osten”; a following text question accepts “Meine Bereitstellung.” English replies remain available, but are not required.

This is not unrestricted multilingual natural-language parsing. Shorthand commands such as “skip,” “other,” and “second,” and the multi-choice conjunction “and,” remain English-only. Localized paraphrases or ordinal words are outside this change.

The question text and choices come from the chat agent. Changing the VS Code locale or `agents.voice.language` does not itself translate that content; localized replies work when the supplied choices are localized, and free-text answers preserve the user's language.

Implementation: #343301.
state.title: Support localized approvals in GPT Live Voice Mode

## Context

Copilot Connectors are an independently gated, authenticated source in the customization Marketplace and MCP management UI. VS Code owns catalog, consent, and status UI; the Copilot runtime owns session-time MCP projection and credentials.

Use a disposable profile with a GitHub account eligible for Copilot Connectors. Enable:

```json
"chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled": true,
"chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled": true
```

Leave `chat.customizations.marketplace.sources.publicFeed.enabled` on initially so source independence can be checked. If the service is unavailable for the account or rollout, record the HTTP/status shown and mark the test blocked rather than changing account security settings.

## Authentication and connector lifecycle

1. Start signed out of GitHub and run **Chat: Open Customizations**.
2. Verify Discover still shows healthy non-connector sources. The Copilot Connectors source should present an explicit sign-in/recovery action rather than hiding other results or starting OAuth automatically.
3. Sign in with ordinary GitHub scopes. Browse the generic connector catalog and verify passive browsing does not unexpectedly request connector-management consent when the backend permits read-only access.
4. Open a connector such as Microsoft Learn Docs and use **Check Connection** or **Connect**. Verify any missing connector permission is requested explicitly for the same account. Cancel once and confirm no connection is created.
5. Repeat and authorize. Verify status updates without reopening Customizations, connector details remain accessible, and connected MCP servers appear under MCP Servers **Installed** while the product appears under **Connectors**.
6. Disable the GitHub Feed and verify Connectors remain available. Re-enable it, then disable only `chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled`; verify fresh connector discovery stops without breaking the other Marketplace sources.
7. Re-enable Connectors, disconnect the connector, and verify its status and MCP entries update. Recoverable HTTP 403 or rollout failures should remain actionable and must not trigger passive re-consent loops.

## Fresh Copilot Agent session tool projection

1. Connect a connector that exposes an easily verifiable read-only tool, such as Microsoft Learn Docs.
2. Immediately create a completely fresh **Copilot Agent** session; do not reuse a session that existed before connecting.
3. Ask the agent to use the connector's tool (for Microsoft Learn Docs, request an official documentation lookup) and verify the tool is available in that first fresh session and returns a relevant result.
4. Verify a user/workspace MCP server with the same name keeps its normal precedence and is not overwritten by the managed connector projection.
5. Disconnect the connector, then create another fresh Copilot Agent session. Verify the disconnected connector tool is no longer exposed.
6. Disable `chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled` and create one more fresh session. Verify connector tools remain absent while ordinary Copilot chat still starts successfully.

## Accessibility and cleanup

1. Navigate source recovery, connector cards, details, status actions, Installed, and Connectors using only the keyboard.
2. Verify sign-in, consent-required, connecting, connected, disconnecting, error, and disconnected states have understandable labels and do not rely on color alone.
3. Disconnect any test connector and restore the experimental settings.

**Expected:** Connector catalog access and consent are explicit and isolated from other sources; lifecycle status stays synchronized in Customizations; and a newly connected connector is reconciled before the first fresh Copilot Agent session becomes usa

state.body:
Bulk worktree cleanup in the Agents window needs clearer progress, stable results, and better performance with large session collections. Users should be able to see what happened to a whole batch without rows disappearing underneath them. Cleaning up a worktree must continue to preserve its session history.

### Requested improvements

- Immediately show confirmed worktrees as queued and prevent duplicate submissions while scheduling.
- Keep successfully cleaned rows in place for the lifetime of the open cleanup editor. Show **Worktree removed**, zero worktree storage, and no cleanup checkbox; keep the session link usable. Exclude these rows from cleanup selections and selected-size estimates. Closing and reopening should show current worktrees, not retain past completion rows.
- Keep a batch summary with removed, pending, failed, and needs-attention counts, including across filter changes and subsequent batches.
- Preserve selection, deliberately unchecked rows, session identity, and focus across progress updates and row recycling.
- Display the selected worktree count and estimated reclaimable size together, such as **Clean Up 3 Worktrees (~1.2 GB)**, with a clear screen-reader equivalent.
- Continue scheduling the rest of a batch when one worktree fails, reporting the affected session and error.
- Keep failed and unresolved worktrees visible. Offer **Retry Failed Worktrees** for eligible failures in the current filter without submitting unrelated selections. An unavailable or failed measurement must not be mistaken for confirmed removal.
- Use native virtualized `WorkbenchTable` widgets with resizable columns, fixed headers, and bounded, independently scrollable bodies. Render only visible rows and update changed storage cells without rebuilding unrelated row metadata or controls. Keep Select All above the table and scroll headers/rows together in narrow windows.
- Keep Select All, selected count, estimated size, and cleanup submission scoped to the complete filtered eligible set, including off-screen worktrees.
- Preserve keyboard navigation, usable session links, screen-reader progress and row information, and updated accessibility help.

### Done sessions can still need cleanup

**Done/archived is a session lifecycle state, not confirmation that its worktree was removed.** Older archival cleanup could time out after five seconds and leave a worktree behind. The cleanup editor must continue to show these leftover worktrees, including after reopening, and allow eligible retries with the longer cleanup timeout. Only confirmed removal should produce a nonselectable **Worktree removed** result.

### Storage measurement and performance scope

The database-backed storage estimates introduced in #344356 are separate from these UI improvements and are not available in the reported 1.144 installation. Preserve that cache behavior where available: unchanged idle worktrees can reuse valid persisted estimates, while active, changed, or invalidated worktrees still require measurement.

Virtualization and narrower cell updates address rendering cost; they do not by themselves introduce viewport-only measurement or constant-time processing of full service snapshots. Keep complete filtered selection and size-estimate semantics rather than silently limiting them to visible rows.

### Implementation

Tracked by #344589. The retention, combined count/size, native-table, accessibility, and recovery changes are committed and pushed in `ab2f580667042acf330b148dd03cbe41f82a06f5`. Validation passed for 105 cleanup editor/service tests, 23 targeted provider tests, client type-checking, and changed-file hygiene. The PR description records exact commands and manual validation limitations.
state.title: Improve bulk worktree cleanup progress and recovery

state.body:
Extensions cannot add Markdown syntax to the new Markdown editor (`vscode.markdown.editor`).

The preview has `markdown.markdownItPlugins`, and many extensions use it to add syntax: footnotes, admonitions, wiki links, definition lists, emoji shortcodes, and so on. The editor parses with micromark through `@vscode/markdown-editor` and has its own view, so none of those plugins reach it. Checked in 1.137.0. The editor bundle (`markdown-editor-out/editor.js`) has no reference to `markdownItPlugins`.

As far as I can find, the only extension point the editor has is `markdown.codeBlockEditorProviders`. It replaces the view of fenced code blocks that match a selector. That helps for diagram-style blocks. It does nothing for inline syntax or for block syntax outside a code fence.

The result is that a document that renders correctly in the preview, with the user's installed extensions, renders differently in the editor, and extension authors have no way to close that gap. #337447 (footnotes) is one case of this. Each missing construct now needs its own request against the built-in package.

Requested: a contribution point that lets an extension add syntax to the editor. Two possible ways:

- Accept micromark syntax extensions plus a matching rendering and serialisation hook. This is the closest match to how the editor parses today, and micromark's extension format is already public.
- A narrower version: let an extension claim a node type or an inline pattern and render it read-only, while the source text round-trips unchanged. That would cover most preview plugins, whose output is display-only.

Whichever is chosen, the source text must round-trip unchanged when a user edits around the extended syntax, so that installing an extension never rewrites a file.
state.title: Markdown editor: let extensions add syntax, like markdown.markdownItPlugins does for the preview

state.body:
### Problem

The comment boxes that carry agent feedback for a session are drawn over the
editor reading view, pinned to the right side of the viewport. They cannot be
moved. While a comment box is open it covers the source lines underneath it, and
when comments on nearby lines are shown at the same time the right half of the
reading area is almost completely blocked. When one comment box is tall enough
to push the boxes below it further down, there is also no way to tell which line
those pushed-down comments are anchored to.

### Proposed solution

- Let a comment box be dragged to any position inside the editor viewport, while
  the box still follows the reading view as it scrolls.
- Moving a comment box must not change the range it is anchored to.
- Draw a dashed pointer line between a comment box and the range it is anchored
  to, the way Word comment balloons connect to their text with a leader line, and
  Google Docs comment cards link visually to the text they refer to.
- While the pointer hovers over a comment box, highlight the range that box is
  anchored to, so the association is easier to read.

### Alternatives considered

- Add a collapse button to the comment box so its content can be folded away.
  This reduces the overlap, but still gives no visible pointer back to the
  anchored text.

### Additional context

- Comparable implementations: Word comment balloons with leader lines, Google
  Docs comment cards in the right margin.
- Why this matters: the feedback loop of an agent session is reading and writing
  many short comments across one file. If every box covers the code it comments
  on, that review pass is much slower than it needs to be.

### Environment

- VS Code: 1.138.0 (x64), stable
- OS: Windows 10 Pro, 10.0.19045, 64-bit
- Area: the `add comment` feature in the Markdown editor inside the Agents window

Reported by @BlazeNebula. Drafted with GitHub Copilot (agent-assisted).
state.title: Markdown editor: Make the comment box repositionable, with a pointer line to its anchored range

### Problem

When working on Flutter projects with multiple flavors (dev / staging / production), I constantly switch between three controls that live in three different places:

1. **Run button** – in the Run and Debug view
2. **Launch configuration picker** – in the Run and Debug view header (only visible when that view is open)

state.body:
## Summary

Add an explicit environment picker to the Agents Window new-session experience. Initially, the picker could offer **Local** and **Remote**, **Cloud** while being designed to accommodate additional environment types over time.

## Motivation

The place where work runs is a distinct choice from the source or workspace being used. Today these concepts can become coupled, making it harder to understand or extend session creation as more execution environments become available.

An environment picker would make this choice visible and establish a scalable model for environments such as:

- **Local** — run on the current machine.
- **Remote** — run through a supported remote connection or host.
- Future environments, such as cloud-hosted, containerized, or other provider-backed environments.

## Proposed direction

- Add an **Environment** picker to the new-session UI.
- Keep environment selection independent from:
  - Source/workspace selection.
  - Agent or harness selection.
  - Session intent.
- Start with **Local** and **Remote** where supported.
- Allow environment providers to contribute availability, display information, configuration/connection actions, and capability constraints without redesigning the picker for every new environment type.
- Remember the user's explicit selection when appropriate.
- Clearly communicate unavailable or unsupported source/environment/harness combinations rather than silently switching environments.
- Ensure the selected environment remains visible before launch and is represented consistently when restoring or inspecting a session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can explicitly choose between available Local and Remote environments when creating a session.
- [ ] Environment selection is modeled separately from the selected source/workspace and agent/harness.
- [ ] The picker can accommodate additional environment types without introducing environment-specific top-level UI.
- [ ] Unsupported combinations are disabled or explained with actionable guidance.
- [ ] The selected environment is preserved across session creation and restoration where applicable.

## Feature request

Support versionless model-family names in the `model` frontmatter of custom agent files (`.agent.md`) so they resolve to the newest available model in that family.

For example, a setting such as:

state.body:
## Problem

Agent Bakeoff can compare models and reasoning configurations, but it does not let users compare the same workflow with and without a skill, or compare two versions of a skill.

This makes it hard to tell whether a skill improves results, introduces regressions, or adds time and token usage without enough benefit. Comparing different models at the same time also makes it harder to attribute the difference to the skill.

## Desired comparisons

- Run the same task side by side with a skill enabled and disabled.
- Compare a skill before and after an edit on the same task.
- Keep the model, reasoning settings, prompt, starting repository state, and other customizations the same so the skill is the variable under comparison.
- Inspect results, code changes, validation evidence, elapsed time, and token usage, with clear labels for the skill state or version used in each attempt.

The disabled attempt should actually exclude the skill, rather than rely on an instruction to ignore it.

## Connection to evaluation systems

These comparisons could help skill authors identify useful test tasks, expected outcomes, and failure cases for evaluation systems. The comparison evidence should make it possible to distinguish improvements from regressions and run-to-run variation, and to reproduce the conditions of each attempt. A single judged winner is not enough to establish that a skill consistently helps.

The same need applies to plugins that bundle skills or other workflow customizations.

Related: #335085, #342693.

_🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

state.body:
## Feature request

Allow an automation to start by executing a script, before creating an AI session. The script should be able to complete the automation entirely without AI participation, or request that a new AI session be started.

Conceptually, an automation could support an action such as `prompt | script`. A script action would perform deterministic work or checks first and decide whether AI is needed.

## Motivation

Many automations can do useful work with a script alone, or cheaply determine that there is nothing for an agent to do. Starting an AI session for every trigger adds unnecessary cost and noise. Conversely, a script may discover work or encounter a failure for which AI assistance is useful.

## Independent outcomes

Script success/failure and the decision to continue with AI should be independent, supporting all four combinations:

| Script result | Start a new AI session? | Intended behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Success | No | Complete the automation successfully without involving AI. |
| Success | Yes | Start a new AI session with the script's output/context for follow-up work. |
| Failure | No | Report the failed script/run without involving AI. |
| Failure | Yes | Start a new AI session with the failure details for investigation or recovery; retain the script failure in the run history. |

## Expected behavior

- Run the script before creating an AI session, not as a tool invocation inside an already-started AI session.
- Provide an explicit, documented way to request or suppress AI continuation independently of the script's success/failure status.
- When continuation is requested, allow a configured prompt and script output/context to be passed to the new session.
- Preserve script output, errors, and exit status in the automation run history, including runs that never create an AI session.
- Surface invalid or missing control output and script execution errors explicitly, with documented behavior.

## Design question: signaling contract

The exact protocol needs design. A special exit code (for example, `-2`) or a stdout marker such as `no-ai` could express "no AI needed", but a single special status conflates independent concerns, and free-form stdout markers may collide with ordinary output.

Consider a structured result or dedicated control channel that expresses the AI-continuation decision separately from the process exit status. The request is for the four combinations above, not a particular exit code or marker. The design should also define how an AI follow-up affects the overall run status after a failed script.
state.title: Automations: support script-first actions with optional AI continuation

## Current limitation

Compare Agents currently requires both a Git remote and at least one commit before comparison setup is available. Neither restriction reflects the actual isolation requirements: committed local branches can already create worktrees without a remote, while an unborn repository can be isolated by snapshotting its current non-ignored files into an internal base commit before creating each attempt worktree.

This blocks local-only projects and newly initialized projects from using Compare Agents even though they can run safely in independent worktrees.

## Requested behavior

- Offer Compare Agents for a local Git repository without a remote.
- Offer Compare Agents for an unborn repository with no commits.
- Preserve independent worktree isolation for every attempt, Judge, and Synthesizer session.
- For an unborn repository, snapshot the current tracked, staged, modified, and non-ignored untracked files without changing the user index or creating a commit on the source branch.
- Start each isolated branch from that snapshot so the worktree is populated and clean and comparison diffs include only agent changes.
- Continue honoring the existing ignored-file copy and symlink configuration.
- Keep existing committed local and remote repository behavior unchanged.

## Validation

Cover no-remote eligibility, unborn-branch worktree selection, and a real-Git end-to-end flow proving the source branch remains unborn while the isolated worktree is populated and clean.

state.body:
### Problem

A `TreeItem` can declare a single `command`, executed when the user clicks the item's label. There is no way to declare a different command for a modifier-click (Alt/Ctrl/Cmd), so extensions that expose a "primary action" and a closely-related variant must either pick one as the click behaviour, or ship a setting that flips it globally.

The common shape of this is "open" vs "open in a new window" / "open to the side": conventional in tabbed UIs, and something users expect to work by habit.

### Why this is a gap rather than a new concept

VS Code already has exactly this concept, one level down. The `menus` contribution point accepts an `alt` key, documented as the identifier of an alternative command to run, which must itself be declared in the `commands` section. So an inline action *button* on a tree item can already have an alt behaviour, while the tree item's own click cannot. The proposal is only to close that asymmetry.

### Proposal

Let `TreeItem.command` be paired with an optional alternative, e.g.:

```ts
treeItem.command = { command: 'ext.open', title: '', arguments: [x] };
treeItem.altCommand = { command: 'ext.openInNewWindow', title: '', arguments: [x] };
```

Semantics mirroring `menus.alt`: when the modifier is held at click time, the alternative runs instead. Extensions that don't set it are unaffected.

### Alternatives considered

- **A setting per extension.** Works, but it's a global flip rather than a per-click choice, and every extension reinvents it with a different name.
- **Inline action buttons.** Already used, and fine as a discoverable fallback, but they require hitting a small target on the right edge of the row instead of the row itself — which is the ergonomic problem being reported.
- **`window.openFoldersInNewWindow`.** Solves the folder-opening case specifically, but it is global and changes native behaviour (`File > Open Folder`, Recent, `code .`), so it isn't scoped to the tree the user is actually clicking in.

### Related

- #18064 — the same request for QuickPick items (open since 2017)
- #130880 — key bindings on tree view items
- Downstream example: alefragnani/vscode-project-manager#825 and #817
state.title: Allow TreeItem.command to declare an alternative command for modifier-click

## Feature request

Allow Quick Open (Ctrl+P) to accept a supported link directly and open its target using VS Code's link-handling infrastructure.

Part of #342050.

## Motivation

A copied link should be a usable navigation input, not something that first has to be pasted into a document or chat to become actionable. This should work with the views that can handle that link, rather than assuming every input is a file-name query or every URL belongs in an external browser.

## Proposed behavior

- Recognize supported links entered or pasted into Ctrl+P and offer a clear action to open the target.
- Use the shared link-handler resolution/defaults, including contributed handlers where applicable.
- Provide a discoverable keyboard open-to-side action, equivalent to the story's Alt+click intent. Place the target beside the editor group from which Quick Open was invoked, preserving that view.
- Preserve navigation context encoded in the link where supported by the selected handler.
- Keep existing file-search and Quick Open prefix behavior intact; recognize links without broadly reinterpreting ordinary search text.
- Give clear feedback for invalid or unsupported links rather than silently opening the wrong target.

## Acceptance criteria
