state.description:
Fixes the intermittent `chat/generatedImages/chatGeneratedImages/BatchGridNarrow/Light` screenshot change, most recently reported on an unrelated PR in [#344959 (comment)](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344959#issuecomment-6495931338). This follows #343082, which fixed a different flake in the same fixtures.

## Cause

- The Screenshots job renders fixtures with 8 workers. Each worker renders its contiguous slice of fixtures in a single page, without reloading. `BatchGridNarrow` renders right after `BatchGrid`.
- All batch fixtures draw their images with the same `createImage(width, height, index)` calls, so they produce byte-identical `data:` URLs. `BatchGrid` is 760 px wide, so it draws them larger.
- Chromium appears to draw the narrow grid's thumbnails from those larger decodes when they are still around. Only portrait thumbnails are affected. They are drawn at the smallest scale: 68 px tall from 1356 px, about 1/20, versus about 1/15 for squares and landscapes. Whether the decodes are reused varies from run to run, so the antialiased edges of the sun and mountain move by a few levels.

## Evidence

**CI history.** I fetched the screenshot service manifests for about 700 `main` commits. Since its last intentional change (#343609), `BatchGridNarrow/Light` has had two hashes:

- `12dec515`, 145 times.
- `35f07299`, 3 times today (0f33e8274d, fc8954c90f, d41a36a4d8). Each time the next commit went back to `12dec515`.

The other `BatchGrid*` fixtures kept a single hash. I checked two flipped and two normal runs: they used the same runner image, Chromium 149.0.7827.55, `node_modules` cache, and 1949 fixtures. The difference is 772 px with a max channel delta of 12/255, all in portrait thumbnails #3, #5 and #8. The layout is identical.

**Local repro.** I used a small Playwright script on macOS that renders fixtures in one page like the CLI does, with the same `--disable-partial-raster` launch flag. Before this PR, the narrow grid's output depends on what rendered earlier in the page:

| Rendered before `BatchGridNarrow` | Before this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `BatchGridLoading` (no images) | `1fe68475` | `77715b40` |
| `BatchGridLoading`, `BatchGrid` | `df6ef8b8`: portraits #3, #5, #8, #10 differ | `77715b40` |
| `BatchGridLoading`, `BatchGridInProgress` | `472139da`: portraits #3, #5 differ | `77715b40` |
| `BatchGrid`, `BatchGridInProgress`, `BatchGridLoading` | `472139da` | `77715b40` |

The tiles that change are the portraits that the preceding fixture rendered. `BatchGridInProgress` leaves #8 generating and has no #10. Each sequence gave the same hash on repeated runs.

**Same mechanism as CI.** I compared CI's flake (`35f07299` − `12dec515`) with the local leak after `BatchGrid` (`df6ef8b8` − `1fe68475`) pixel by pixel. The leak covers 99% of CI's changed pixels, and the deltas correlate with Pearson r = −0.99. So on `main` the usual render (145 of 148) is the one drawn from `BatchGrid`'s decodes, and the rare one is the clean render.

## Fix

`renderBatchGrid` takes a `firstVariant` offset, and `BatchGridNarrow` passes 10. Its images keep the same palettes and dimensions but are labelled `11 / …` to `20 / …`, so no other fixture renders the same bytes. Other fixtures are unchanged.

## Expected screenshot changes

The screenshot report on this PR should list only `BatchGridNarrow/Light` as changed, because of the new labels and portrait edges no longer drawn from `BatchGrid`'s decodes. It is not in `blocks-ci-screenshots.md`, so no baseline update is needed.

## How to test

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed, on the branch rebased onto current `main`.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/test/browser/componentFixtures/chat/chatGeneratedImages.fixture.ts`: passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/component-explorer render --project ./test/componentFixtures/component-explorer.json --workers 1 --fixture-id-regex '(chatAutoModeResolutionContentPart/Routing|chatGeneratedImages/BatchGrid(Narrow)?)/Light$'`, 3 tim

state.description:
## Summary

On macOS, frequent writes to an untracked file kept the watcher batch open and delayed the invalidation of tracked files until the writes stopped. This made the native cases of `irrelevant_events_do_not_delay_invalidation` fail consistently (took ~3.3s, i.e. the whole churn).

Why: FSEvents keeps the `ItemCreated` flag set on a recently created file, so each write to an existing file shows up as a `Create(File)` event. When a tracked file in the same directory changed, `mark_parent_dir` added that directory to the batch, even though nothing had listed it. The fast path in `is_relevant` then treated every later `Create` of a sibling as relevant because its parent was in the batch, and each of those events pushed the batch deadline back.

The fast path now only checks the path itself. The slow path still checks the parent against `dir_invalidator_map`, so events under a directory whose listing is tracked still count as relevant.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p turbo-tasks-fs --lib watcher::` on macOS: all 19 tests pass, including `repeated_writes_to_tracked_file_are_debounced`. Before this change, the two native `irrelevant_events_do_not_delay_invalidation` cases failed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
state.title: Turbopack: don't treat events as relevant because their parent dir is in the watcher batch

Adds a unit test harness check that fails any top-level suite which leaves a different set of commands, menu items or keybindings registered than it started with.

## Why

All test files in a unit test run share one page, so a registration that a suite doesn't dispose changes the behavior of every suite that runs after it. PR CI runs per-area file sets with `--runList` and `--workers 4`, while the official build runs every file in one page. A leak can therefore pass PR CI and still break `main`. That happened with #344654: `chatViewModeActions.test` called `registerChatActions()` in `suiteSetup` and never unregistered `workbench.action.chat.open`, which broke `ChatTipService` in every official unit test job until #344844 fixed it.

This check makes such a leak fail in the leaking suite itself, in whatever file set it runs, PR CI included.

## How

- `src/vs/platform/actions/test/common/registryLeakCheck.ts`: `installRegistryLeakCheck(mocha.suite)` adds two hooks to every top-level suite:
  - a `suiteSetup` hook, registered before the suite's own hooks, that snapshots `CommandsRegistry`, `MenuRegistry` (commands and items for every `MenuId`) and `KeybindingsRegistry`
  - a `suiteTeardown` hook, registered after them, so it runs after the suite's own cleanup. It fails with the list of registered, replaced or unregistered entries.
- `test/unit/browser/renderer.html` and `test/unit/electron/renderer.js` install it before loading the test modules.
- Registrations made while modules load are part of the baseline, so only registrations made by a suite's hooks and tests count.
- The 8 suites that leak today are in `knownLeakingSuites`, so this lands green. They should be fixed separately and removed from that list:
  - `AgentSessionsActions`
  - `Chat code-block action telemetry`
  - `ChatMcpAuthenticationContentPart`
  - `Edit session sync`
  - `ExtHostLanguageFeatureCommands`
  - `Inline chat zone widget — menu contributions`
  - `RetryChatAction`
  - `Sessions - Layout Actions`

## Validation

- **Red, with #344844 reverted, running only `chatViewModeActions.test.ts`:** the check fails `Chat View Mode` in both the Chromium and Electron runners, starting with `registered command 'workbench.action.chat.open'`.
- **Green, with #344844:** 19 passing in Chromium and 20 in Electron.
- **Full Chromium suite** (all files in one page): 49,501 passing. Before the allowlist, the check failed only the 8 suites listed above. The one other failure was the unrelated `Extensions viewlet notification layout` network error, which also fails on this machine without the change. The 8 allowlisted files pass together (129 passing).
- **Full Electron suite with `--workers 4`:** 0 leak-check failures. The 167 failures on this machine are the same local rendering timeouts (`MultiEditorTabsControl`, `ChatListRenderer` and others) that also occur without the change.
- **Cost:** one check (two snapshots plus the diff) takes about 0.9 ms at full registry size (1,281 commands, 171 menus, 604 keybindings). Across 2,708 top-level suites that's about 2.5 s per full run, which is under 0.5% of an 11 min Chromium run.
- eslint is clean, and tsc reports no errors in `platform/actions`.

## Not covered

- Registries other than commands, menus and keybindings, for example editor contributions or configuration.
- Changes in the order of menu items that are registered the same number of times. Commands report a changed active registration, and keybindings and menu items report how often each object is registered.
- Leaks between nested suites in the same file.
- Non-registry leaks such as global CSS (see #344831) or focus order (#344605).

## Overlap with open drafts (checked Oct 29 with `git merge-tree`)

- **#342237 (parallel workers), #344229 (repeat added tests) and #343097 (worker benchmark experiment):** this PR adds no new conflicting files with any of them. They already conflict with `main` in `test/unit/*` and the workflows. The only overlap is in #343097's `ren

With `chat.agentHost.experimental.mcpToolRouting` enabled, keep Connector authentication out of unrelated chat responses while making Connectors discoverable through tool search.

### Changes

- Suppress proactive inline hints and screen-reader notifications for Connector-owned MCP servers using authoritative ownership metadata, including late-arriving ownership.
- Register deferred routing proxies when the asynchronous Connector catalog arrives, and refresh/remove them when the catalog changes. Names and descriptions identify the catalog display name, such as **Work IQ (Connector)**, while activation targets the exact runtime server ID.
- Feed those proxies into the existing SDK tool-search candidate path. Merely discovering a Connector does not start it or request authorization.
- Request the existing session-account Connector authorization only when its routing tool is invoked. Handle both SDK authentication callbacks and authorization requirements reported only through Connector status, including challenges that arrive while startup is pending.
- Preserve cancellation, disabled-server checks, client-tool replacement ordering, retry after failed registration, and live tool discovery. Never accept a per-MCP token as Connector authorization or write Connector tool metadata to the shared configured-server cache.
- Update the setting description and add regression coverage. All new routing proxies are deferred; the reviewed eager-tool sets are unchanged.

Connector reconciliation still uses the existing idle boundary after account-credential rebind: it releases the stale authentication request, refreshes the Connector once the turn is idle, and a subsequent routing attempt can discover the current tools. This PR does not change that lifecycle or bypass consent.

state.description:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344442

With `files.autoSave` and `files.trimTrailingWhitespace` enabled, typing a word followed by a space in the Markdown editor and pausing lost the space: auto save trimmed it, and the editor received the trimmed document. Typing `Hello `, pausing, and typing `world` produced `Helloworld`.

In the text editor this does not happen: on auto save, the trim save participants (`files.trimTrailingWhitespace`, `files.trimFinalNewlines`) leave the lines with a cursor alone. They only knew about code editor cursors, though. A custom text editor such as the Markdown editor is not a code editor, so every line was trimmed.

Custom text editors that implement the proposed `customTextEditorNavigation` API (used for Outline and breadcrumbs) already report their selection in document positions, and the Markdown editor does. The trim participants now treat that selection like a code editor cursor on auto save:

- Trailing whitespace: the cursor line keeps its whitespace up to the cursor; all other lines are still trimmed.
- Final newlines: nothing at or above the cursor line is removed.
- If a visible editor that is neither a code nor a diff editor shows the file but does not report a cursor (no navigation API, or no text selection), auto save skips both trims instead of trimming the line being typed on.

Explicit saves trim as before.

## Validation

- New save participant tests cover a custom editor that reports its cursor and one that does not.
- Reproduced in Code OSS with `files.autoSave: afterDelay` (1000 ms), `files.trimTrailingWhitespace: true`, and the Markdown editor, by typing ` Hello `, waiting for auto save, then typing `world`:
  - Before: the file contained `First paragraph. Helloworld`.
  - After: `First paragraph. Hello world`, while another line `Other line   ` in the same file was trimmed to `Other line` by the same auto save.

## Limitations

`customTextEditorNavigation` reports one selection per panel, so only one cursor per custom editor is spared.
state.title: Spare the Markdown editor's cursor line when trimming whitespace on auto save

## Summary

Top of a stack: #100349 → #100294 → #100324 → #100350 → this PR.

When a Node.js middleware entrypoint triggers registering `instrumentation.ts`, #100350 emits the lifecycle spans as siblings of `middleware GET`. This PR nests them inside the middleware span instead, since the middleware triggered registration:

```
route / page entrypoint (unchanged):
 [P →] GET /page (BaseServer.handleRequest, backdated to cover registration)
        ├─ load instrumentation module
        ├─ register instrumentation
        └─ prepare route module → render …

Node.js middleware entrypoint, no parent:
 GET (Next.request, backdated)
  ├─ middleware GET
  │   ├─ load instrumentation module
  │   └─ register instrumentation
  └─ GET /page

Node.js middleware entrypoint with host span / incoming traceparent P:
 P
  ├─ middleware GET
  │   ├─ load instrumentation module
  │   └─ register instrumentation
  └─ GET /page
```

### How

- The middleware adapter calls the deferred emitter first thing inside the `Middleware.execute` span, rather than right before starting it.
- When this request triggered registration, the middleware span is backdated to the request start so it covers registration; otherwise its timing is unchanged.
- The shared parent is still captured before entering the middleware span, so the middleware and the render stay siblings, and `traceparent` handling / forwarding are unchanged.

## Verification

- Collector suite: cold Node.js middleware direct entrypoints (no parent, incoming `traceparent`, host span) now assert the lifecycle spans are children of the middleware span, with the middleware span starting no later than them and no earlier than its parent. Fail-first: these 3 tests fail on #100350.
- Deploy-capable `test/e2e/app-dir/otel-middleware-trace`: the deployed span tree snapshots now show the Node.js middleware's lifecycle spans under `middleware GET`. Self-hosted startup spans remain roots.
state.title: Nest middleware-triggered instrumentation spans in the middleware span

## Summary

Stacked on #100324. Includes the commits from #100392, which were folded into this PR.

Next.js emits two lifecycle spans for `instrumentation.ts` in the Node.js runtime: `load instrumentation module` and `register instrumentation`. They're backdated, because they're emitted after `register()` returns (`register()` usually installs the tracer provider). Until now they were always separate root traces.

Direct entrypoints (Vercel, adapters, standalone handlers) register instrumentation lazily, in the first request. That split the first request's work across extra traces. Now the spans join the trace of the request that triggered registration:

```
route / page entrypoint:
 [P →] GET /page (BaseServer.handleRequest, backdated to cover registration)
        ├─ load instrumentation module
        ├─ register instrumentation
        └─ prepare route module → render …

Node.js middleware entrypoint, no parent:
 GET (Next.request, backdated)
  ├─ middleware GET (backdated to cover registration)
  │   ├─ load instrumentation module
  │   └─ register instrumentation
  └─ GET /page

Node.js middleware entrypoint with host span / incoming traceparent P:
 P
  ├─ middleware GET (backdated to cover registration)
  │   ├─ load instrumentation module
  │   └─ register instrumentation
  └─ GET /page
```

### How

- `ensureInstrumentationRegisteredWithDeferredSpans`: when this call starts registration and registration succeeds, the lifecycle spans are recorded instead of emitted. The function returns an idempotent emitter to that caller only. Concurrent callers, later callers and startup callers get nothing.
- `RouteModule.ensureInstrumentation(req, { deferSpans: true })` is called by the templates before `traceRequest`. It records when the request started and returns that time, together with the emitter, as `instrumentation`. `traceRequest` takes it as an option, backdates the request span to that time, and emits the lifecycle spans as the span's first children.
- The Node.js middleware template passes the emitter and the start time to the adapter. The adapter calls the emitter first thing inside the `Middleware.execute` span and backdates that span to the request start.
  - The shared parent (incoming `traceparent`, host span, or the backdated inserted `Next.request` root) is still captured before entering the middleware span. The middleware and the render stay siblings, and `traceparent` handling and forwarding are unchanged.
- Unchanged:
  - `next start` / `next dev` startup registration (separate roots).
  - Registration errors: emitted immediately with the same statuses, including non-`Error` throws.
  - Edge (no lifecycle spans).
  - No `instrumentation.ts`, or no `register` export.
- User-created spans in `instrumentation.ts` are out of scope (see #100324).

## Verification

- Collector suite, cold direct entrypoints:
  - Route/page requests, with and without an incoming `traceparent`, and with a host span.
  - Node.js middleware requests: no parent, incoming `traceparent`, host span.
  - Each test asserts exactly one load span and one register span in the request's trace, parented as shown above and covered by the backdated parent. For middleware, the parent is the middleware span, and it starts no later than the lifecycle spans and no earlier than its own parent.
  - Direct-entrypoint single-trace assertions no longer exclude lifecycle spans as startup work. Under `next start`, startup spans stay roots. Fail-first verified.
- Deploy-capable `test/e2e/app-dir/otel-middleware-trace`: span tree snapshots of the lifecycle spans with their ancestors, plus the first request's tree including them.
  - Deployed: children of the request span that triggered registration, or of `middleware GET` for Node.js middleware.
  - `next dev` / `next start`: startup roots.
  - No deploy gate.
- Unit tests for the deferral helper: once-only, concurrency, startup ownership, no `register`, `register()` errors (including `throw undefined`), and mo
state.title: Emit instrumentation lifecycle spans in the request that registered it

state.description:
Every platform's Compile job blocks in **Apply CG NOTICE** until the Quality job uploads the `notice_output` artifact. `notice@0` often times out against the NOTICE API after a fixed ~241 s and is retried, so the artifact can arrive minutes after the compile jobs need it.

Across 42 scheduled insiders from Oct 14 to 29:
- **15 builds hit at least one timeout**, with 28 failed calls in total. The retry usually succeeds in about 30 s.
- In those builds the macOS Compile jobs waited up to **11.7 min**. On macOS that wait is on the release path (Compile, then Sign, then Publish).
- Linux and Windows waited up to 10.3 min.

## Change

This moves the NOTICE steps of the Quality job to right after dependency install, ahead of `Compile & Hygiene` (~3.3 min). The moved steps are:
- built-in extension CG details
- Component Detection
- `notice@0`
- the cache fallback
- the merged NOTICE upload

`notice_output` is ready about 3.3 min earlier. That absorbs a single NOTICE API timeout entirely. The Quality job isn't on the critical path; it finishes 10–20 min in, long before Publish. No step changed, and the YAML still holds the same set of steps. A new `Remove NOTICE intermediates` step deletes `.oss-build-out` and `ThirdPartyNotices.generated.txt` before the lint checks. ESLint and hygiene would otherwise reject them, and the outputs are already staged.

**Why scanning before compile is safe:** Component Detection reads manifests and lockfiles. Its debug log on 490496 shows that the only files compile adds to the scan are 6 `out-build/**/cgmanifest.json` copies of the `src/**/cgmanifest.json` files it already reads, so the detected components are the same. `notice@0` still runs after Component Detection, so the NOTICE comes from this build's snapshot.

`notice@0` has no request-timeout or retry input (only `outputfile`, `outputformat` and `additionaldata`), so the 240 s wait can't be shortened from the pipeline. A step `timeoutInMinutes` cancel wouldn't be retried.

## Validation

- Official-parameter def 111 run [490960](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=490960), on insider 490752's commit with Publish off. It failed in `Compile & Hygiene` on the intermediates, which is now fixed. The `notice_output` it uploaded is byte-identical to 490752's: `ThirdPartyNotices.new.txt`, `.extensions.txt` and `.generated.txt`. Only `notice-meta.txt` differs, in its build and branch fields.
- Rerun with the fix: [491073](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=491073), using the same parameters. I'll check that Apply CG NOTICE is green on every platform and that the NOTICE is unchanged.
- YAML parses. The job has the same steps as before plus the cleanup step.

> Authored with Copilot

## Summary

When a Client Component imports a module outside `app/` (e.g. `lib/shared.js`) that depends on `next/headers`, the error said the API was being used "in the Pages Router", even in apps with no `pages` directory. The RSC transform picked the message by whether the file is inside `appDir`, but a module outside `app/` can still be part of the App Router graph.

The transform now takes an explicit `isAppRouter` option. Webpack sets it from the bundle layer, and Turbopack from whether the context has an `appDir` (only the Pages Router context passes none). App Router graphs get the Client Component message; Pages Router files still get the Pages Router one.

state.description:
MPA form submissions to Cache Components pages could return only the continuation of a prerender. The action executed, but the response omitted the HTML document and did not render the returned `useActionState` value.

This change renders a complete document for MPA form submissions while retaining the RDC supplied by the prerender. This preserves ordinary `'use cache'` values on deployments where the default handler has no prerendered entries in memory. The action handler also prepares the render phase for MPA form submissions that do not revalidate data. Ordinary not-found responses include the root layout.

The diagnosis and reproduction in #99981 identified the self-hosted case. This fix also handles postponed state supplied by Vercel before the action body, without changing how that body is decoded.

The tests cover plain and stateful forms, both postponed-state variants, submission before hydration, cache reuse, invalidation, blocking routes, and ordinary and global not-found responses.

Fixes #99756
Closes #99981

state.description:
Fixes #343911

## Root cause
After a top-level worktree session is nested under another session, its chat becomes a non-default chat that owns an additional-worktree record. `WorktreeAnnouncementContribution.onOutgoingTurn` announces any owned worktree whose per-chat `worktreeAnnouncement.emitted` memento is unset. The memento did not travel with the move, so the next turn announced "Created isolated worktree" again. After a reload the original notice is restored from history and the memento is set, which hid the problem.

## Fix
`moveChat` marks the receiving chat as already announced for every worktree it comes to own because of the move: the hand-over, and the transfers from `planWorktreeMove`. All of these records already existed and were already announced. This goes through a new `didHandOverWorktree` on the chat contributions service and an `onDidHandOverWorktree` hook, which sets the existing memento. `onOutgoingTurn` is unchanged, so a genuinely new worktree (first send, a peer chat's first send, `isolate_session` on a chat with turns) still announces once.

The new hook is optional, consistent with the existing hooks (`onDidRestoreSession?`, `onOutgoingTurn?`, `onHydrateTurns?`), which are all optional.

## Tests
- `agentService.test.ts`: a session nested with its worktree already announced does not announce on its next turn; a chat whose own worktree transfers with it is marked as announced.
- `chatContributions.test.ts`: not re-announced for a handed-over chat; a restore shows the original notice once; a new worktree for a chat with prior turns announces once.
- Mutation checks: removing the hand-over marking fails the nest test; removing the transfers marking fails the transfers test.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`, `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`, `npm run typecheck-client`: clean.
- Whole `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/` folder: 13545 passing, 75 pending, 0 failing. An earlier run hit one timeout in "legacy sessions their provider cannot read its catalog for are parked, then woken and converted when it becomes readable". It passes alone and is an unrelated pre-existing flake.

## Live check (throwaway seeded profile, claude/codex off)
- Unfixed build: after nesting, the next turn shows the notice a second time.
- Fixed build: the notice shows once on the first send. After nest, no repeat. After a reload, the original notice shows once. After nest then Undo, the next turn shows no repeat.
- Promote was not driven live: the UI has no reachable promote action for this chat. It goes through the same `moveChat` marking site.

state.description:
> **Note:** this PR was squash-merged with its first two commits only. Two follow-up commits pushed to the branch after the merge were not included: making the harness-switch carry-over single-use (the open Copilot review thread) and removing three source comments. The validation and review below describe that later head (`b52994bae2f`), not the merged code.

Fixes #338347

## What changed

In the Agents window, a prompt typed in a new chat of an existing session was lost when the user switched to another chat and back. Now it is kept per chat and restored when that chat is shown again.

- `ISessionsChatViewStateService` stores an in-memory unsent draft per chat resource, next to the per-chat view state it already keeps.
- `SharedChatInputComposer` gets `getDraft()` / `setDraft()` for the input text and attachments.
- `NewChatInSessionWidget.setChat` saves the previous chat's draft and applies the new chat's draft. A repeated call for the same chat only refreshes it. `dispose` saves the current draft. A chat that was never shown keeps whatever the composer restored.
- A harness switch replaces the draft chat but must keep the typed input (the existing "carry over" behavior). Only the chat of the harness being switched to keeps the input. Opening any other unsent chat meanwhile shows that chat's own draft.

## Why

`chatGroupView` swaps the new-chat view for a chat view when the active chat changes, which disposes the composer and its input. Switching back built a fresh composer whose only restore was the shared global draft. That is not tied to a chat, so the input came back empty or showed a stale older draft.

## Regression provenance

Unknown. I did not bisect: the cause is the view swap in `chatGroupView` together with the composer only restoring the shared global draft, not a single identified commit. Existing tests did not cover leaving and re-entering an untitled peer chat.

## Things to know

- Drafts are in memory only, like the per-chat view state, so they do not survive a window reload.
- Inline `#file` references typed in the prompt come back as plain text after the round trip. This is the same as the existing New Session draft, because `IChatDraft` only carries text and attachments.
- Performance and lifecycle (by inspection, not measured): one extra LRU cache (limit 100) holding a small object per saved chat, no hot-path work, no new listeners, and the draft is saved before the composer is disposed.

## How to test

1. Start a session in the Agents window.
2. Open a new chat in it (Cmd+T).
3. Type a prompt and do not send it.
4. Switch to the original chat, then back to the new chat. The prompt is still there.
5. Clear the input, switch away and back. It stays empty. Send a prompt, switch away and back. It is not restored.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run <every *.test.ts in src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser, src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/test/browser and src/vs/sessions/test/browser>`: 2301 passing, 2 pending.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter spec --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatInSessionWidget.test.ts --grep "draft|harness|peer chat"`: 25 passing. On the base product the same command has 6 failing (the prompt comes back empty or stale).
- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run eslint` and the hygiene check on the changed files, and `npm run valid-layers-check`: clean.
- Live in Code OSS with `--agents` on a build of the final head: the repro, the cleared-input case and the sent-prompt case pass. Before the fix, the same steps showed a stale draft.
- Not run live: the harness switch (needs a session with more than one chat harness) and two simultaneous unsent chats (Cmd+T reuses the single unsent peer chat). Both are covered by unit tests only.

## Review

Independent different-model review of the final head: no actionable findings. Earlier rounds found two issues in earlier versions, both fixed

state.description:
### What?

Net the collectible counts of an `AggregatedDataUpdate` in a new `AggregatedDataUpdate::optimize()`, called after the follower task's lock has been released.

### Why?

When an aggregating task gains (or loses) an upper, `AggregatedDataUpdate::from_task` builds an update from the task's own collectible counts plus `+1` for every positive aggregated collectible.

- **Cancelling entries:** a task that takes or drops the collectibles of its subgraph holds an own `-1` for each of them, so most of those entries cancel out. An earlier large `next build` investigation found one such update with 106,268 entries, of which only 4 had a nonzero net count.
- **Serialization:** in a large `next build`, ~6,000 uppers connect the same task. `from_task` runs while that follower's lock is held, so anything done per update while the lock is held serializes across all workers.
- **Why the earlier version didn't help:** a previous version of this PR netted inside `from_task`, still under the lock. It didn't improve emit time.

### How?

- **`from_task`:** back to its original form (own entries, then `+1` per positive aggregated entry). It keeps a `Vec::with_capacity` upper bound so the vector isn't reallocated while the task is locked.
- **`optimize()`:** sums the collectible entries per collectible, drops zero sums, and keeps the dirty container update unchanged. It reuses the vector's allocation.
- **Call sites:** `optimize()` is called right after the follower lock is dropped, at the sites that apply the update to uppers afterwards. These are the new-follower paths and the lost-follower paths. In the lost-follower paths, `invert()` also moved out of the lock, after `optimize()`. The `balance_edge` paths, which hold both locks through `apply`, are unchanged.
- **Semantics:** applying the optimized update (or its inversion) gives the same final counts in the upper, and the same set of collectibles whose presence changes. Intermediate flips within one update can be skipped. Result order is unspecified.

**Tests:**
- Unit tests for summing, cancellation, mixed counts, empty and single entries, and disjoint keys.
- Equivalence of final counts and presence changes for add and invert.
- The real `optimize().invert()` path on `CollectibleRef`s, including the dirty container update.
- An integration test that reads an operation which takes its child's collectibles, through several root uppers.

**Measurement** on canary `8521c6ae0` (`bench/nested-deps-app-router-many-pages`, 32 CPUs, cold untraced builds, 1 warm-up plus 4 interleaved rounds, median of the paired per-round changes vs canary):

| | change |
|---|---:|
| `turbopack-emit` | **−32.2%** (17.4 s → 11.9 s) |
| "Compiled in" | −11.2% |
| wall | −10.0% |

All three were faster in all 4 rounds. Output (`.next` file set) and issues are unchanged vs canary. This is one VM and 4 rounds, and the gain isn't broken down between the preallocation and moving work out of the lock.
state.title: turbo-tasks-backend: optimize aggregated updates outside of the lock

state.description:
### What?

Fixes Turbopack production and dev builds of App Router route handlers with `export const runtime = 'edge'` when `cacheHandlers` is configured. These builds currently fail with `edge-app-route.js: Expected ';', '}' or <eof>`. Webpack builds of the same app already work.

### Why?

The webpack loader and Turbopack both fill the `edgeCacheHandlersRegistration` injection point in the shared `edge-app-route.ts` template, which sits at statement position after `const edgeCacheHandlers = {}`.
- **webpack** emits assignment statements.
- **Turbopack** (`wrap_edge_route` in `crates/next-core/src/next_app/app_route_entry.rs`) emitted object-literal property fragments, which don't parse at statement position.

Existing coverage missed this because the edge fixture in `cache-handlers-upstream-wiring` only sets the singular `cacheHandler`. The loop that generates these entries never ran for an edge route.

### How?

- **Turbopack codegen:** Turbopack now emits one assignment per configured kind (`edgeCacheHandlers[<kind>] = cacheHandlerN`), matching the webpack loader. Each kind is still serialized with `serde_json`. The template and the webpack loader are unchanged, so both bundlers keep sharing the same template contract.
- **Regression fixture:** the new `edge-with-cache-handlers` fixture has two distinct handler modules (`default` and `custom`), one force-dynamic edge route and no edge page. It pins `cacheComponents: false` and `experimental.cachedNavigations: false`, because Cache Components is not supported on the edge runtime. Without both pins, the experimental CI shards would turn these flags on through env defaults, and the fixture would fail config validation or the build.
- **What the test checks:** the route reads the cache-handler registry that `EdgeRouteModuleWrapper` fills before invoking it, and returns each handler's marker. The test asserts both markers over HTTP, so it fails if the build breaks or if either kind is missing or swapped.
  - The suite has no gates. The fixture is a valid edge app in every shard, so the assertions run everywhere, including deploy.
- **Limits:** the test proves registration only. It doesn't exercise `'use cache'` hits or revalidation on edge.

### Verification

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| New test, `test-start-turbo`, unfixed published binary | ❌ fails with the parse error above, as expected |
| New test, `test-start-turbo`, local native build with the fix | ✅ passes |
| Existing edge test (`cacheComponents disabled, edge app router`), same fixed build | ✅ passes |
| New test, `test-start-webpack` | ✅ passes |
| New test, `test-dev-turbo` | ✅ passes |
| New test with the experimental (cache-components) CI env, `test-start-turbo` and `test-dev-turbo` | ✅ passes |
| Standalone repro (published canary.8 + fixed native binary), `next build` + `next start`, `GET` the edge route | ✅ builds and returns the expected JSON |

Not run locally: deploy-mode tests (they run in CI).

Fixes #99894

state.description:
### What?

Since #99702, `next dev` in a terminal prints server error code frames at the terminal width it had when it started. After the terminal is resized, frames wrap in a narrower terminal and stay cut short in a wider one, until the dev server restarts.

### Why?

The dev server's output is piped through the CLI now, so `process.stdout.columns` is undefined in the server and `codeFrameColumns()` falls back to `NEXT_PRIVATE_TERMINAL_COLUMNS`. The CLI sets that once, when it forks the server.

### How?

When the CLI pipes the server's output, it listens for `resize` on its own stdout and sends the new width to the server over the existing IPC channel. The server updates `NEXT_PRIVATE_TERMINAL_COLUMNS`, so the next code frame uses it.

I added a case to `test/e2e/agent-upgrade-terminal` that resizes the terminal from 80 to 50 columns and checks the code frame fits. It fails without the fix (the frame stays 80 wide) and passes with it.

Fixes #99915

### What?

Removes the`collector_is_not_re_executed_for_collectibles_it_has_not_read_yet` test from `turbo-tasks-backend`'s `collectibles_outdated_dependency.rs`. The other variant (`gated_collector_is_not_re_executed_for_collectibles_it_has_not_read_yet`) stays, and its behaviour is unchanged.

### Why?

The ungated test failed intermittently on canary with `take=…: executions after the input change` (left 2, right 1).

The cause is the race that the module's doc comment already described, not a backend bug. `State::set` invalidates its readers one by one. When the collector is invalidated before the emitter, it re-executes right away, its strongly consistent read of the still-clean source returns at once, and it reads the **old** collectibles. When the new collectibles arrive, it re-executes again, as it should. Instrumentation confirmed this in every failure: the extra execution read `count=200` but saw 5 collectibles. It reproduced in about 2 of 120 serial release runs under CPU load.

So "exactly one execution" can't be asserted without controlling that order.

I was not very confident about this test when it was added, so dropping it seems reasonable.
state.title: turbo-tasks-backend: remove racy ungated collectibles_outdated_dependency test

## What changed

Moving chats in the Agents window sessions list no longer shows anything in the list: no progress notice ("Moving 'X' into 'Y'...") and no result notice. state.description:
Follow-up to #344989, addressing its review comments and a Windows bug found while verifying it in Code OSS.

In Restricted Mode, the Markdown extension only copies pasted or dropped files to destinations inside the workspace. The check from #344989 had three problems:

- **Path casing:** it compared paths case-sensitively. On Windows, the workspace folder URI and the document URI can differ in drive letter case (`/C:/...` vs `/c:/...`), so every destination looked outside the workspace and no media file was copied at all. Containment now uses `vscode.workspace.getWorkspaceFolder`, which follows the case sensitivity of the workspace folder's file system.
- **Backslashes:** it treated `\` as a separator everywhere. On POSIX, `\` is a regular file name character, so `../../project\other/img.png` could pass the check while resolving outside the workspace. Destinations whose path below the workspace root contains `\` are now rejected on every platform.
- **Symbolic links and junctions:** the check was purely lexical. A folder inside the workspace that links to a folder outside it let a paste write outside. Each existing path segment below the root, including an existing target file, is now checked with `vscode.workspace.fs.stat`, and destinations that pass through a link are rejected.

When a configured destination is rejected, the file is copied next to the document instead; if that is rejected too, the file is not copied and the link points to the original file. Trusted workspaces are unchanged.

Tests: unit tests cover each case, and all `markdown-language-features` tests pass. Verified in Code OSS on Windows in a Restricted Mode workspace that sets `markdown.copyFiles.destination` to a path outside the workspace and contains a junction to an outside folder:

| Build | Paste into `README.md` | Paste into `docs/README.md` (junction) |
|---|---|---|
| #344989 + casing fix, without link check | – | ❌ file written outside the workspace |
| This PR | ✅ copied into the workspace, nothing written outside | ✅ not copied, nothing written outside |
state.title: Markdown: harden copy destination checks in Restricted Mode

state.description:
Follow-up to #344992. Addresses its review comment: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344992#discussion_r4414329927

### Problem
#344992 added `headSha` to the repair checkpoint that "When No Changes Were Made" merging (`ifUnchanged`) uses as its baseline. A checkpoint saved by an older build has no `headSha`. When a new repair started, it reused that checkpoint unchanged. Repairs can now push from any checkout. If the repair pushed from another worktree while the recorded checkout stayed clean at its old commit, `unchangedForMerge()` still passed, and the repaired head could be merged.

### Fix
When a repair reuses a checkpoint for the current merge generation that has no `headSha`, it now records the head this repair starts from. The checkpoint keeps its recorded chat, directory, and commit, so both the local baseline and the head must stay unchanged. Checkpoints that already have a `headSha` are not changed.

### Validation
- Added a regression test: restore an old-format checkpoint, repair from a chat without a checkout, then move the head while the recorded checkout stays clean. Without the fix the test fails and the repaired head is merged (`mutations: ['merge']`). With the fix, unchanged-only merging turns itself off and nothing is merged.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` with `githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration`, `artifactIntegrationServerTools`, `artifactServerTools`, `clientArtifactIntegrationEndpoint`, `sessionArtifactRemoval`, and `artifactIntegrations`: passed (232 tests).
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>`: passed.

state.description:
### What?

With Turbopack GC enabled, a task recorded in the persisted GC roots map now stays protected from collection until its TTL expires. Before, a recorded root was dropped from the map as soon as it became resident again. This also fixes pinned roots falling out of the roots map after their `Meta` was evicted.

### Why?

At refresh time, `gc_roots_refresh_and_age_out` dropped every *resident* root from the persisted roots map, assuming the pass's root scan would judge it. But the judgement would ~always judge them as dead.  A task becomes a root because it had only transient pins from a prior session, if we read it back to 'refresh' then it doens't have those transient pins and will always be collected.  On a warm `next dev` start, startup invalidation propagates through the aggregation graph and restores almost every prior root before anything requests it. So every root that hadn't been re-pinned yet was collected in the first GC pass, along with its whole exclusive subtree. The 3-day TTL never applied, and the next session had to recompute and re-persist everything.

On `bench/nested-deps-app-router-many-pages` with GC enabled:
- a warm session that idled before its first request collected about 4.3M tasks;
- the next session then ran as slowly as a cold one.

A related bug: the root scan can't see a task whose `Meta` has been evicted, so the refresh also dropped roots that were still pinned.

### How?

**Once a root, always a root, until it ages out.**

In theory a prior session root could gain a 'persistent pin' and then lose it which might mean we could collect it, this case is currently uncovered (and completely theoretical).

### Verification

- `cargo nextest run -p turbo-tasks-backend`: all tests pass.
- `cargo clippy -p turbo-tasks-backend --all-targets` and `cargo check -p turbo-tasks-backend --release` are clean.
- The end-to-end numbers above were measured with an earlier revision of this PR. In that run, an idle warm session collected 0 tasks and kept all 246 roots, and the next session ran at warm speed. I haven't re-run them on this revision. The cold-to-warm path they measured still keeps prior roots protected, and it now has fewer special cases.

Not covered here: retention cost (memory and cache size) and persisted-byte amplification.
state.title: turbo-tasks-backend: keep recorded GC roots until their TTL expires

### What?

`pnpm new-test` with the `unit` type now generates a flat `test/unit/<name>.test.ts` from a template, and nothing else.

### Why?

The `test` generator copied from `test/unit/test-template`, which didn't exist. As a result, `pnpm new-test --args false my-unit unit` created no test file at all, only `test/unit/my-unit/tsconfig.json` and `next-env.d.ts`. That layout also doesn't match how unit tests are organized: they are flat files in `test/unit/`. Since `AGENTS.md` requires generating tests with `pnpm new-test`, the unit type needs to work.

### How?

- Added a unit template, `test/unit/test-template/template.ts`. It's a minimal Jest test that passes as generated, with a pointer on how to import the code under test. A single `add` action renders it to `test/unit/{{ toFileName name }}.test.ts`.
  - Unlike the e2e templates, the file is deliberately not named `*.test.ts` and has no spaces in its path. Otherwise the unit runner would collect the template as a test, and on Windows `run-tests.js` spawns jest through a shell that splits the Handlebars filename at its spaces. That makes the `test unit windows` job pick up unrelated e2e suites and fail.
- The generator treats unit tests as a separate case:
  - `appDir` is ignored, so output never goes into `test/unit/app-dir/`.
  - The `tsconfig.json`/`next-env.d.ts` steps are skipped, since those only make sense for Next.js app fixtures.
  - The e2e, production and development generation is unchanged.
- Documented the unit invocation in `AGENTS.md`.

### Verification

- `pnpm new-test --args false my-unit unit` and `pnpm new-test --args true my-unit unit` both create only `test/unit/my-unit.test.ts`, and `pnpm jest test/unit/my-unit.test.ts` passes.
- `node run-tests.js --type unit --dry` and `pnpm jest --listTests test/unit/test-template` no longer pick up the template.
- `pnpm new-test --args true my-e2e e2e` and `pnpm new-test --args false my-prod production` still generate their fixtures, test file, `tsconfig.json` and `next-env.d.ts`.

## Summary

Installed plugin details currently lose marketplace source metadata that is available while browsing. This change preserves trustworthy GitHub repository provenance and surfaces it alongside the installed version and location.

- Projects repository metadata from configured plugin marketplaces into customization resources.
- Resolves installed provenance from direct marketplace metadata first, then the installation catalog association.
- Links canonical GitHub repositories from installed plugin details, targeting the validated ref and plugin path when available.
- Omits ambiguous, malformed, query-bearing, fragment-bearing, non-HTTPS, and non-GitHub repository values rather than inferring provenance.
- Refreshes only the repository row when asynchronous installation metadata arrives, preserving the user's current focus.
- Keeps the repository link shrink-wrapped so only its visible text is clickable, with truncation and custom hover behavior for constrained layouts.

Author and source-update timestamps are not exposed by the current authoritative marketplace contracts, so this change does not fabricate those fields. This PR does not add the author or last-updated metadata requested in #343866; that issue remains open and requires authoritative marketplace fields.

## How to Test

1. Open Chat Customizations and select an installed plugin from the GitHub Feed.

### Why?

The upgrade choice currently delays compilation. Run build work independently so compilation can continue while the user decides and be discarded when they choose Upgrade.

### How?

Interactive flow:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Child corks logs and keeps running"] -->|IPC: ready to prompt| B["Parent shows upgrade menu"]
    B -->|Skip| C["Close menu → IPC uncork → continue"]
    B -->|Upgrade| D["Close menu → stop child → upgrade"]
    A -->|IPC: fatal| E["Close menu → IPC reply → uncork → exit"]
```

Run interactive builds in a supervised child using the shared inherited-TTY output controls. Load config and initial route callbacks before corking, and let the parent own menu input. Skip releases held logs and continues the same child. Upgrade force-stops owned work before handing off. Fatal errors close the menu, uncork and retain the failure status; shutdown does not drain final worker or native output.

Keep noninteractive, inspector and preload builds on their existing path. Carry project environment and telemetry settings into the parent. Direct native diagnostics and output still in transit retain the shared TODOs. Real-terminal probes covered completion, failure, interruption and a stubbed upgrade handoff; existing loader integration passed in dev and production.

Closes NAR-943

Stacked on #337130 and depends on it. Only the last two commits, `copilot: expose the chat session id to language model request middleware` and `copilot: only trust the conversation id from the chat participant`, belong to this PR; the rest is the base PR.

## Summary

- The request middleware context from #337130 now carries `sessionId`, the chat session a request belongs to, so an extension can tag every request of one chat with the same id and let a gateway group them. A new chat gets a new id, and separate VS Code windows have separate sessions.
- `sessionId` is `undefined` for requests that are not made from a chat session, such as an extension calling `vscode.lm` directly.
- To make the id available to the provider, the proposed `chatProvider` API gains `ProvideLanguageModelChatResponseOptions.sessionId` (one d.ts field), and core forwards it along the chat path. That part needs API owner sign-off and can be reshaped independently of the rest.

## Why

Gateways such as LiteLLM attach requests to a session through a request header (`x-litellm-session-id`), which is what makes per-chat grouping and cost views work. With `customendpoint` the extension does not control the network request, so the only way to send such a header is through the middleware, and the middleware had no way to tell which chat a request came from. It could tell the vendor, model, URL and provider group apart, but two chats on the same model looked identical.

```ts
copilot.registerLanguageModelRequestMiddleware({
	selector: { vendors: ['customendpoint'] },
	provideRequestHeaders: async ({ sessionId }) =>
		sessionId ? { 'x-litellm-session-id': sessionId } : {},
});
```

## Validation

- Unit tests: the proxy test asserts the authenticated session id reaches the bridge request, and the agent host handler test asserts it reaches the language model request options. The custom endpoint provider test asserts the id reaches the middleware context, and a new test covers the fallback: the core option wins, `_conversationId` is used for requests initiated by this extension, and it is ignored for other initiators, for non-string values and when absent. The Azure Entra test and the registry fixture include the field.
- `vitest` for `src/extension/byok` and `src/extension/api`, `tsc --noEmit` for the Copilot extension, `npm run typecheck-client` at the repo root, `scripts/test.sh --grep "ByokLmProxyService|AgentHostByokLmHandler"`, `eslint` on changed files and `npm run hygiene` pass.

`formatRouteToRouteType` didn't handle dynamic segments with literal prefixes like `/@[username]`.

Two issues:
1. `isDynamicRoute` was called in strict mode, which only matches whole-segment brackets (`/[param]`). Prefixed segments like `/@[username]` were classified as static.
2. The segment mapper only checked `part.startsWith('[')`, so `@[username]` wasn't converted to a template literal.

Fixed by switching to non-strict `isDynamicRoute` mode and adding a `part.includes('[')` fallback branch that applies the same `SafeSlug`/`CatchAllSlug`/`OptionalCatchAllSlug` substitutions.

Both `typegen.ts` (dev server) and `next-types-plugin/index.ts` (webpack build) had identical copies of the function, so both are updated.

state.description:
## Problem

`Integrated Browser › preserves native page lifecycle across editors, popups, and restart` fails intermittently on Linux and macOS ([run 36120855518, job 108025747044](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36120855518/job/108025747044)):

```
locator.waitFor: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for locator('.tab').filter({ hasText: 'Browser Smoke Popup Child' }) to be visible
```

In the failure screenshot the popup page has rendered, but its tab still shows the host name (`127.0.0.1:41045`), which is the fallback label used when the model has no title.

## Root cause

This is the race described in #335987:

1. When a page opens a popup, the main process creates the child view and starts loading it immediately.
2. The renderer builds its `BrowserViewModel` from a state snapshot taken when the view was created, and only then subscribes to the view's dynamic IPC events.
3. Events fired before the subscription reaches main are lost. A fast page can commit and set its title in that gap, so the model keeps an empty title.

It happened in 4 Electron-Smoke jobs in the last ~15h of PR runs, 2 on Linux and 2 on macOS: 108025747044, 107951348615, 107885059240 and 108087350213.

## Fix

This PR takes the popup-reconciliation part of #335987, without its favicon-loader changes (those are in #336077) and without its per-event version numbers.

- **Platform:** a new `getNavigationState(id)` returns a lightweight `IBrowserViewNavigationState`: URL, title, back/forward, loading, favicon and errors. `IBrowserViewState` extends it. No screenshots or session data go over IPC.
- **Renderer model:** navigation, loading, title and favicon events are relayed through the model's own emitters, so the model's state is updated before consumers see an event. After subscribing, the model reads the navigation state once and applies only what changed. A snapshot that changes only the title fires a title event, not a navigation.
- **Seeded state:** URL, title and favicon from the snapshot are applied only once a navigation has committed. Until then the model keeps what it was seeded with: the requested URL, or a restored editor's title and favicon.

**Why no versions are needed:** the events and `getNavigationState` use the same ordered main-process channel. `ChannelServer` subscribes as soon as each `listen` request arrives and forwards events as they fire. It builds the snapshot synchronously and sends the reply on the microtask queue, so no Electron event can run in between. Any event the model received was therefore fired before the snapshot, and is already reflected in it. Anything fired later arrives after the reply.

#336077 is stacked on this PR. It scopes main's favicon state to the current page, so the favicon replayed here is the current page's too.

## Validation

- **Unit test:** a new test covers a popup that loaded before subscribing, a restored page that hasn't navigated yet, and a live event that arrived before the snapshot and isn't repeated. All 180 tests under `**/browserView/**` pass.
- **Smoke test:** the `Integrated Browser` suite passes 7/7, three times in a row.
- **Delay experiment:** I added a temporary 2s delay before the renderer creates the model for a new view. Without the fix, the test fails with the CI error. With the fix, the whole suite passes.
- **Static checks:** `npm run typecheck-client`, eslint and `build/hygiene.ts` pass on the changed files.

When this test runs alone (`-g "preserves native page lifecycle"`), its `afterEach` times out waiting for the restored page to close. That also happens on `origin/main`, so it isn't related to this change. The full suite, as CI runs it, passes.
state.title: browser: reconcile popup state missed before the renderer subscribes

## What?

Replace the `lzzzz` dependency with `lz4` across Turbopack persistence, its SST inspection tool, and the optional task-cache compressed-size diagnostics.

## Why?

The published `lzzzz` 2.0.0 bindings declare `LZ4F_freeCompressionContext` as returning no value, but the bundled liblz4 1.10.0 implementation returns `LZ4F_errorCode_t`. Linking `next-napi-bindings` for `wasm32-wasip1-threads` exposes this function-signature mismatch through Rust's `linker_messages` lint, while `cargo check` does not detect it.

#98629 proposed vendoring and patching `lzzzz` as a narrow workaround. Switching to `lz4` instead removes the incorrect FFI declaration without carrying a patched third-party crate: `lz4-sys` declares the function with the correct `LZ4FErrorCode` return type. The persistence code still uses the same liblz4 1.10.0 implementation and raw LZ4 block format, so existing persistence files remain readable and compressed output is byte-identical for the representative inputs tested.

## How?

Persistence continues to store independent raw LZ4 blocks without embedded size prefixes and supplies the expected output length during decompression.

The hot path calls liblz4 directly through `lz4::liblz4`. Compression reserves `Vec` spare capacity and reuses an aligned 16 KiB native compression state per worker thread: the first block calls `LZ4_compress_fast_extState`, and later blocks call `LZ4_compress_fast_extState_fastReset` at acceleration 1. This matches the state lifecycle that made `lzzzz` faster than `LZ4_compress_default`, which creates and initializes stack state on every call. Decompression calls `LZ4_decompress_safe` directly.

The three static-linking-only compression symbols omitted by `lz4-sys` are declared locally. All lengths and native return values are checked, each unsafe block documents its pointer, alignment, capacity, and initialization invariants, and the `Vec` length is set only after a successful in-bounds result.

Five interleaved release benchmark rounds measured the final fast-reset path against `lzzzz` and the prior direct-default implementation:

| Input | Final vs `lzzzz` | Final vs direct default | Compressed bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 KiB mixed | +0.04% | +4.64% | 4,959 |
| 12 KiB mixed | -0.26% | +4.51% | 7,370 |
| 64 KiB mixed | +0.42% | +4.68% | 38,052 |
| 1 MiB mixed | -1.30% | -0.52% | 617,207 |

The common 8–12 KiB blocks are within 0.3% of `lzzzz`; every compressed output is byte-identical. A same-executable comparison independently measured fast reset +3.50%/+3.55% at 8/12 KiB versus `LZ4_compress_default`, with parity at 1 MiB.

Release artifact size remains negligible: `sst_inspect` increases by 1,648 bytes (+0.13%), while `next-swc.linux-x64-gnu.node` decreases by 4,192 bytes (-0.0028%) relative to `lzzzz`. Fast-reset state adds 20,352 bytes (+0.0137%) to the `.node` file compared with the prior direct-default PR revision.

state.description:
### What?

With `cacheComponents` on, clicking a `<Link>` to a page that
1. waits for request-time data
2. then calls `redirect()`, `notFound()` or throws a “real” error

never navigates, and blocks the main thread at 100% until the next navigation

Reproducing requires a combination of:
- `cacheComponents` is on
- the page's shell has a hole with no `<Suspense>` or `loading.tsx` above it (which `instant = false` allows). The throw can be anywhere in that render, even inside its own `<Suspense>` further down
- the client already holds a prefetched shell for the page, this could be from a default `<Link>` prefetch or from a full page load of any URL of the same dynamic route

The same navigation works as a cold, full-page load, or with `cacheComponents: false`

There’s a minimal reproduction in https://github.com/controversial/next.js/tree/repro/blocking-route-redirect-stuck beyond what's in #97898 and #97534 

### Why?

This is caused by a loop between `useDeferredValue(rsc, prefetchRsc)` and React error recovery

1. The render for the link click uses the prefetched shell as the initial value of a `useDeferredValue`. There’s a hole where the request-time part (e.g. `await cookies()`) goes. If there’s no Suspense boundary above the hole, React can’t finish the render, so this render lane is left pending.
2. Once the navigation response arrives from the server, it contains a `redirect()` or `notFound()` or other error, which shakes out of `useDeferredValue` in the second render. There’s a `RedirectBoundary` that catches the error, but it doesn’t navigate until its `useEffect`, which won’t run until after the render is **committed**.
3. Before React commits an error boundary, it retries every pending lane. The click lane from (1) is one of them, and `useDeferredValue` hands back the shell again. The retry hits the same hole and suspends again.
4. Now there’s nothing for React to commit; React won’t commit an incomplete tree for a transition, and it marks the lanes as waiting for data, which for our redirecting shell hole the data never arrives. The retry from 3also schedules a new deferred render, going back to step 2. 

This repeats hundreds of times a second and nothing ever commits.


Before https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/36911, React used to leave this loop by itself, but now a retry that suspends at the shell no longer turns recovery off for that lane. 



### How?

A new helper, `getInitialRsc(cacheNode)` in `render-tree.ts` picks the initial value for `useDeferredValue`, instead of always returning the prefetched shell with the hole:
- If `rsc` is a `DeferredRsc` that is still `pending`, returns the prefetched shell with the hole
- otherwise returns `rsc` itself

This way, when we get to the sync retry that has the real data (3), it throws again instead of re-returning the shell that suspends again,  and React can commit the error boundary instead of looping. 

This is the same heuristic that’s used in `FreshnessPolicy.HistoryTraversal` for back/forward. 

The change is `+15 -10` source lines; the rest of the diff is comments and tests!

#### Alternatives considered

#98088 tried handling redirects in the router data layer, but that would still leave `notFound()` and thrown errors stuck the same way.

Skipping the shell in `layout-router.tsx` once the deferred data has settled would fix the plain cases but leave open:
- a server action that redirects to a prefetched blocking page that redirects again
- `redirect()` in a page that has a blocking `generateViewport` with `optimisticRouting: false`
- `prefetch={false}` link to another page of the same dynamic route, with `optimisticRouting: false`

i believe this is the more holistic fix

#### Small behavior change

- A segment that mounts after its data arrived now skips the shell, for example in `staleTimes.dynamic` reuse, seeded navigations, or a hidden Activity page coming back, saving one render pass and a
state.title: Fix navigations that never finish when a prefetched blocking route redirects or throws with Cache Components

state.description:
Fixes #133566.

`Repository.clean()` builds the discard command from the files the user picked:

```ts
const args = ['clean', '-f', '-q'];
...
this.exec([...args, '--', ...chunk])   // chunk = repo-relative paths
```

Git reads everything after `--` as a **pathspec**, not as a plain path, so a file whose name contains glob characters is expanded into a pattern. The Source Control view names a single file in the confirmation dialog, so the user confirms discarding one file and loses the rest of their untracked work.

Reproduced with git 2.47.3 in a repo containing `*`, `other.txt` and `third.md`:

```
$ git clean -f -q -- '*'            # current behaviour
$ ls
tracked.txt                          # other.txt and third.md are gone

$ git clean -f -q -- ':(literal)*'  # with the fix
$ ls
other.txt  third.md  tracked.txt     # only the file named `*` is gone
```

### Change

```diff
-			for (const chunk of splitInChunks(paths.map(p => this.sanitizeRelativePath(p)), MAX_CLI_LENGTH)) {
+			for (const chunk of splitInChunks(paths.map(p => `:(literal)${this.sanitizeRelativePath(p)}`), MAX_CLI_LENGTH)) {
```

`literal` pathspec magic only changes how git interprets the name. Paths with no glob characters behave exactly as before, and `splitInChunks()` measures the prefixed strings, so the `MAX_CLI_LENGTH` budget still holds.

I checked the absolute and nested cases too, since `clean()` passes absolute paths through `sanitizeRelativePath()`:

```
$ git clean -f -q -- ":(literal)$PWD/*"      # only the `*` file removed
$ git clean -f -q -- ':(literal)sub/*'       # only `sub/*` removed, `sub/keep.txt` kept
```

`:(literal)` has been supported since git 1.9.

### Tests

Two tests in `extensions/git/src/test/git.test.ts`, using the existing `recordingRepository()` pattern from `stackOperations.test.ts` to record the arguments handed to git:

- a single file named `*` must be passed as `:(literal)*`;
- a directory containing `*`, `file?.txt` and `[abc].md` must pass all three literally.

Both **fail on master** (which produces `'*'`, `'file?.txt'`, `'[abc].md'`) and pass with the change:

```
git
  Repository clean
    ✔ passes a file named like a glob as a literal pathspec
    ✔ passes every file of a directory as a literal pathspec
2 passing
```

`undo()` also runs `git clean -fd` without paths, but that one is *meant* to discard everything, so it is untouched.

I have not run the full integration suite (it needs a VS Code build); the two new tests were run directly against the compiled extension with a stub for the `vscode` module.
state.title: git: discard files by literal pathspec so a file named `*` cannot wipe the rest

Summary
This PR fixes a focus-related issue in the Explorer view. When focus is requested before the Explorer tree has been fully initialized, the code can call into the tree while it has no input set. That can result in invalid focus state or unexpected reveal behavior during early lifecycle and command-triggered transitions.

Problem
The Explorer view exposes a focus() method that immediately calls this.tree.domFocus(). However, there are scenarios where this method can be invoked before the tree is fully created or before it has received an input. In those cases, the tree is not ready to handle focus operations, and the code path can behave incorrectly.

Fix
This change adds a guard in ExplorerView.focus() to ensure:

the tree exists
the tree has an input before attempting to focus it
If the tree is not ready yet, the method falls back to the default super.focus() behavior instead of calling into an uninitialized tree.

The existing auto-reveal flow remains unchanged once the tree is initialized and ready to operate.

Files Changed
src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/views/explorerView.ts
Why This Matters
This avoids edge-case failures in the Explorer when focus is requested during view activation, restoration, or command-driven navigation. It keeps the Explorer behavior stable without changing the normal user-facing flow once the view is initialized.

Validation
Reviewed the focus implementation in the Explorer
Confirmed the guard prevents focus access before tree initialization
Confirmed normal focus and auto-reveal behavior still runs once the tree is ready

## Problem

The `vscode/askQuestions` tool renders a question carousel above the chat input. When options have descriptions (the common "clarifying questions with recommended defaults" pattern), each option row expands to two lines — the option title plus its explanation — and the card's outer `max-height` is `45vh`. The result: the card occupies most of the chat area, hiding the agent's prior output the user is still reading.

CLI agents like Codex present the same information more efficiently: the option list shows only the short titles, and the description appears as a hover tooltip on the row the user is actually looking at.

## Change

`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/media/chatQuestionCarousel.css` — two lines:

1. Hide the option-description span (`.chat-question-list-label-desc { display: none; }`).
2. Reduce the carousel container `max-height` from `min(420px, 45vh)` to `min(300px, 35vh)`.

That's the entire diff. The hover tooltip is already in place: `renderSingleSelect`/`renderMultiSelect` call `_hoverService.setupDelayedHover(listItem, { content: option.label, position: HoverPosition.BELOW })`, and `option.label` carries the full `"Title - Description"` string that the carousel splits into two DOM spans. So hiding the second span removes the inline duplication while preserving the complete text on hover.

## Behavior / Risk

- Option rows: title only (single line). Hover to see the description.
- Card max-height: ~300px / 35vh (was ~420px / 45vh). The content already scrolls inside the container, so no clipping is introduced — only the outer footprint is smaller.
- No changes to `AskQuestionsTool`, the data model, keyboard navigation, selection, submit, or draft persistence.
- Summary (post-submit) rendering is unchanged — it uses a different DOM tree (`renderSummary` / `renderConversationSummary`).

## Files

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/media/chatQuestionCarousel.css`

N/A (CSS-only UI change).

Fixes #336708

state.description:
## Bug

When a nested JSDoc `@property` has a type that does not parse (commonly a removed Closure `function(string)=` form), every nested `@property` after it is dropped from the typedef. Flat properties recover; nested ones do not. This worked in 6.0.3 and broke in 7.x after Closure `function(...)` types were removed and recovery became insufficient.

```js
/**
 * @typedef Sig
 * @property {object} Args
 * @property {string} Args.name
 * @property {function(string)=} Args.onSave
 * @property {((v: string) => void)=} Args.onCancel  // dropped today
 */
```

## Root cause

1. After an unsupported braced type like `{function(string)=}`, the parser treated `function` as a name and left `(...)` before `}`, so the property name never parsed.
2. In `parseChildParameterOrPropertyTag`, a child whose name did not match (including a missing name) aborted the nested type literal, so later matching nested tags were never collected.

## Fix

- `parseJSDocTypeExpressionCloseBrace`: if `}` is missing and the next token is `(`, skip leftovers (with brace/paren/bracket depth) through the closing `}` so the tag name still parses. Only start this recovery at `(` so unrelated missing-`}` cases keep the following name in place.
- In `parseChildParameterOrPropertyTag`, keep a missing-name property/parameter child nested instead of treating it as end-of-nesting.

## Tests

- Parser unit test `TestJSDocNestedPropertyRecoveryAfterBadType` asserting nested `Args.onCancel` is kept
- Compiler case `jsdocNestedPropertyRecoveryAfterBadType.ts` (+ baselines): only TS1005 on the Closure type; `check.ts` has 0 errors and `onCancel` remains in `keyof Sig['Args']`
- Updated `typedefTagWrapping` error/types baselines where `function(...)` typedef names are now recovered (typed as `Function`)

Fixes #65020

Related: similar open #65022

This PR was authored with assistance from Cursor Agent. I have read and understand the change and am prepared to discuss and revise it in review.

> [!TIP]
> Best reviewed commit by commit, hide whitespaces.

### Why?

The upgrade choice currently pauses dev startup. Let the server keep working while the user decides, and show held logs after the choice closes.

### How?

Interactive flow:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Child corks logs and keeps running"] -->|IPC: ready to prompt| B["Parent shows upgrade menu"]
    B -->|Skip| C["Close menu → IPC uncork → continue"]
    B -->|Upgrade| D["Close menu → stop child → upgrade"]
    A -->|IPC: fatal| E["Close menu → IPC reply → uncork → exit"]
```

After config and initial routes load, cork stdout/stderr in the existing dev child while keeping their inherited TTYs. Forward worker, Rust-handled loader and installation output into those same streams. The parent owns menu input; Skip closes the menu before IPC uncorks logs and forwards stdin. Upgrade force-stops owned work before starting the upgrade.

Fatal errors close the menu, uncork and retain the existing exit status. Restart automatically skips the choice. The safeguard also skips after ten seconds or about 10 MiB, checked once per second from cork. Shutdown waits for screen restoration, without draining workers, native callbacks or final writes.

Direct native diagnostics can interfere with the menu, and output still in transit can be lost at fatal exit. These limitations, Windows descendant cleanup and stdout/stderr ordering remain documented in source TODOs. Real-terminal probes covered background work, replay, failure, restart and interruption; the upgrade handoff was stubbed.

Closes NAR-943

## Summary

Fixes two native Go / TS7+ bugs:

### Fixes #64883 — Escaped `in` / `instanceof` after class field initializers

After a class field initializer, Unicode-escaped `\u{69}n` / `\u{69}nstanceof` on the next line were parsed as the `in` / `instanceof` operators (TS1260 + parse error). Per ECMA-262, keyword terminals cannot be expressed with Unicode escapes, so these should be IdentifierNames (matching V8).

**Change:** Treat escaped keywords as non-operators in the binary-operator path so ASI can end the previous expression and the escaped name can start a new class member. Unescaped `in` after a field initializer still continues the expression (test262 `fields-asi-5.js`).

### Fixes #64981 — `new (f() as T).C()` drops required parentheses on emit

`new (getPlugins() as any).Linker()` was emitted as `new getPlugins().Linker()` (i.e. `(new getPlugins()).Linker()`), causing a runtime TypeError.

**Change:** Parenthesize when the leftmost expression (stopping at calls, walking through parentheses / partially-emitted / assertion wrappers) is a `CallExpression`, matching classic TS6 emit: `new (getPlugins().Linker)()`.

## Test plan

- [x] Added Go unit tests in `parser_test.go`, `printer_test.go`, and `typeeraser_test.go`

  ### Summary

  Fixes an issue where remote agent host sessions fail to open or retry when extension startup or provider
  replacement cancels the in-flight chat load, and prevents infinite retry loops when rendering load failure
  banners.

  ### Root Cause

  1. Unhandled Cancellation: Remote agent host initialization triggers provider replacement, cancelling in-
  flight loads with a CancellationError that left the chat permanently failed without retrying.
  2. Autorun Feedback Loop: ChatGroupView previously executed view.setChat() in an autorun that also observed
  reactive surface and historyStatus changes. When a load failed, updating the failure banner re-ran the autorun,
  causing an infinite retry loop.
  3. Draft Loss: Text entered into the composer while loading or during cancellation retries was wiped out when
  the model attached or failed.
  4. Reselection Inaction: Reselecting an already-focused failed chat returned early because the view already
  held the resource, preventing manual recovery without switching away first.

  ### Changes

  • **chatView.ts**:
      • Added bounded automatic retry (at most 1 retry) for in-flight loads cancelled by provider replacement
      (isCancellationError).
      • Preserved drafts across loading, retries, late provider registrations, and manual retries via
      _inputBeforeLoad.
      • Allowed same-chat reselection to retry unbound, failed chats instead of returning early.
  • **chatGroupView.ts**:
      • Decoupled view.setChat() selection from reactive surface and historyStatus updates into separate
      autoruns to prevent retry feedback loops.
      • Exposed reopenActiveChat() for clean manual and same-chat retry dispatching.
  • **chatGroupsView.ts & sessionView.ts**:
      • Forwarded same-session and same-chat reselection down to reopenActiveChat().
      • Preserved hostVisible when reopening an already-open session.
  • **sessionsService.ts**:
      • Forwarded openSession() to SessionView on active session reselection to support single-click recovery of
      both active chats and chats in inactive split groups.
  • **sessionsManagementService.test.ts**:
      • Updated partial SessionView test doubles to implement openSession: () => {}.


  ### Testing

  Verified against current pushed commit 93d48ee0fac0e10d783b73f6d0ca47f4d091e611:

  • Unit & Integration Tests:
      • .\scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts: 121 passing
      • .\scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/chatGroupsView.test.ts: 115 passing
      • .\scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionView.test.ts: 17 passing
      • .\scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.
      ts: 277 passing (2 pending)
  • ESLint: Clean (0 errors, 0 warnings across all 9 modified files)
  • git diff --check: Clean (0 errors)
  • TypeScript Transpilation: Clean (10,283 client source files compiled without error)
