Fixes #336428.

Regular editor windows render the agent-host review confirmation but do not load the Agents-window commands it calls. The resulting command-not-found error is presented as “No unreviewed comments,” leaving Reveal Selected disabled.

This adds editor-only feedback commands backed by the owning host's annotations channel. They await hydration, preserve host URI mapping and peer-chat ownership, open/delete comments, and record the explicit reveal selection before approval. Registration is eager but host services are instantiated lazily. The renderer now distinguishes load failures from an empty result.

The selection path rejects empty or stale IDs before any writes and clears unchecked pending selections left by interrupted reveals. It preserves annotation entries and unrelated metadata. Dedicated Agents-window registrations remain separate; there are no imports from `vs/sessions`.

Validation:

- 16 focused Chromium browser tests pass, covering editor registration without host startup, WSL resource mapping, hydration/errors/disposal, selection and stale IDs, interrupted reveals, navigation/deletion, and renderer error/empty states.
- Targeted TypeScript diagnostics for all five changed files: zero.
- ESLint for all five changed files and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Tests used freshly transpiled changed modules with existing compiled test dependencies. A full build and live WSL UI verification were not performed. The full layer check was interrupted after WSL became unresponsive; it is not claimed as passing.

Reviewed before submission for host startup side effects, layer boundaries, subscription lifetime, stale selections, and accidental disclosure of unchecked comments.

## Public source patch

[Source patch, review notes and validation](https://github.com/RyanEwen/vscode-patches/blob/main/docs/patches/vscode-336430.md) · [Download source patch](https://github.com/RyanEwen/vscode-patches/raw/refs/heads/main/source-patches/vscode/336430.patch)

The source proposal targets the recorded upstream base. A separate [installed-bundle backport](https://github.com/RyanEwen/vscode-patches/blob/main/docs/fixes/agent-feedback-review-editor.md) is validated on Windows ARM64 VS Code 1.137.0 (`645f29cc31`), whose editor client also serves WSL windows. Bundle tests and deployment checks passed; live UI verification remains outstanding.

Automated review follow-up: `cc59706b4b6349329f7af86d159e654eb1864093` disposes each command's cancellation listeners and announces asynchronous loading failures through the shared ARIA helper. Both review threads are addressed. All 16 focused tests pass, targeted TypeScript diagnostics are zero, and targeted lint passes. The public source snapshot and validation notes are updated.

Cherry-pick commit: `c28ba4eb731fa5775c2d0b46d6bb68f9bbe8e266`.

- Apply managed sandbox allowed-host, read/write, and read-only lists instead of corresponding local grant lists, including explicitly empty managed lists.

3. Configure empty managed grant lists and managed `addCurrentWorkingDirectory: false`; verify local and automatically generated grants do not widen them.

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Android 16; Mobile; rv:158.0) Gecko/158.0 Firefox/158.0

### Steps to reproduce

I opened an official government PDF notice from the bodacc.fr portal using the built-in Firefox PDF viewer on both my Windows PC and Android phone.
Example direct link to a [bodacc.fr document](https://www.bodacc.fr/telechargements/COMMERCIALES/PDF/A/2026/20260185/1/BODACC_A_PDF_Unitaire_20260185_03078.pdf).
All the documents from this site have the same problem.

### Actual results

The text rendered as completely garbled, unrecognizable characters. Upon closer inspection, every single letter is experiencing a uniform +2 character mapping displacement (a Caesar Cipher glitch). For example, the word "BODACC" is being drawn on the screen canvas as "DOFCEE" (B→D, O→Q, D→F, etc.).
Toggling advanced internal config entries like pdfjs.disableFontFace or browser.display.use_document_fonts inside about:config does not resolve the issue. The exact same text layer reads perfectly fine when downloaded and opened in Chromium-based browsers or desktop viewers like Adobe Acrobat.

### Expected results

The browser's PDF.js library should have correctly decoded the document's internal CID-keyed / OpenType font maps and displayed the regular, legible text layer without shifting the character indices.

state.description:
Paste and Go (`pasteAndGo.label` in `browser.properties`, added by `UrlbarInputBase.mjs` `_initPasteAndGo` and its copy in `SmartbarInput.mjs`) has no accesskey; G, S and O are free in the textbox context menu. Add search engine (`search-one-offs-add-engine-menu`) has none; G, I and N are free. The per-page "Add <engine>" items (`AddSearchEngineHelper`, up to three inline) are generated from data and have no accesskey. Paste & Search in the search bar's context menu has none either.

Bug 2073853 adds an automation check: a menupopup or panel-list that opens with two visible items sharing an accesskey, or with items lacking one beside items that have one, logs an `AccessKeyConflictError` and fails the running browser-chrome test. This menu carries an `accesskey-conflicts-bug` attribute naming this bug so the check skips it. The fix picks unique letters for static items (a message whose accesskey changes gets a new Fluent id; no migration recipe) and removes the attribute in the same patch so the check guards the menu from then on. Items generated from data can't be given accesskeys, so a menu that mixes them with static items either drops the static items' accesskeys or moves the generated items into a submenu. Conflicts are per visible menu instance, so a letter has to be free among the items that can show together, not merely in the Fluent file.
state.summary: Paste and Go, Add search engine and Paste & Search in the address bar context menu have no accesskey

Currently, we do not offer context menus for date and grouped site entries (available when _Site_ or _Date and Site_ sorting is selected) in the History sidebar.  Attached are the current context menus for date and grouped site in the old sidebar. 

We would like to start offering it, with the following options:

**Date**
Open All in Tabs (followed by a separator)
Delete

**Site**
Open All in Tabs (followed by a separator)
Delete
Clear All Data for Website (formerly known as Forget about this site...) 

In both cases, _Copy_ receives a very very modest usage, so unless we can implement it very quickly, I think we should drop its support.

state.description:
STR:
1. Close a tab.
2. Create a tab group with two tabs and close the group.
3. In History > Recently Closed Tabs, open the group's submenu and reopen each of its two tabs.
4. Press Ctrl+Shift+T.

Expected: the tab from step 1 reopens.
Actual: nothing reopens, and `undoCloseTabGroup` throws "Tab group not found in source".

When the last tab leaves a closed group, `#cleanupOrphanedClosedGroups` drops the group but leaves the window's `lastClosedTabGroupId` pointing at it, so `SessionWindowUI.undoCloseTab` tries to reopen the group. Closing and reopening the window keeps the stale ID, because the restored window copies `lastClosedTabGroupId` from its closed state.
state.summary: Reopen Closed Tab fails after reopening a closed tab group's tabs one at a time

state.description:
Follow-up to bug 2069796.

`selectIcons()` in `FaviconLoader.sys.mjs` picks, besides the tab icon, a rich icon that is stored in Places for surfaces showing large icons (e.g. New Tab). The candidates are the icons the page declared as rich (`apple-touch-icon`, `fluid-icon`) plus `rel="icon"` icons whose declared width is at least `FAVICON_RICH_ICON_MIN_WIDTH` (96), and the one with the largest declared width wins. The declared width is computed by `extractIconSize()`.

This has a few problems:

1. `extractIconSize()` only looks at the first token of `sizes`. An ICO correctly declaring all its frames, e.g. `sizes="16x16 32x32 48x48 256x256"`, gets a width of 16 and is never a candidate, while the same ICO declared as `sizes="256x256"` is. The width should be the largest of the declared sizes.

2. `rel="icon"` icons without `sizes`, or with `sizes="any"` (common for SVG), get a width of -1 and are never candidates, even if they are actually large (e.g. a 512px PNG, or a scalable SVG). Declared rich icons without `sizes` are instead accepted with the same -1 width.

3. On equal declared widths the first declared icon wins, while for the tab icon selection the last declared one wins ("When multiple icons are in the same set, the latest wins").

Expected: the rich icon pick considers all declared sizes, handles scalable and unsized icons consistently, and uses the same tie-breaking as the tab icon selection.
state.summary: Large page icons are not picked as rich icon when `sizes` lists several sizes or is missing

state.description:
`NewTabPagePreloading` observes none of the three prefs its own `enabled` getter reads, so it never discards a preload those prefs have invalidated. `about:newtab` resolves to `chrome://browser/content/blanktab.html` while `browser.newtabpage.enabled` is false, and `AboutNewTabRedirector` reads that pref when it opens the channel rather than when `loadURI` is called, so a preload issued before the pref went false comes back blank. While the pref stays false `getPreloadedBrowser` early-returns, so the blank browser is neither consumed nor dropped; when the pref goes back to true it is served to the next new tab.

The cost is one blank new tab page, and reloading it fixes it. The pref is a visible setting -- New Tabs, in about:preferences#home -- and is written by Sync, so nothing about this needs a test harness, but in the browser the flip has to land inside the load window. In CI it is reliable: `browser_enabled_newtabpage.js` flips the pref while a preload is in flight and leaves the blank browser for the next test in the newtab browser-chrome manifest to consume, which is one cause of bug 1970996.

`defineLazyPreferenceGetter` takes an `onUpdate` callback, so discard `preloadedBrowser` across `BrowserWindowTracker.orderedWindows` when an input changes, with the ungated take factored out of `getPreloadedBrowser`, which today early-returns exactly when the discard is needed. Enterprise policy cannot reach this: it locks the pref before any window exists.
state.summary: Blank new tab page after browser.newtabpage.enabled is turned off and back on

state.description:
`urlbar-result-menu-show-less-frequently2`, `urlbar-result-menu-report-inaccurate-location2`, `urlbar-result-menu-dont-show-weather-suggestions2` and `urlbar-result-menu-dont-show-market2` in `browser.ftl`, and `firefox-suggest-command-dont-show-addons2`, `firefox-suggest-command-dont-show-mdn2`, `urlbar-result-menu-dont-show-flight-status2` and `urlbar-result-menu-dont-show-sports2` in `enUS-searchFeatures.ftl` define no `.accesskey`, while Dismiss (D), Manage (M), Learn more (L), Remove from history (R) and Get help (H) do. Result menu commands are `{name, l10n}` objects, so the key comes from Fluent alone. The fixture in `browser_splitbutton.js` reuses `urlbar-result-menu-dismiss-suggestion2` for two and three entries of one split button, which the shared result panel-list renders together; it needs distinct labels.

Bug 2073853 adds an automation check: a menupopup or panel-list that opens with two visible items sharing an accesskey, or with items lacking one beside items that have one, logs an `AccessKeyConflictError` and fails the running browser-chrome test. This menu carries an `accesskey-conflicts-bug` attribute naming this bug so the check skips it. The fix picks unique letters for static items (a message whose accesskey changes gets a new Fluent id; no migration recipe) and removes the attribute in the same patch so the check guards the menu from then on. Items generated from data can't be given accesskeys, so a menu that mixes them with static items either drops the static items' accesskeys or moves the generated items into a submenu. Conflicts are per visible menu instance, so a letter has to be free among the items that can show together, not merely in the Fluent file.
state.summary: Quick suggest commands in the address bar result menu have no accesskey

Bug 2049387 moved the New Tab dialogs onto the new `--dialog-*` design tokens (D310155). Those tokens are defined in toolkit (D310151), so they first ship in Firefox 160. When the New Tab train-hop is applied to Firefox 158 or 159, the tokens are undefined and every declaration that uses them resets to its initial value.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Apply the current New Tab train-hop to Firefox 158 or 159 and restart.
2. Open a new tab and open one of the dialogs below.

Actual result:
- The "Delete from history" confirmation (`.confirmation-dialog`) and the "Report" form (`.report-content-form`) have no background, border or shadow, so the page shows through them.
- The Top Sites edit and topic selection modals (`.modalOverlayOuter`) and the Weather opt-in dialog lose their border, corner radius and shadow.

Expected result:
The dialogs look as they did before bug 2049387.

Each `--dialog-*` reference in `_ConfirmDialog.scss`, `ReportContent.scss`, `_ModalOverlay.scss` and `_Weather.scss` needs a fallback to the value it replaced, marked `@backward-compat { version 160 }`. The D310155 review suggested these fallbacks.
state.summary: Some New Tab dialogs are transparent when the train-hop is applied to Firefox 158 and 159

state.description:
Behind the `widgets-ad-large` page layout variant, the widgets row shows a sponsored card in the last slot of the first row. The card's position in the document does not match where it paints, so keyboard and screen reader users reach it before the widgets that appear ahead of it.

Affected from three card columns up, and from two when small widgets sit ahead of the card. One card column always matches.

The visual slot comes from a `grid-column` per container width, while the document position is fixed. CSS `order` moves boxes but not tab order, so the fix is to make the document position follow the window width. Note that `columns - 1` is not a correct index while small widgets can share a slot.

Accessibility triaged this as S3 and confirmed it can ride a follow up, as long as the card stays reachable and activatable. It is: the card is a plain link, the context menu beside it is a labelled button, and nothing removes the cell from the tab order or the accessibility tree.

The variant lands in bug 2071407 and the card in bug 2071410.
state.summary: Keyboard focus reaches the Widgets row sponsored card out of order

`TabNotesController` removes its window listeners (`CanonicalURL:Identified`, `TabNote:*`, the tabs progress listener) only after `TabNotes.deinit()` has closed the database. If `browser.tabs.notes.enabled` is turned back on before the close finishes, the re-enable path adds the listeners first and the stale disable path then removes them, so tab notes stay broken in every window until the next toggle.

On enable and at startup, the listeners are added only after the database has opened, so canonical URLs reported in the meantime are dropped until the later `CanonicalURL:Detect` sweep.

This causes intermittent failures in [browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_note_preview.js](https://tests.firefox.dev/test.html?test=browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_note_preview.js) and [browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_preview.js](https://tests.firefox.dev/test.html?test=browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_preview.js) on linux standalone ("Found an unexpected tab at the end of test run").

Fix: add and remove the window listeners without waiting for the database (`TabNotes` initializes itself lazily). `TabNotes.deinit` forgets its init immediately and also closes a connection whose init is still in flight, and a new init waits for the pending close.
state.summary: Tab notes stop working after browser.tabs.notes.enabled is toggled off and quickly back on

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Firefox 158.0 (64-bit) on macOS while signed in to a Mozilla account.
2. Enable the native Firefox VPN (IP Protection) feature.
3. Use the VPN for some time. The connection worked intermittently.
4. Disable the VPN through the Firefox interface.
5. Attempt to open any website in Firefox.

**Troubleshooting performed:**
- Changed `network.proxy.type` from 5 to 0 – no improvement.
- Changed `network.trr.mode` from 0 to 5 – no improvement.
- Started Firefox in Troubleshoot Mode – websites loaded normally.
- Set `browser.ipProtection.enabled` to `false` in `about:config` – normal browsing was immediately restored.

### Actual results

After disabling the built-in VPN, Firefox stopped loading all websites. Pages remained in a continuous loading state without displaying content or an error message.

The internet connection itself was working correctly, and other browsers on the same computer had no connectivity issues.

The problem persisted after restarting Firefox and adjusting proxy and DNS settings.

Normal browsing was only restored after completely disabling the built-in VPN feature by setting `browser.ipProtection.enabled` to `false`.

### Expected results

After disabling the built-in Firefox VPN through the user interface, Firefox should immediately resume normal browsing using the regular internet connection.

All websites should load normally without requiring changes to advanced configuration settings (`about:config`) or restarting Firefox.

The VPN feature should be capable of being enabled and disabled without affecting normal browser connectivity.
state.summary: Firefox 158.0 on macOS stops loading all websites after disabling built-in VPN (IP Protection)

state.description:
The invariant "a tab state may only reference tab groups defined in its own
window" is maintained by the writer and is not checked anywhere on the read side.
Only the writer keeps it true; every reader assumes it.

Where state enters without validation:
- SessionFile parses the state as JSON and checks the version, nothing else.
- session.schema.json defines no relationship between a tab's groupId and the
  window's groups; the window definition does not even require groups.
- the raw state can be rewritten by sessionstore-state-read observers before it is
  parsed and reused.
- SessionMigration reads another profile's file and reproduces the same shape.

Readers that assume the invariant (four, in different code paths):
- SessionStore.sys.mjs:7957 - #prepDataForDeferredRestore
- SessionMigration.sys.mjs:58 - profile migration
- Tabbrowser.sys.mjs:5204 - createTabsForSessionRestore (window restore)
- SessionStore.sys.mjs:2470 - #saveOpenTabGroupsOnClose (window close)

Consequences when a reference does not resolve:
- Window restore aborts at that tab and every later tab of the window is dropped.
  The fallback for this one path is bug 2080608 / D332744.
- In a deferred session the failure escalates instead of aborting: #initSession
  returns the unprepared state and #initializeWindow restores from it, so a
  DEFER_SESSION launch (automatic restore switched off) becomes a full automatic
  restore of every window, cookies included.

Proposed direction: normalize unresolvable groupIds once where the state enters,
the way #migrateSplitViewIds already normalizes invalid splitViewIds. That covers
all four readers instead of the single path the fallback patches.

On prevalence: no naturally occurring case is known. The fallback in bug 2080608
was driven by a malformed input produced by a third-party session-file rewriter, so
this bug is about the read side being unable to detect or repair an inconsistent
state from any source, not about an observed Firefox write path.
state.summary: Session restore trusts tab group references without validating them on load

state.description:
When Firefox starts, `SessionStartup` reads the saved session and, once the browser is idle, counts the pinned tabs in it to record the `browser.engagement.max_concurrent_tab_pinned_count` metric. The same callback also counts saved tab groups for a debug log message, using `initialState.savedGroups.length`, which was added in bug 1973441. Session files written by Firefox 132 and earlier have no `savedGroups` property (it was introduced in bug 1908423), so for those profiles - for example someone upgrading from ESR 128 - that line throws a TypeError, and the pinned-tab metric is never recorded.

The rest of Session Restore already treats `savedGroups` as optional when reading saved state; SessionStore, for example, uses `state?.savedGroups ?? []`. Change [this line](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/browser/components/sessionstore/SessionStartup.sys.mjs#261
) to do the same:

```
  let savedGroupsCount = initialState.savedGroups?.length ?? 0;
```
Please also add an xpcshell test in browser/components/sessionstore/test/unit/ (and list it in xpcshell.toml there). `test_startup_session_async.js` and the `afterSessionStartupInitialization` helper in head.js show how to start `SessionStartup` against a session file. The new test should:

- call Services.fog.initializeFOG()
- write a session file to sessionstore.jsonlz4 in the profile, with IOUtils.writeJSON and `{ compress: true }`, containing one window with one pinned tab and no `savedGroups` property
- start `SessionStartup` and wait for it to initialize
- use `TestUtils.waitForCondition` to wait until `Glean.browserEngagement.maxConcurrentTabPinnedCount.testGetValue()` is 1

Without the fix the test times out after a few seconds; with it, it passes.

To verify the fix:

./mach test browser/components/sessionstore/test/unit/
./mach lint browser/components/sessionstore/

https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/contributing/stack_quickref.html

The bug will get automatically assigned to you when you submit a patch. Please comment here if you are actively working on it so people don't cross the streams.

state.description:
Steps to reproduce:

1. In Settings, turn on "Open previous windows and tabs".
2. Open two windows. In window A, open some tabs. In one of them, open https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Sandbox&action=edit and type some text. Do not save.
3. In window A, select all tabs: click the first tab, then Shift+click the last tab.
4. Right-click a selected tab and choose "Close Tabs".
5. At the prompt "This page is asking you to confirm that you want to leave", click "Stay on page". Window A stays open with all its tabs.
6. Quit Firefox (menu > Quit). If the page prompts again, choose "Leave page".
7. Start Firefox.

Actual results:

- Window A is not restored. It is in History > Recently Closed Windows, and Ctrl+Shift+N reopens it.
- If window A is the only window, Firefox opens one blank tab. The old tabs are in the list of recently closed tabs, and only `browser.sessionstore.max_tabs_undo` of them (default 25) are kept. The other tabs are lost. "Restore Previous Session" is not available.

Expected results:

Window A is restored with all its tabs, because it was open when Firefox quit.

Notes:

Windows or Linux only -- this does not repro on MacOS.

Cause:

- `closeWindow()` in `toolkit/content/globalOverlay.js` calls `SessionStore.maybeDontRestoreTabs(window)` before `window.close()`, and does not check whether the window really closed. It does this only when the platform is not macOS.
- `removeMultiSelectedTabs()` calls `Tabbrowser.removeTabs()`. When the tabs to remove are all the tabs of the window and `browser.tabs.closeWindowWithLastTab` is true, `removeTabs()` calls `closeWindow(true, ...)` before any `beforeunload` check. The `beforeunload` prompt comes later, during `window.close()`. When the user cancels it, the window stays open with `_maybeDontRestoreTabs` set.
- Nothing clears `_maybeDontRestoreTabs` while the window stays open, so it is saved to the session file.
- At the next automatic restore, `#removeExplicitlyClosedTabs()` in `SessionStore.sys.mjs` moves a window with this flag to `_closedWindows`. If it is the only window, it moves all its tabs to `_closedTabs` instead.

Notes:

- macOS is not affected, because `closeWindow()` does not set the flag there.
- Closing only the last tab of a window is not affected: there, `beforeunload` runs before `closeWindow()`. Deleting a tab group that holds all tabs of a window is not affected either: `removeTabGroup()` runs `beforeunload` first and does not close the window.
- This can explain some reports in bug 1330633. Bug 2073206 comment 0 describes the same result ("Ctrl+Shift+N restores the window with all its tabs").

Possible fix: set `_maybeDontRestoreTabs` only after the window has really closed, or clear it when the close is cancelled.

state.description:
`SidebarController.registerPrefSidebar` installs pref observers that hide the sidebar when the panel's pref is turned off. These observers outlive the window. Turning such a pref off after closing a window that had that panel open calls `hide()` on the closed window, which throws because its state was cleared on uninit:

```
TypeError: can't access property "arm", this._splitterAriaUpdateTask is null
```

User impact: only an error in the browser console, e.g. when one of these prefs is changed by Nimbus.

On CI it was logged 2,396 times in 1,465 jobs, from 2 tests, out of the 31,690 mozilla-central mochitest jobs of 2026-10-15 in the errors dashboard (https://tests.firefox.dev/errors.html?kind=mochitest#date=2026-10-15). `browser_opentabs_sidebar.js` and `browser_chat_sidebar.js`, which reset these prefs after closing windows.

Created attachment 9649553
Demonstration video with Firefox 156's vertical tabs sidebar - proportions problem with many pinned tabs

This is kind of the opposite (but complementary) issue to bug #2033306.

When you have tons of pinned tabs, and you collapse the sidebar into a thin column, the pinned tabs auto-position the draggable separator to the maximum required to fit them all, regardless of how many normal tabs you have open, making it a scrollfest where it is nearly impossible to see normal tabs.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable vertical tabs mode
2. Open a ton of normal tabs (let's say, a hundred)
3. Pin a lot of tabs (let's say 15 to 30 pinned tabs)
4. Toggle the vertical tabs sidebar's compact mode, by using the toolbar's "Collapse sidebar" button or using `Alt+Ctrl+Z`

## Actual Results

See attached video: the numerous pinned tabs expand to fill nearly the entire height of the collapsed sidebar, leaving very little manoeuvering room for normal tabs.

## Expected results

I think there should be some sort of upper limit / proportionality rule for the auto-positioning of the movable separator divider widget when toggling to collapsed mode, when there are enough "normal" tabs (vs pinned tabs) to warrant it. Or maybe it should maintain the same ratio as what the user had set in expanded mode (again, "when there are enough normal tabs to fill the space below").
state.summary: When toggling sidebar's collapsed mode, pinned vertical tabs have no height limitation for the divider separating them from normal tabs

state.description:
## Steps to reproduce
1. Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME 46 Wayland), IBus 1.5.29 with ibus-hangul 1.5.5 (Korean 2-set layout), `GTK_IM_MODULE=ibus`.
2. In `about:config` set:
   - `browser.urlbar.keepPanelOpenDuringImeComposition = true`
   - `browser.urlbar.clipboard.featureGate = true`
3. Put some text on the clipboard.
4. Focus the address bar (Ctrl+L), switch to Hangul and type `rkskek` (= 가나다).

## Actual results
The address bar shows **가나나다**. The second syllable is committed twice. With 강아지 (`rkddkwl`) the result is 강ㅇ아지.
After typing only 가나, the field looks like 가나, but it actually holds a committed 나 plus an invisible composing 나. Pressing Backspace gives 가나ㄴ.
It is intermittent, but reproduces most of the time.

## Expected results
가나다

## Notes
- It does not reproduce with only one of the two prefs enabled (Firefox defaults are both `false`).
- Zen Browser enables both prefs by default, so Zen users on Linux with IBus hit this: https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/15983
- Only the 2nd syllable and only Korean (composition) input are affected.

## Analysis
When ㅏ is typed after 간, IBus emits: preedit `""` → commit `가` → preedit `나`. While the preedit is `""`, the urlbar value is momentarily **empty**. With `keepPanelOpenDuringImeComposition = true` a query starts during composition. Because `searchString` is empty, `UrlbarProviderClipboard.isActive()` calls `controller.browserWindow.readFromClipboard()` **synchronously**.

`MOZ_LOG=IMEHandler:5,IMEStateManager:5` shows that while `DispatchCompositionEvent(eCompositionChange "")` is still on the stack, `OnCommitCompositionNative("가")` and `OnStartCompositionNative`/`OnChangeCompositionNative("나")` run re-entrantly. The `preedit-end` belonging to the cleared preedit is delivered afterwards. `IMContextWrapper` then dispatches `eCompositionCommitAsIs` for `나`, and IBus commits `나` again.

With default prefs, the same input produces the normal order: preedit `""` → `OnEndCompositionNative` → commit → new composition.

My inference, not verified in the C++ code: the synchronous clipboard read waits for data by iterating the GTK main loop, which dispatches the pending IBus D-Bus signals in the middle of composition event handling.

## Suggested fix
In `UrlbarProviderClipboard.isActive()`, don't read the clipboard while the urlbar editor is composing. More generally, avoid a synchronous clipboard read in a path that runs on input events.
state.summary: Korean IME syllable committed twice in the address bar when the clipboard suggestion reads the clipboard during composition (keepPanelOpenDuringImeComposition + clipboard.featureGate, GTK/IBus)

state.description:
**[Notes]:**
Multiple distinct HNT Card Stack interactions emit telemetry-identical pings. The following actions all generate the same telemetry (event=CLICK, event_source=CLICK_BUTTON, message_id=HNT_CARD_STACK):

- Import card: CTA and dismiss
- Import dialog: Import and Cancel
- Mobile card: CTA and dismiss
- Default Browser card: CTA and dismiss

As a result, the telemetry does not appear to provide enough context to identify which card generated the event or whether the user performed a primary action, dismissed a card, confirmed an import, or cancelled it. This makes card-level engagement and conversion analysis difficult.

**[Affected versions]:**
- Firefox Nightly 160.0a1 (Build ID: 20261019215902)

**[Affected Platforms]:**
- Windows 11 x64
- macOS 15.7.4
- Ubuntu 24.04 x64

**[Prerequisites]:**
- Have the latest Firefox Nightly 160.0a1 en-* build installed/extracted and opened.
- Have the Nimbus DevTools [extension](https://github.com/mozilla-extensions/nimbus-devtools/releases/download/release%2Fv1.0.0/nimbus-devtools.xpi) installed.

**[Steps to reproduce]:**
1. Open the devTools extension and click on the Feature Configuration Enrollment.
2. Select fxms-message-15 from the drop-down, paste in the contents of this [GitHub gist](https://gist.github.com/AllegroFox/8e41621f375dbafeb251b2507038d494), and click Enroll.
3. Change the drop-down to newtabTrainhop, enter the contents of this [gist](https://gist.github.com/nathan-barrett/9b99c6cd1bc80f735108cb5e4aefe0a4), and click Enroll.
4. Restart the browser and set up Glean using the testing steps from here: [TestRail](https://mozilla.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/7731733&group_by=cases_archived:section_id&group_order=asc&display=compact&group_id=753191).
5. Open a new tab to display the card stack.
6. Complete the new tab cards by clicking the primary button of each card until dismissed from the page.
7. Open the browser with a new profile following the prerequisites.
8. Repeat steps 1-5.
9. Complete the new tab cards by clicking the secondary (Dismiss) button of each card until all of them are dismissed from the page.
10. Navigate to the [Glean Debug Viewer](https://debug-ping-preview.firebaseapp.com/) and look for your debug ID.
11. Select your debug ID and open the “messaging-system” pings.
12. Observe the contents of the pings.

**[Expected result]:**
- The pings include profile age information, the cards shown, their order data, and a specific "messaging_system.event" value, depending on the action.

**[Actual result]:**
- The pings do not include profile age information, the cards shown, their order data, or their specific actions.

**[Additional Notes]:**
- Here are telemetry examples for 2 different actions from 2 cards: 
-> [CTA mobile card](https://debug-ping-preview.firebaseapp.com/pings/CF-1-DESKTOP/f12d1742-9900-46f6-8b53-756970b83e01)
-> [Dismiss default card](https://debug-ping-preview.firebaseapp.com/pings/CF-1-DESKTOP/6dbcc251-4d00-4f2c-9358-72772dc1c65e)
state.summary: The HNT_CARD_STACK telemetry does not provide enough context to distinguish user interactions

state.description:
Steps to reproduce the problem:
1. View some local PDF (using a file:// URI) in a fresh Firefox Nightly profile.
2. Move the actual PDF file out from under yourself (e.g. rename it, or move it, or delete it, or remove the USB flash drive where it was loaded from, etc.)  Note that Firefox's presentation of the PDF is unaffected; hooray.
3. Click the "See PDF features" link in the info-bar that appears at the top of Firefox.
4. Click the "Back" button (either on the toolbar or in-content, doesn't matter)

What is the expected behavior?
I should still be able to view the PDF.  (since I was viewing it just fine after step 2, and then I just idly accepted Firefox's invitation to see PDF features.)

What went wrong?
Firefox takes me to a "File not found" page.

The main issue here is that this "See PDF features" link is **navigating the same tab**.

Suggested fix: **We should have it instead open in a new tab** - that would avoid this issue, I think.  (And there's precedent for doing that elsewhere, e.g. `about:preferences#privacy` has has several "Learn more" links that open in new tabs.)

Note: This might only be a problem for local files.  I tried to reproduce it with a web-hosted PDF (and in step 2, I disconnected from the network), but in that case the file still loaded OK when I navigated back to it, presumably because we kept it in BFCache and/or other forms of local cache.  But maybe file:// URIs are special and bypass the relevant caches because they're already local and hence don't generally need to be cached.
state.summary: PDF Viewer "See PDF Features" infobar link navigates user away from the PDF that they're viewing, potentially unable to return (at least for local PDFs that have disappeared in the meantime)

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:157.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/157.0

### Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open a New Tab page in Firefox.
2. Click the "Customize" button at the bottom right.
3. Toggle the "Weather" widget switch to ON under the Widgets section.
4. Observe the New Tab page layout.

### Expected Results:
The Weather widget should render properly alongside other enabled widgets (such as Clock, Timer, or Checklist).

### Actual Results:
The Weather widget does not display on the New Tab page at all, even though the toggle switch in the Customize settings indicates that it is turned ON.

### Key Technical Observation:
- Inspecting the layout reveals an invisible/blank DOM element present in the widget grid (occupying space/bounds). 
- This confirms the Weather widget element is being instantiated in the layout, but fails to render its UI/content, likely due to a silent failure in the geolocation service or API fetch step.

### Additional Notes:
- Verified that `browser.newtabpage.activity-stream.system.showWeather` is set to `true` in `about:config`.
- Attempting to set or change default location settings in Windows Location Permissions causes the Windows Settings app to crash/close unexpectedly, preventing Firefox from fetching OS-level geolocation data.
- The UI fails silently without presenting any placeholder or fallback prompt for manual location input when location services fail.
state.summary: Weather widget is missing/hidden on New Tab page even though enabled in Customize menu

### Steps to reproduce

0. Ensure prefers-reduced-motion is on.
1. Open so many tabs that they start getting smaller.
2. Put mouse cursor on tab 2 from the left.
3. Close with middle mouse button repeatedly until there is no tab under the mouse cursor.
4. Move mouse cursor away.

### Actual results

Tab animation occurs BOTH on step 3 AND on step 4, separately.

### Expected results

There should have been no animations. And absolutely not twice.
I would have expected tabs to the left of the cursor, to never expand into the cursor.
Only after the cursor leaves the tab bar, should the existing tabs resize.

Note: Firefox not respecting prefers-reduced-motion when adding new features, is a longstanding issue. The before-shipping checklist for new features should be amended, or coding guidelines for animations should be changed.

state.description:
Four menus: `sidebar-bookmarks-context-menu` (the `sidebar-*` items Open in New Tab / Container Tab / Window / Private Window, Edit Bookmark, Delete Bookmark and Copy Link have none beside the Places items that do), `sidebar-history-context-menu` (Delete Pages from History beside Open All in Tabs), `sidebar-opentabs-menu` (Tab order and Recently active beside Connect Another Device) and `sidebar-synced-tabs-context-menu` (Open in New Tab, Open in New Container Tab).

Bug 2073853 adds an automation check: a menupopup or panel-list that opens with two visible items sharing an accesskey, or with items lacking one beside items that have one, logs an `AccessKeyConflictError` and fails the running browser-chrome test. This menu carries an `accesskey-conflicts-bug` attribute naming this bug so the check skips it. The fix picks unique letters for static items (a message whose accesskey changes gets a new Fluent id; no migration recipe) and removes the attribute in the same patch so the check guards the menu from then on. Items generated from data can't be given accesskeys, so a menu that mixes them with static items either drops the static items' accesskeys or moves the generated items into a submenu. Conflicts are per visible menu instance, so a letter has to be free among the items that can show together, not merely in the Fluent file.
state.summary: Sidebar context menu items have no accesskey beside items that do

state.description:
While working on [bug 2081441](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2081441) I found that if ConfirmationHint.show() gets called a second time while a hint is still opening, it ends up starting two auto-hide timers, and only one of them gets cleaned up when the hint closes. The leftover one fires about 3 seconds later and closes whatever hint is open at that point, so a later hint can disappear almost right after it shows up.

It looks like show() handles the hint being closed or fully open, but not the in-between "showing" state.

**Steps to reproduce:**

This is a timing issue (the second hint has to be triggered within a fraction of a second of the first), so it's hard to hit by hand. The easiest way to see it is with the test from bug 2081441, so it would likely be verified with further automated tests:

1. In browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_group_menu.js, remove the wait for the hint to open inside the loop in test_saveAndCloseGroup_confirmationHintCappedAtThree. That test saves and closes several tab groups back to back, so the second hint gets triggered while the first is still opening.

state.description:
Open the search mode switcher in the address bar or the new tab search bar and pick an engine that offers no suggestions for an empty query, e.g. Ecosia, or press its first letter. The results panel opens with no rows, showing only its border and shadow.

`UrlbarView.onQueryFinished` closes the view when a query returns nothing, except in search mode, where it keeps the view open so the one-off buttons stay reachable. With the search mode switcher there are no one-off buttons, so nothing fills the panel.

Bug 2073612 covers the panel staying open after its last result is removed; this is the panel opening empty in the first place.
state.summary: Entering search mode for an engine with no suggestions opens an empty results panel

state.description:
Created attachment 9657133
poc_trunc_trap_cvi.pdf

### Summary
    The PostScript Type 4 WebAssembly compiler emits the trapping `i32_trunc_f64_s` instruction instead of saturating truncation, leading to unhandled worker crashes (`RuntimeError: float
  unrepresentable in integer range`) on legal PDF inputs with out-of-range float values, `NaN`, or `Infinity`.
    
    ### Discovery & Methodology
    Discovered via an 8-core differential fuzzing harness testing 400,000 cases between the WebAssembly compiler and JavaScript fallback evaluator.
    
    ### Environment
    - **Operating System:** Linux x86_64 (Kali Linux)
    - **Browser:** Firefox 140.11.0esr (Build ID: 20260514160037) & latest Nightly
    - **Component:** PDF.js master (`src/core/postscript/wasm_compiler.js`)

    ### Steps to Reproduce
    1. Start Firefox with a clean profile.
    2. Press `Ctrl + Shift + K` to open the Web Developer Console.
    3. Open the attached minimal testcase: `poc_trunc_trap_cvi.pdf`.

    ### Expected Results
    The PDF renders cleanly without throwing exceptions. The JavaScript fallback interpreter (`PSStackBasedInterpreter`) safely wraps integer conversions using ECMAScript `ToInt32` (`value | 0`)
  semantics.

    ### Actual Results
    The rendering worker crashes with an unhandled WebAssembly trap:
    `RuntimeError: float unrepresentable in integer range`
    Shading stream evaluation aborts.

    ### Root Cause Analysis
    In `src/core/postscript/wasm_compiler.js`, float-to-integer conversions for operators such as `cvi` (line 430), `_compileBitshiftNode` (line 542), and `_compileBitwiseOperandI32` (line 669) use the
  trapping opcode `i32_trunc_f64_s` (0xAA).

    Per the WebAssembly core specification, this instruction traps if the value exceeds 32-bit signed limits (|val| >= 2^31), or is `NaN`/`Infinity`. Valid PDF Type 4 functions frequently produce domain
  values or intermediary calculation results exceeding this range.

    ### Regression Window
    Introduced in `src/core/postscript/wasm_compiler.js` via PR #21841.

    ### Suggested Fix
    Use the WebAssembly non-trapping saturating truncation opcode `i32.trunc_sat_f64_s` (`0xFC 0x02`):
    ```javascript
    // In OP table:
    i32_trunc_sat_f64_s_prefix: 0xfc,
    i32_trunc_sat_f64_s_idx: 0x02,
state.summary: PDF.js: WASM trap on out-of-range floats in Type 4 functions

state.description:
Environment
Firefox 159.0 release, build 20261023105132.
Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Resolute Raccoon).
Linux kernel 7.0.0-42-generic (x86_64), X11.
Intel Core i9-12900H, 20 logical CPUs.

Symptoms and reproduction
During ordinary browsing with Firefox left open, high CPU spikes occur intermittently, a few times per week at most. Firefox's own about:processes page has shown about 380% CPU. The trigger is unknown and there is no deterministic reproducer.

Profile
https://share.firefox.dev/3WLCInw

Over approximately 7.09 seconds of sampled activity in parent process 9258:
- Process CPU counter averages approximately 325% (100% = one logical CPU).
- sqldb:places.sqlite #4: approximately 6.91 CPU-seconds, or 97% of one logical CPU, executing the shortcut-ranking SQL query.
- GeckoMain: approximately 6.83 CPU-seconds, or 96% of one logical CPU, with UI/localization and task processing.
- glean.dispatcher: approximately 6.78 CPU-seconds, or 96% of one logical CPU, serializing and committing its metrics database.
- Other threads combined: approximately 36%, estimated as the remainder of the process CPU counter after the three threads above.

The process average is therefore approximately 325%, equivalent to 3.25 logical CPUs. The approximately 380% reading in Firefox's about:processes page is a separate observation; it is not the recording's average. The Places query accounts for approximately one logical CPU. The recording also shows substantial concurrent main-thread and Glean activity, but it does not establish that shortcut ranking causes that activity.

The Places thread spends almost all its CPU under a Connection::stepStatement SQL frame. Its truncated SQL label starts with WITH input_keys(guid), contains 14 input GUIDs, joins moz_places without an alias, then selects place_ids.guid AS key. This matches fetchShortcutInteractions in SmartShortcutsRanker/RankShortcuts.mjs at the captured build revision:
https://hg.mozilla.org/releases/mozilla-release/file/5add844c26613d7e4d84c799d6e23cf987b1240d/browser/extensions/newtab/lib/SmartShortcutsRanker/RankShortcuts.mjs#l617

That query aggregates shortcut clicks/impressions from moz_newtab_shortcuts_interaction over the last two months. SQLite strftimeFunc appears in approximately 63% of the database thread's CPU-weighted stacks.

Expected
Refreshing shortcut rankings should not keep a database thread at almost one full core throughout this recording.

Scope and related reports
This report focuses on the Places query; it does not claim this query explains all process CPU. Glean is concurrently committing/serializing its metrics database, and the main thread is busy with UI/localization/task processing.

Bug 2042142 concerns a different query, fetchLast10VisitsByGuid, in the same ranking module:
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2042142

Disabling shortcut personalization and its interaction feed, while keeping ordinary shortcuts enabled, is being tried. It is too early to determine whether that prevents recurrence.
state.summary: Smart Shortcuts fetchShortcutInteractions query consumes a core during intermittent high CPU (Firefox 159/Linux)

Several telemetry functions iterate over `Services.wm.getEnumerator("navigator:browser")`, which already lists a new window before its `gBrowser` exists. Collecting tab counts, tab group stats or the site origin count while a window is opening throws:

```
TypeError: can't access property "tabs", win.gBrowser is undefined
```

This happens in `getOpenTabsAndWinsCounts`, `getPinnedTabsCount` and the tab group telemetry in `BrowserUsageTelemetry.sys.mjs`, and in `BrowserTelemetryUtils.computeSiteOriginCount`.

User impact: the sample collected while another window opens is lost, e.g. when opening a window or popup while tabs are loading elsewhere.

On CI it was logged 14,492 times in 5,377 jobs, from 110 tests, out of the 31,690 mozilla-central mochitest jobs of 2026-10-15 in the errors dashboard (https://tests.firefox.dev/errors.html?kind=mochitest#date=2026-10-15).

Steps:

2. Create a tab group and close it.
3. Open History > Recently Closed Tabs.

The closed group has no submenu there, and `SessionStore.getClosedTabGroups()` returns nothing for the window.

`getClosedTabGroups` checks `sourceOptions.sourceWindow.closedGroups` before collecting the source window's closed groups. `sourceWindow` is the window itself, which has no `closedGroups` property, so the check is always false. Bug 1947503 added the check; the `?? []` it added in the same branch already covers session data without `closedGroups`, so the branch can go back to a plain `else`.

state.description:
Data on commonly thrown errors in startup show the top error is a `TypeError` originating in `SidebarController.startDelayedLoad`. A claude analysis showed a possible cause for this. Hard to say if it is actually the cause but covering this case is cheap.

```
getBackupState() returns null, which updateUIState doesn't handle

startDelayedLoad ends with:

const backupState = this.SidebarManager.getBackupState();
...
await this.updateUIState(backupState);

SidebarManager.getBackupState() (browser/components/sidebar/SidebarManager.sys.mjs:404) returns null in two cases:
- The sidebar.backupState pref doesn't parse. For example it's "", or it's missing so the lazy getter yields undefined. JSON.parse throws, and the catch block returns null.
- The pref is literally "null".

updateUIState(state = {}) (browser-sidebar.js:800) relies on its default parameter. A default only applies for undefined, not null, so the first line throws:

const isValidSidebar = !state.command || ...   // TypeError: state is null

The pref's default is "{}", so this only happens if the pref was set to something odd. setBackupState won't write null itself because it returns early on a falsy state.
```

We can either have `getBackupState` clear the pref in error and return the pref default, or change it to return `undefined` which would then trigger the default argument for `updateUIState`.
state.summary: `getBackupState` can return null which causes a TypeError in `updateUIState`

`browser_trigger_listeners.js` fails `test-verify`'s chaos-mode step ("3. Run each test 10 times in one browser, in chaos mode.") with a timeout: `This test exceeded the timeout threshold... Test ran for 205s, limit was 180s (timeout factor 2)`, followed by a full `Test timed out` on the second chaos pass. Steps 1 and 2 (non-chaos verify passes) pass fine, and the file passes normally outside `test-verify`.

Confirmed via a try push of the file's pre-Bug 2070783 content that this is pre-existing: it fails the same way with or without that unrelated fix applied, so it isn't a regression from any specific patch — the file is simply too large/slow to survive `test-verify`'s chaos-mode repeat passes.

The file has grown to ~20 `add_task`s across ~1280 lines covering several unrelated trigger-listener areas (`openURL` visit counters, address-bar-navigation triggers, IP Protection panel triggers, etc.). Splitting it into a few smaller files along those functional boundaries (and updating the relevant `browser.toml`) should bring each file's chaos-mode runtime back under the `test-verify` timeout. No test logic needs to change, just splitting the test file.
state.summary: Split browser_trigger_listeners.js so it survives test-verify chaos mode

**[Affected Platforms]:**
- Windows 11 x64
- Ubuntu 24.04 x64

**[Prerequisites]:**
- Have Firefox Release 158.0.1 installed on your machine.
- Have the following prefs set to `true`:
-> “browser.smartwindow.enabled”
-> ”browser.smartwindow.firstrun.hasCompleted”
- Set the “nimbus.debug” pref to `true` in the “about:config” page.
- Copy and paste this link into the browser to force enroll in the experiment: `about:studies?optin_slug=smartwindow-microsurvey-round-2-us&optin_branch=survey&optin_collection=nimbus-preview`.
- Have more than 2 chat interactions. 
- Have a New Smart Window session.

**[Steps to reproduce]:**
1. Open the browser with the profile from the prerequisites.
2. Open a new tab.
3. Open the device’s settings and move the date to 1 day in the future.
4. Close and reopen Firefox.

**[Expected result]:**
- The microsurvey is no longer displayed to the user.

**[Actual result]:**
- The microsurvey remains displayed.

**[Notes]:**
- The Brief [document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1os80GoTUglioWhAr1zJTeH2r7Fy47vHu0CC5pWde1Ok/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.ffxicw7s8nyt) states that the microsurvey should time out after 24 hours.

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:158.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/158.0

### Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open a window with several tabs in two or more named tab groups, with the groups collapsed, plus one tab outside any group.
2. Set "Open previous windows and tabs" (browser.startup.page = 3).
3. Update Firefox to 158.0.1, or restart with that session file.

### Actual results

Actual result:
- Only the tab outside a group is restored. The group headers come back, but all the tabs inside them are missing.
- In recovery.jsonlz4 the window keeps "busy": true and never finishes restoring.
- The next normal shutdown saves this broken state, so the tabs are lost for good unless the user restores the upgrade backup by hand.

Details:
- Windows 11 Home (10.0.26200), Firefox 158.0.1 x64 en-US, build 20261019185856. The previous build was 20261007201254.
- The pre-update upgrade.jsonlz4-20261019185856 held 18 tabs in 2 groups.
- Putting that file back as sessionstore.jsonlz4 gave the same hang: 1 tab, busy: true.
- Editing the same file so each group had "collapsed": false restored all 18 tabs and both groups correctly. That points to collapsed groups as the trigger.
- Saved (closed) groups were not affected.

Workaround: Expand all tab groups before updating, or edit the session file so the groups have collapsed: false.

### Expected results

Expected result: All tabs restore inside their groups.
state.summary: Session restore hangs and wipes tabs if collapsed tab groups present after updating to 158.0.1

state.description:
Steps:
1. With `browser.sessionstore.restore_on_demand` on, restore a tab in the background so it is pending with `about:mozilla` as its current entry.
2. Call `browser.loadURI()` on it with `about:mozilla#frag`.

Expected: the tab stops being pending and loads `about:mozilla#frag`.

Actual: the tab stays pending on the blank placeholder document with its URI rewritten to `about:mozilla#frag` (empty title, `text/html`), and it never restores. Loading `about:robots` instead restores it as expected.

A pending tab's docshell reports the restored URL as its current URI (`SetCurrentURIForSessionStore`), so the load is a same-document navigation. It adds a history entry without a network load, and the restore listener in `SessionStore.sys.mjs` reacts only to `onStartRequest`; its `OnHistoryNewEntry` is empty behind a `TODO(kashav)`. `ContentRestore.sys.mjs`, removed in bug 1886892, handled this in `OnHistoryNewEntry` by resetting the current URI to `about:blank` and starting a real load.

`browser_replace_load.js` covers this case but has been disabled since bug 1646894. Its setup also waits on `promiseBrowserLoaded` for a tab added with `about:blank`, which never fires a load now.
state.summary: Pending tab stays blank and never restores when loaded with a URL that differs only in its fragment

state.description:
Since bug 2049500, the overflow fade on vertical tabs spans a full tab row. When a tab gets scrolled into view (e.g. selecting it via Ctrl+Tab or the all-tabs menu, which goes through `_handleTabSelect` and `ensureElementIsVisible`), the tab strip scrolls only until the tab touches its edge, so the tab ends up under the fade and looks half-faded.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Enable vertical tabs and open enough tabs to overflow the tab strip.
2. Scroll to the top, then select a tab that is just below the visible area (e.g. with Ctrl+Tab).

Expected: the selected tab is fully visible.
Actual: the selected tab sits at the bottom edge inside the fade.

`scrollIntoView` honors `scroll-padding`, so a `scroll-padding-block` on the vertical scrollbox that matches the fade length keeps the tab clear of it.
state.summary: Vertical tabs scrolled into view stay partly faded at the edge of the tab strip

state.description:
In `MultiStageAboutWelcome`, the effect for `transition === "in"` clears the state two animation frames later with `setTransition("")`. If a navigation has set the transition to `"out"` before then, this overwrites it. That turns off the "only transition out once" guard in `handleTransition`, so a second navigation schedules another advance timer.

Result: a screen gets skipped. Because the timer's closure checks a stale `index`, a pending advance can also move past the last screen, leaving an empty page. Smart Window first run hits this with a short `auto_advance` (the intro's auto-advance re-arms on the re-render and navigates twice). It makes [`browser_aiwindow_firstrun.js`](https://tests.firefox.dev/test.html?test=browser/components/aiwindow/ui/test/browser/browser_aiwindow_firstrun.js) fail intermittently ([bug 2012723](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2012723)).

Fix: only clear the transition if it is still `"in"`: `setTransition(prev => (prev === "in" ? "" : prev))`.
state.summary: MultiStageAboutWelcome can advance two screens at once when a navigation happens right after a screen appears

state.description:
`AttributionParent` in `browser/extensions/newtab/lib/actors/NewTabAttributionParent.sys.mjs` keeps its Remote Settings client in a module global, `gAllowListClient`, but binds its sync handler per instance in the constructor (`this._onSync = this.onSync.bind(this)`). Only the instance that creates the client subscribes, in `retrieveAllowList()`. Every other instance's `didDestroy()` hands `RemoteSettingsClient.off` a callback that was never registered, and `off` throws `Error: Unknown callback`.

Two consequences. The noisy one is an exception on every actor teardown: 5,465 of them from `browser_attribution_actor.js` alone in one CI day, the loudest error that test emits. The one that matters is that when the actor which *is* the subscriber is destroyed, the only `sync` listener goes with it, and `retrieveAllowList()` early-returns once `gAllowListClient` is set, so nothing re-subscribes. `onSync` is dead from then on and the allowlist stops following Remote Settings for the rest of the session.

The client is a module global that outlives every actor, so its subscription should be too: subscribe once alongside the client and leave `didDestroy()` out of it, or keep the bound handler next to the client and unsubscribe only when the client itself is dropped.

`browser.newtabpage.activity-stream.discoverystream.attribution.enabled` defaults to false, which is why this is S4: nothing ships with the feature on today.

`test_onSync_updates_allowlist` in `browser_attribution_actor.js` cannot catch either consequence. It calls `parent.onSync()` directly, so it never exercises the subscription, and it then overwrites the allowlist with `setAllowListForTest([origin])` before asserting, so its assertion passes whether `onSync` worked or not. Repairing it belongs in the same patch as the fix.
state.summary: AttributionParent.didDestroy() throws "Unknown callback" and drops the attribution allowlist's Remote Settings subscription

state.description:
`test_newtab_dwell_time_in_ping` notifies `user-interaction-active-non-synthesized` by hand, sleeps 100 ms, closes the tab and asserts that `Glean.newtab.dwellTime` has a sample. `TelemetryFeed` credits each session's dwell stopwatch only up to the timestamp of the last "active" notification, which is deliberate: an idle tick means the user did nothing since then.

Because the test fabricates that notification instead of generating input, it has no control over the idle deadline. `EventStateManager`'s user-activity timer is armed by any trusted event, which test-synthesized events are, and its tick notifies `user-interaction-inactive-non-synthesized`, the topic the feed observes. When a tick lands inside the test's 100 ms window the feed credits zero and stops the clock, so no sample is accumulated and the ping carries no `newtab.dwell_time`:

    TEST-UNEXPECTED-FAIL | test_newtab_dwell_time_in_ping - dwell_time is in the newtab ping - null == true

The per-test profiles show the tick: `user-interaction-inactive-non-synthesized` from `UITimerCallback::Notify` 93 ms after the test's own "active" notification and 31 ms before its cleanup. It has failed this way twice on central in the 21 days to 2026-09-16, and much more often under `test-verify`, which runs the file about 30 times per task.

The fix is to stub the feed's `now()`, which exists so tests can drive the clock, and notify "active" twice with the fake clock advanced in between, the shape a continuing interaction has. An idle tick then credits the interval between the two notifications wherever it lands.

Test dashboard: https://tests.firefox.dev/test.html?test=browser/extensions/newtab/test/browser/browser_newtab_ping.js
state.summary: Intermittent browser/extensions/newtab/test/browser/browser_newtab_ping.js | test_newtab_dwell_time_in_ping - dwell_time is in the newtab ping - null == true

Created attachment 9668385
poc_type4.pdf

### Short Description
A 733-byte PDF makes Firefox's PDF worker consume memory without bound until the tab, the browser or (on Android) the device runs out of RAM. No user interaction beyond opening the file is required.
### Affected
  - Firefox 158.0.1 desktop: bundles pdf.js 6.4.195; tab memory reached ~5 GB.
  - Firefox for Android 158.0.1: same file exhausted device RAM
  - pdfjs 6.4.299 (Tested Deploying Locally as well as [Official Online Demo](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/web/viewer.html) provided in [pdf.js repo](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js))

### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
  1. Save the attached poc_type4.pdf  or run attached make_type4_pdf.py to create the malicious pdf.
  2. Open it in Firefox 158 from local storage (desktop or Android).
  3. Watch memory in the Browser Task Manager(Shift+Esc) or OS task manager.

**Expected**: the one-page PDF renders in milliseconds (see attached valid_type4.pdf control).
**Actual**: The PDF worker never completes; memory grows continuously. On desktop it reaches ~5 GB and the machine swaps. On Android the device runs out of RAM and other apps are killed. Closing the tab is the only way out and the viewer cannot cancel the worker.

### Root Cause

In `src/core/postscript/lexer.js`, `Lexer._getNumber()` may return a number token without advancing `this.pos` when the numeric regex fails to match or matches a non-finite literal such as `1e999`. In these cases, `next()` rewinds on `+`, `-`, and `.`, causing the parser to repeatedly process the same character. Each iteration allocates a new `PsNumber`, resulting in an infinite loop and unbounded memory consumption.

**Trigger inputs:** `{+}`, `{-}`, `{.}`, and `{1e999}`. The provided PoC uses `{+}`.

#### Note:
I would like to submit more Attachments(Andriod, Windows, Locally Deployed Pdf.js Video POC) but the form allows single attachment submission, so i have attached the main Malicious pdf `poc_type4.pdf` in initial report. 

What would you suggest me to use to share these POC Videos as well as the Python script to create this Malicious PDF?
state.summary: Unbounded Memory Growth in FireFox PDF Viewer(pdf.js) and Affects Firefox Desktop and Android

Strings are in `tabbrowser.ftl` and `tabContextMenu.ftl`, which together leave f j k q z unused; the mute item's message id is chosen at runtime by tabbrowser.

Bug 2073853 adds an automation check: a menupopup or panel-list that opens with two visible items sharing an accesskey, or with items lacking one beside items that have one, logs an `AccessKeyConflictError` and fails the running browser-chrome test. This menu carries an `accesskey-conflicts-bug` attribute naming this bug so the check skips it. The fix picks unique letters for static items (a message whose accesskey changes gets a new Fluent id; no migration recipe) and removes the attribute in the same patch so the check guards the menu from then on. Items generated from data can't be given accesskeys, so a menu that mixes them with static items either drops the static items' accesskeys or moves the generated items into a submenu. Conflicts are per visible menu instance, so a letter has to be free among the items that can show together, not merely in the Fluent file.

For example, issue14982.pdf (800 x 5424 pt) at 110% with DPR 1.5 gets a 1758 x 11931 px canvas: a render takes about 2 s, against 40 ms at 70% where the canvas fits.

With acceleration enabled, the viewer should use the smaller of the two sizes, and rely on the detail view beyond it: the same render then takes about 40 ms.

Created attachment 9657132
poc_unreachable_0mod.pdf

### Summary
    The PostScript Type 4 WebAssembly JIT compiler (`src/core/postscript/wasm_compiler.js`) contains an unhandled opcode omission causing an unrecoverable `RuntimeError: unreachable` trap when rendering
  PDF documents containing `{ 0 mod }` Type 4 functions.
    
    ### Discovery & Methodology
    Discovered via differential fuzzing and static audit comparing the WebAssembly JIT compiler against the reference JavaScript interpreter (`PSStackBasedInterpreter`).
    
    ### Environment
    - **Operating System:** Linux x86_64 (Kali Linux)
    - **Browser:** Firefox 140.11.0esr (Build ID: 20260514160037) & latest Nightly
    - **Component:** PDF.js master (`src/core/postscript/wasm_compiler.js`)
    
    ### Steps to Reproduce
    1. Start Firefox with a clean profile.
    2. Press `Ctrl + Shift + K` to open the Web Developer Console.
    3. Open the attached minimal testcase: `poc_unreachable_0mod.pdf` (drag & drop into Firefox or use File -> Open File).
    
    ### Expected Results
    The document should render smoothly without throwing runtime errors, matching the behavior of the JavaScript fallback interpreter.
    
    ### Actual Results
    The rendering worker crashes with an unhandled WebAssembly trap:
    `RuntimeError: unreachable`
    The shading pattern fails to render and worker execution is aborted.
    
    ### Root Cause Analysis
    In `src/core/postscript/wasm_compiler.js`, the `OP` table (lines 26-60) defines WebAssembly opcodes but omits `drop` (opcode `0x1a`).
    
    In `_compileModNode(first, second)` at line 563:
    ```javascript
    if (first.type === PS_NODE.const && first.value === 0) {
      if (!this._compileNode(second)) {
        return false;
      }
      this._code.push(OP.drop);
      this._emitF64Const(0);
      return true;
    }

  Because OP.drop is missing from the object, it evaluates to undefined. When pushed into the bytecode array and converted via new Uint8Array(code), undefined coerces to byte 0x00.

  In WebAssembly, 0x00 is the unreachable opcode. Any execution hitting this path unconditionally traps.

  ### Regression Window

  Introduced in src/core/postscript/wasm_compiler.js via PR #21841.

  ### Suggested Fix

  Add drop to the OP table:

    const OP = {
      // ...
      drop: 0x1a,
      // ...
    };
state.summary: PDF.js: WASM unreachable trap on Type 4 mod with zero divisor

Created attachment 9650665
testcase.html

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Settings > Files and Applications, set "Portable Document Format (PDF)" to "Use [external application]" (tested with Adobe Acrobat Reader).
2. Load a web page that embeds a PDF in an iframe (see attached testcase).

Environment: Windows 11 64-bit, Firefox 157.0 (fr). Reproduced on both managed and unmanaged machines. No Handlers, PDFjs or DisableBuiltinPDFViewer enterprise policies are set.

### Actual results

The PDF is rendered inside the iframe with the built-in viewer (pdf.js). The external application setting is ignored.

With pdfjs.disabled=true, the iframe shows "Unable to display this PDF here" with an "Open PDF" button, which downloads the file and only then opens it in the external application.

Direct links to PDF files still open correctly in the external application. Only the iframe case is affected.

Also reproduces in Firefox 158 Beta.

### Expected results

The configured external application opens the PDF, as it did in Firefox 156 (works as expected in 156.0b5, broken in 157.0 and 158 Beta).

Business impact: we are an MSP. Several of our customers use a web ERP that shows generated PDFs (purchase orders, invoices) in an iframe. Their users relied on this behavior to open the PDF directly in their PDF editor and send it by email from there. About 18 machines are affected so far across 5 customers, with more expected as they update to 157. Current workaround: pdfjs.disabled=true, which adds an extra click and disables PDF preview on all sites.
state.summary: PDF in iframe renders in pdf.js instead of the configured external application (regression in 157)

state.description:
With vertical tabs enabled, File > Close Window is hidden. This shows on macOS, where the menubar is always available, and on other platforms when the menubar is opened from the keyboard.

`tab-bar-visibility.js` hides `menu_closeWindow` and gives `menu_close` the label "Close" when `hideTabsToolbar` is true, which was meant for windows that only ever hold one tab, such as popups. Since bug 1915739, `hideTabsToolbar` is also true with vertical tabs, which hold any number of tabs.

The "Close" label never shows: the File menu's `popupshowing` handler (`updateTabCloseCountState` in `browser.js`) always replaces it with `menu-file-close-tab`, so a popup window shows "Close Tab" too. Both messages `tab-bar-visibility.js` sets lack an accesskey.

The fix could base both on the single-tab window condition instead of `hideTabsToolbar`, and choose the label in `updateTabCloseCountState` with a message that has an accesskey.
state.summary: File menu has no Close Window item when vertical tabs are enabled

state.description:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Restore a session state in which a window contains a tab with a groupId that is not present in that window's groups array. This happens in the wild whenever tab data and tab group definitions get separated — e.g. a session file assembled from _closedWindows/savedGroups (where the group definitions live), a partially written store, or a merge of two states.
2. Start Firefox with the state (browser.startup.page = 3, or use Restore Previous Session).

### Actual results

Tabs restore up to the first tab with the unresolvable groupId. That tab and every remaining tab of the window never open, with no error in the UI. The only trace is in the browser console:

```
JavaScript error: moz-src:///browser/components/sessionstore/SessionStore.sys.mjs, line 6341:
Error: Shouldn't be trying to restore a tab that has no position
```

### Expected results

All tabs are restored. The tab whose group cannot be resolved is restored ungrouped (that is clearly the intent — the code even says "if a tab refers to a tab group we don't know, skip any group processing").
state.summary: Session restore silently drops every tab after a tab whose groupId is not in the window's groups list

state.description:
A `domwindowopened` observer can close a newly created restore window synchronously, before `Services.ww.openWindow()` returns. `SessionStore.#openWindowWithState()` then registers restore data and a showing promise for that already-closed handle. There will be no subsequent before-show or close notification to settle the promise, so `#openWindows()` waits indefinitely and the surviving windows are not restored.

A deterministic privileged test case is to intercept the first additional window opened by `setBrowserState()` with a `domwindowopened` observer and close it synchronously. The primary window and a second additional window should still complete their restores. The same boundary needs handling when `undoCloseWindow()` receives an already-closed handle.

The proposed patch returns an already-closed handle before registering restore data or a showing promise. Bulk restoration skips that slot, decrementing the restore count only when a counted restore is active; this preserves the idle counter used by `setWindowState()`. `undoCloseWindow()` keeps its return value and closed-object notification but does not wait for first-show on the canceled handle.

This is a small lifecycle extraction from [D315350](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D315350), related to bug 500911. It does not require the focus transaction or native activation changes. Its scope is synchronous closure during creation while another restore participant survives, plus undo-close compatibility. Later closure and completion with no surviving restore participant remain separate cases.

The regression test covers one canceled additional window, all additional windows canceled with the primary surviving, idle `setWindowState()` notification accounting, and a canceled undo-close followed by a normal undo-close. In Try 112807, the new test and the existing closed-window notification test both pass on Linux opt/debug under headed X11/GNOME. Both builds and all nine source checks pass. An unpatched negative-control run has not been performed for this new test.

Try: [Linux opt](https://treeherder.mozilla.org/jobs?repo=try&revision=466b5e97e75aecf8ac18b81e45ba7b6a000073e9&selectedTaskRun=XSs_qSONRVaLHnEozp5qTg.0), [Linux debug](https://treeherder.mozilla.org/jobs?repo=try&revision=466b5e97e75aecf8ac18b81e45ba7b6a000073e9&selectedTaskRun=dycf_plvSA6f11Jknsk-zw.0).

The group header label for recent searches (`urlbar-group-recent-searches`), shown
above the recent searches group in the address bar results panel, currently reads

convention for desktop UI labels, and specifically contradicts two things already in

   `browser/locales/en-US/browser/preferences/preferences.ftl` labels this exact same

   `urlbar-group-search-suggestions` ("{ $engine } suggestions") and
   `urlbar-group-trending` ("Trending on { $engine }").

The address bar results panel is not a menu bar, app menu, or context menu, so the
title case exception does not apply here.

This is a casing-only change with no change in meaning, so the existing message ID is
edited in place and no new ID is needed.

```
browser/locales/en-US/browser/browser.ftl
urlbar-group-recent-searches: "Recent Searches" -> "Recent searches"

- The automated casing test
  `browser/base/content/test/browser-static/browser_sentence_case_strings.js` does not
  cover address bar strings, and this phrase is not in its PHRASES allowlist, so no
  companion test change is required.

This fix was traced and validated using an AI-assisted content design workflow (Claude).

state.description:
`ExternalComponentWrapper`'s loading effect has no staleness check. `loadComponent()` awaits a dynamic `import()` and then acts on refs, but React can tear the effect down and start a new one while that await is pending, and the old continuation still runs.

A search feature-gate flip does exactly that. `newtabFeatureGate` swaps the SEARCH component between `UrlbarNewTabComponentRegistrant`'s `moz-urlbar` and `SearchUIUtils`'s `content-search-handoff-ui`, which re-runs the effect on a preloaded `about:newtab` that is still mounting. Two things then go wrong:

- Default branch: the stale continuation still passes `containerRef.current && !customElementRef.current`, so it appends the superseded configuration's element -- after its own cleanup has already run. The new effect's continuation then sees a set ref and creates nothing. Which search bar you end up with depends only on which of the two imports resolves first, and the wrong one survives until the page is reloaded.
- `react-bundle` branch: the stale continuation appends a second `<script>` to `document.head` and overwrites `scriptRef.current` and `cleanupRef.current`, leaking a script element and a mounted React tree that nothing will ever clean up, and mounts into a shadow root that cleanup has already emptied and disconnected from `document.l10n`.

The trigger is wider than a gate flip. The `REFRESH_EXTERNAL_COMPONENTS` reducer returns `components: action.data`, a fresh array identity, so any registry update re-runs the effect even when no configuration changed; `browser.nova.enabled` alone produces one, although neither registrant's `getComponents()` reads it. And a single gate flip calls `updated()` on both SEARCH registrants, so two broadcasts arrive back to back and the second lands inside the first one's import window.

Suggested fix: give the effect a cancellation flag, set it in the cleanup function, and bail out after each `await`, rather than treating `customElementRef.current` as proof of what is in the DOM. The comment excluding `props` from the dependency array records the assumption that is wrong.

Found by reading the code during a flakiness burndown of browser/extensions/newtab/test/browser. No test currently reaches it: bug 2062212 turned the gate off in `add_setup` for `browser_as_render.js`, which was the one test exercising a mid-mount flip.

state.description:
From claude:
`browser_multiselect_tabs_using_keyboard.js` calls `CustomizableUI.reset()` in its cleanup function. `reset()` sets `sidebar.verticalTabs` to `false`, and nothing sets it back. The browser-chrome harness only records changed prefs (as a todo unless `comparePrefs` is set); it does not restore them.

In the vertical-tabs variant (`--setpref=sidebar.verticalTabs=true`), every test in `browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser.toml` that runs after this one in the same browser therefore runs with horizontal tabs, so the variant is not testing what it claims to for most of that manifest.

Evidence: the `modifiedPrefs.json` artifact from a passing Windows shippable vertical-tabs browser-chrome task (FGsnFIdeRUa9TG_nFa5W0w) lists `sidebar.visibility`, `sidebar.verticalTabs` and `browser.uiCustomization.horizontalTabstrip` against `browser_multiselect_tabs_using_keyboard.js`, and no later test changes `sidebar.verticalTabs` again.

This also hides a real CustomizableUI bug: with a new profile and vertical tabs enabled, the nav-bar is missing `stop-reload-button` and other default buttons (filed separately). `browser_reload_deleted_file.js` passes in CI only because this reset runs first and rebuilds the horizontal defaults. It fails when the browser restarts in between.

Possible fixes:
- Restore `sidebar.verticalTabs` (and the CustomizableUI state for the current orientation) after the reset, or avoid `CustomizableUI.reset()` and just undo the specific `removeWidgetFromArea("developer-button")` change the test makes.
- `browser_drag_to_pin.js` uses the same `CustomizableUI.reset()` cleanup pattern. It is not tagged `vertical-tabs` today, so it does not affect the variant yet, but it would if it were added.
- Longer term, the harness could fail a test that changes a pref the variant sets, so this kind of problem is caught.

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/148.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

### Steps to reproduce

Local-only reproduction (no live sites or remote PDFs were used):

1. In the local pdf.js harness, run: node gen4tiny.mjs 800 600
2. 2. Run: node run.mjs t-bigimg.pdf 60000
3. 3. gen4tiny.mjs creates a 693-byte PDF with an RGB image XObject declaring 800x600, while its decoded stream contains only 1 KiB.
4. 4. The renderer fails with RangeError: Invalid typed array length, through new Uint32Array -> convertRGBToRGBA -> putBinaryImageData.
5. 5. The same happens at 1000x700 and 30000x30000. The HEAD helper was also replayed directly with a 1 KiB source buffer and throws.
Harness/write-up: hunt/big/harness and hunt/big/ADVISORY-PDFJS.md.

### Actual results

The affected page does not render. Local output:
{"ok":false,"ms":84,"err":"Invalid typed array length: 9600"}
with stack through convertRGBToRGBA / putBinaryImageData. A 693-byte input is sufficient. A complete 20000x20000 RGB image also causes about 28 seconds and about 3.6 GB RSS in the local Node renderer.

Root cause: src/shared/image_utils.js calculates len = width*height*3 from attacker-controlled PDF dimensions and constructs a Uint32Array view without clamping to the available decoded source buffer. src/core/image.js calls the same converter on the worker path.

### Expected results

A truncated or malformed image stream should be rejected gracefully or rendered as a partial/invalid image without throwing an uncaught RangeError or excessive memory use. The PDF viewer should remain usable.
state.summary: RangeError in convertRGBToRGBA when an RGB image stream is shorter than its declared size
