User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:156.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/156.0

### Steps to reproduce

In Firefox 156.0.1 I went to the _Customize sidebar_ tab of the sidebar. I unchecked the option **Open tools from sidebar**. This causes the navigation through the various tabs/tools of the sidebar to become very unreliable. Because the dropdown selector on some of the tabs simply does not work. On the _History_ tab, on the _Passwords_ tab and on the _Tabs from other devices_ tab the dropdown selector works fine. But on the bookmarks tab the dropdown selector is fully bugged. The chevron does not display after the name _Bookmarks_. And the name _Bookmarks_ is also unclickable. As a result, I cannot actually navigate away from the Bookmarks tab using the mouse. I can only navigate away using the keyboard. I verified that I could successfully navigate away to the _History_ tab using the keyboard shortcut _Ctrl+H_. 
The dropdown selector is for me personally also bugged for the _AI chatbot_ tab. That is probably caused because I have not selected the AI chatbot of my choice yet. I am greeted with a screen that offers me to choose between Anthropic Claude, ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Mistral Vibe. The dropdown selector at the top is bugged, and I cannot navigate away to a different tab using the mouse. Although the chevron behind _AI chatbot_ does display, the entire line is displayed in dark grey (it is greyed out) and the line is unclickable and I cannot navigate to a different tab using the mouse. But I verified that I could navigate away using the keyboard. For example, I could press _Ctrl+B_ to go to the _Bookmarks_ tab. But since that tab also has a bugged dropdown selector, I had to press _Ctrl+H_ to go to the _History_ tab to get a working dropdown selector. From there I could navigate to the _Customize sidebar_ tab to once again enable the option labelled _Open tools from sidebar_. With this option enabled, navigating between the various tabs/tools does work reliably.

### Actual results

The dropdown selector is bugged for the _Bookmarks_ tab, and because I have not selected the AI Chatbot that I prefer yet the dropdown selector is also bugged for the _AI chatbot_ tab. I cannot navigate away to a different tab/tool using the mouse. I can only navigate to a different tab/tool using a keyboard shortcut.

### Expected results

The dropdown selector should reliably work for every single tab/tool. I should never have to use a keyboard shortcut to navigate away from the tab/tool, because the navigation with the mouse is broken.

https://connect.mozilla.org/t5/discussions/phasing-out-the-older-version-of-firefox-sidebar-in-2026/td-p/115477/page/2
Citation from asafko:
**With Nova coming out in 157 and as we have not been supporting and testing the old sidebar for a while, we will be turning the updated sidebar on for tWith Firefox 157. If you were on the old version of the sidebar, your layout will default to the dropdown selector, as in the old version. **

Defaulting to the dropdown selector for the people still using the old version of the sidebar is an absolutely terrible idea!!! A very large amount of people is going to be using the dropdown selector then, and it is heavily bugged!!! So if it is still possible to change this before the release of Firefox 157, then you have to respond immediately!!!
state.summary: Dropdown panel selection in new sidebar: cannot navigate away from bookmarks tab (and AI chatbot tab)

Created attachment 9667450
pdf-text-lifecycle-main.patch

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/155.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Firefox 158.0.1 (BuildID 20261019185856) with a fresh temporary profile.
2. Open a locally generated 300-page PDF and wait for the PDF viewer to become ready.
3. Using a local Firefox test harness, initiate text extraction through PdfJsParent.getTextContent() and PageExtractorParent.
4. Immediately close the PDF tab before the viewer returns the text.
5. Observe the state of both pending requests.

The issue was reproduced in a real Firefox process without artificially delaying responses. A test harness was used to invoke and observe the internal methods.

### Actual results

Both text extraction Promises remained pending after the PDF tab was closed and the PdfJs actor was destroyed (actor.manager === null).

The requests were still pending after an additional 17.3 seconds of observation.

PdfJsParent.getTextContent() stores only the Promise resolver in #textRequests. The didDestroy() method does not reject outstanding requests or clear this map.

In a separate test, an outstanding extraction callback also delayed HiddenBrowserManager cleanup until external cancellation occurred.

This behavior was reproduced in Firefox 158.0.1. The relevant lifecycle code also remains present in main revision 134b5b571ed437f50b82b5725a2ac990c9bca8ce.

No browser-wide hang or quantified memory exhaustion was demonstrated.

### Expected results

When PdfJsParent is destroyed, all outstanding text extraction Promises should be rejected with an appropriate error, such as AbortError, and their entries should be removed from #textRequests.

This would allow awaiting callers to finish error handling and release associated resources.

A proposed patch implementing this behavior passed 23 local regression checks and 3 browser reproduction runs. A full mochitest run using mach has not yet been performed.
state.summary: PDF text extraction promises remain pending when PdfJsParent is destroyed

state.description:
When the final session write at shutdown fails, we seem to announce that it succeeded - the `sessionstore-final-state-write-complete` notification gets published unconditionally.  And then the conflation of write failure with crashing makes the sequence hard to follow and the logging and telemetry around it confusing. 

AFAICT this is mostly a code clarity problem. `sessionstore-final-state-write-complete` is really more like "our attempt to write to disk is complete".   But its absence really means "we did not reach the end of a successful final write" - which a crash causes, as would a power loss, an OS kill, or a shutdown hang. 

```js
this._previousSessionCrashed = !checkpoints["sessionstore-final-state-write-complete"];
```

...presents an inference as a fact, obscured by the naming. It seems ultimately the right thing happens - by not completing the final write, the recovery file is left intact and will get restored at the next start up. So this task to try to make all this a bit clearer.
state.summary: _previousSessionCrashed conflates a failed final write with a crash

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:157.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/157.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run GlazeWM with workspace 3 displayed on the left monitor and occupied workspace 2 displayed on the right monitor.
2. Open the browser on workspace 3, then close it there, leaving its previous location on the left monitor.
3. Focus workspace 2 on the right monitor.
4. Launch a browser window using `firefox.exe --new-window about:blank` (the instrumented Zen test used `zen.exe --new-window about:blank`).
5. Observe its initial tiled location and its location after startup settles.
6. Query GlazeWM's window and workspace state.
7. Run `glazewm command wm-redraw`.

These are GlazeWM workspaces, not browser-internal workspaces. Both workspaces were displayed during the measured test. Firefox reproduction was observed manually; the numerical measurements below were collected in Zen only.

### Actual results

The browser initially accepts GlazeWM's assigned tile on the right monitor, then moves and changes size during startup, ending up on the left monitor. GlazeWM still assigns the window to workspace 2 and retains the expected tile rectangle on the right monitor. The physical window overlaps windows on workspace 3.

`glazewm command wm-redraw` restores the intended placement. Explicit moves between monitors also work after startup. Repeating manual repairs on launch is disruptive.

### Expected results

Startup/session geometry restoration should cooperate with the external window manager rather than overriding a position and size it has already applied. If `browser.restoreWindowState.disabled` is intended to disable geometry restoration, it should cover the session-restoration path too, or its narrower scope should be documented.
state.summary: Startup geometry restoration overrides GlazeWM workspace placement and moves Firefox windows to the previous monitor

state.description:
When a page whose scheme isn't http, https, file or about (for instance a moz-extension page) declares a favicon, `LinkHandlerParent` asks Places to store it. `setFaviconForPage` refuses pages with these schemes, and the exception is logged:

```
[Exception... "Component returned failure code: 0x80070057 (NS_ERROR_ILLEGAL_VALUE) [nsIFaviconService.setFaviconForPage]"
```

User impact: none on the tab icon, which is still set. It's an error in the browser console for every extension page with a favicon.

On CI it was logged 16,898 times in 3,502 jobs, from 10 tests, out of the 26,201 mochitest jobs of 2026-10-08 in the errors dashboard (https://tests.firefox.dev/errors.html?data-source=try&kind=mochitest).

Checking the page's scheme before asking Places to store the icon would avoid it.
state.summary: NS_ERROR_ILLEGAL_VALUE from setFaviconForPage for favicons of extension and other non-web pages

new history.png

Currently, the entries within the new _History, Tabs from other devices, and Open tabs_ sidebar panels all have the same tooltip in a format:
_Open %URL% in a new tab_

This is redundant as URL is already displayed in the info panel at the bottom of the page, and doesn't provide enough useful information for single page application websites where URL may be nearly identical, but the title changes from page to page. We would like to change the tooltip for entries in these panels to the same format panels in the old sidebar had:

Page title (followed by a line break)
URL

Note: The new Bookmarks panel correctly displays the tooltip in the desired format
Title (followed by a line break)
URL

### Steps to reproduce

1. Restore a session state in which a window contains a tab with a groupId that is not present in that window's groups array. This happens in the wild whenever tab data and tab group definitions get separated — e.g. a session file assembled from _closedWindows/savedGroups (where the group definitions live), a partially written store, or a merge of two states.
2. Start Firefox with the state (browser.startup.page = 3, or use Restore Previous Session).

### Actual results

Tabs restore up to the first tab with the unresolvable groupId. That tab and every remaining tab of the window never open, with no error in the UI. The only trace is in the browser console:

```
JavaScript error: moz-src:///browser/components/sessionstore/SessionStore.sys.mjs, line 6341:
Error: Shouldn't be trying to restore a tab that has no position
```

### Expected results

All tabs are restored. The tab whose group cannot be resolved is restored ungrouped (that is clearly the intent — the code even says "if a tab refers to a tab group we don't know, skip any group processing").
state.summary: Session restore silently drops every tab after a tab whose groupId is not in the window's groups list

state.description:
Created attachment 9657145
Screen Recording 2026-10-09 at 5.20.46 PM.mov

**Problem**

A user signed into Firefox without the Sync key (third-party auth, a passwordless sign-in, or a VPN/Relay/Smart Window `keys_optional` login that skipped the password) has two ways to turn Sync on, and they land on different FxA pages:

- Sync promo / FxView "Turn on sync" → `gSync.openSyncSetupForEntryPoint` (`browser/base/content/browser-sync.js`) → `FxAccounts.config.promiseSetPasswordURI` → `/post_verify/third_party_auth/set_password?service=sync&entrypoint=…` with uid/email. One click to the create-password form.
- FxA toolbar menu → sync-status button (`_onSyncStatusButtonClick`, signed in + Sync off) → `openPrefsFromFxaMenu("sync_settings")` → about:preferences#sync → "Set up sync" → `SyncHelpers.setupSync()` (`browser/components/preferences/config/account-sync.mjs:198`) → no keys → `promiseConnectAccountURI("sync")` → FxA `/` (email-first). FxA pre-fills the browser account and, for a passwordless account, shows a **cached sign-in** step ("Sign in — Continue to Firefox Sync") before set_password. That's three clicks (menu → prefs → set up → sign in) where the promo path needs one.

Attached is a video recording of signing into VPN with a cached sign-in flow, and then trying to turn Sync on. This used to be 1 click from the Fx menu that would take the user to create a password but now it takes 3 clicks to get there. I'm not sure if there was a Product decision to take the user to `about:preferences` first, but either way we can at least _not_ show the cached sign-in screen on the FxA side by going to `/post_verify/third_party_auth/set_password` instead of to `/` if the sync key is missing.

**How it got this way**

- Bug 1971841 (Dec 11 2025) converted the Sync prefs section to config-based settings; `setupSync()`'s no-key branch was written against `promiseConnectAccountURI`.
- Bug 2006503 (Dec 18 2025) added `promiseSetPasswordURI` and routed `browser-sync.js` to set_password — but only the promo path; the prefs page wasn't touched.
- Bug 1968107 (Apr 2 2026) created the new Account & Sync pane (`account-sync.mjs`) and carried the `/` behaviour over.

**Fix**

- `SyncHelpers.setupSync()` no-key branch → `promiseSetPasswordURI(entrypoint)`, matching `openSyncSetupForEntryPoint`. Consider sharing one helper so the two can't diverge again.
- Ideally the FxA-menu sync-status button for a signed-in, Sync-off, **key-less** account goes straight to set_password rather than via about:preferences (`_onSyncStatusButtonClick` can call `openSyncSetupForEntryPoint`); with the key it can keep opening prefs (see ticket 3 for the first-time case).

**FxA behaviour to rely on**

- set_password redirects accounts that already have a password to `/signin` (password form) — so this is also correct for the `keys_optional` case, where the password form is what fetches the key. No changes needed on he FxA side.

**Tests**: `browser/components/preferences/tests/` for the pane; `browser/base/content/test/browser-sync/` for the menu button.
state.summary: Turning on Sync for an account without the Sync key should open FxA's set_password page directly

When on a site like Phabricator or Bugzilla, hovering to expand/collapse the sidebar intermittently causes the scroll position to jump around and layout to shift/be obscured (see attached screenshot and this [screen recording](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1WvNhWiYb5DU7qUxrVQ0VPBO_vWyClzgo/view?usp=sharing)).

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:154.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/154.0

### Steps to reproduce

This issue is intermittent and has occurred at least three times: around August 28, August 30, and October 8, 2026.

1. Enable Settings > General > Open previous windows and tabs.
2. Use one normal Firefox window containing fewer than 10 open tabs, including tab groups.
3. Close Firefox normally.
4. Shut down Windows normally.
5. Start Windows again.
6. Launch Firefox.

I cannot reproduce the issue on demand. Firefox may work normally for days or weeks before the session is lost again.

### Actual results

Firefox opened with only one about:home tab. All previously open tabs and tab groups were missing.

History > Restore Previous Session was unavailable, and the missing session was not present under Recently Closed Windows or Recently Closed Tabs.

I backed up and decoded the session files before attempting recovery:

- previous.jsonlz4: windows=1, tabs=0, _closedTabs=25
- recovery.jsonlz4: windows=1, tabs=1, current URL=about:home, _closedTabs=25
- recentCrashes=0

The 25 closed entries were older tabs that I had manually closed. They were not the missing active session, which contained fewer than 10 tabs.

For the most recent incident:
- Windows shut down normally at 07:00:49.
- Windows started at 18:35:32.
- An empty Firefox session was written at 18:43:14.
- I did not manually launch Firefox at 18:43.
- I first manually launched Firefox at approximately 19:27 and found the empty session.

The session files were valid JSON and were not truncated or unreadable. Firefox had recorded closed tabs in _closedTabs but recorded no active tabs in tabs[].

There was no corresponding Firefox crash report, Windows application crash, or Firefox update at the time.

Replacing the empty files with an older valid sessionstore backup restored the tabs successfully. After Firefox worked normally for some time, the same data-loss problem occurred again.

### Expected results

Firefox should restore all tabs and tab groups from the previous session.

If restoration fails, Firefox should retain the last valid session as a recoverable backup instead of overwriting it with a clean session containing tabs:[].
state.summary: Session Restore intermittently saves tabs:[] and loses all open tabs after a normal shutdown

Steps:
1. Set `browser.sessionstore.closedTabsFromAllWindows` to false.
2. Create a tab group and close it.
3. Open History > Recently Closed Tabs.

The closed group has no submenu there, and `SessionStore.getClosedTabGroups()` returns nothing for the window.

`getClosedTabGroups` checks `sourceOptions.sourceWindow.closedGroups` before collecting the source window's closed groups. `sourceWindow` is the window itself, which has no `closedGroups` property, so the check is always false. state.description:
Steps to reproduce:

1. In Settings, turn on "Open previous windows and tabs".
2. Open two windows. In window A, open some tabs. In one of them, open https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wikipedia:Sandbox&action=edit and type some text. Do not save.
3. In window A, select all tabs: click the first tab, then Shift+click the last tab.
4. Right-click a selected tab and choose "Close Tabs".
5. At the prompt "This page is asking you to confirm that you want to leave", click "Stay on page". Window A stays open with all its tabs.
6. Quit Firefox (menu > Quit). If the page prompts again, choose "Leave page".
7. Start Firefox.

Actual results:

- Window A is not restored. It is in History > Recently Closed Windows, and Ctrl+Shift+N reopens it.
- If window A is the only window, Firefox opens one blank tab. The old tabs are in the list of recently closed tabs, and only `browser.sessionstore.max_tabs_undo` of them (default 25) are kept. The other tabs are lost. "Restore Previous Session" is not available.

Expected results:

Window A is restored with all its tabs, because it was open when Firefox quit.

Notes:

Windows or Linux only -- this does not repro on MacOS.

Cause:

- `closeWindow()` in `toolkit/content/globalOverlay.js` calls `SessionStore.maybeDontRestoreTabs(window)` before `window.close()`, and does not check whether the window really closed. It does this only when the platform is not macOS.
- `removeMultiSelectedTabs()` calls `Tabbrowser.removeTabs()`. When the tabs to remove are all the tabs of the window and `browser.tabs.closeWindowWithLastTab` is true, `removeTabs()` calls `closeWindow(true, ...)` before any `beforeunload` check. The `beforeunload` prompt comes later, during `window.close()`. When the user cancels it, the window stays open with `_maybeDontRestoreTabs` set.
- Nothing clears `_maybeDontRestoreTabs` while the window stays open, so it is saved to the session file.
- At the next automatic restore, `#removeExplicitlyClosedTabs()` in `SessionStore.sys.mjs` moves a window with this flag to `_closedWindows`. If it is the only window, it moves all its tabs to `_closedTabs` instead.

Notes:

- macOS is not affected, because `closeWindow()` does not set the flag there.
- Closing only the last tab of a window is not affected: there, `beforeunload` runs before `closeWindow()`. Deleting a tab group that holds all tabs of a window is not affected either: `removeTabGroup()` runs `beforeunload` first and does not close the window.
- This can explain some reports in bug 1330633. Bug 2073206 comment 0 describes the same result ("Ctrl+Shift+N restores the window with all its tabs").

Possible fix: set `_maybeDontRestoreTabs` only after the window has really closed, or clear it when the close is cancelled.
state.summary: Window is missing after restart if closing all its tabs was cancelled at a "Leave page" prompt

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:158.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/158.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Firefox 158.0 (64-bit) on macOS while signed in to a Mozilla account.
2. Enable the native Firefox VPN (IP Protection) feature.
3. Use the VPN for some time. The connection worked intermittently.
4. Disable the VPN through the Firefox interface.
5. Attempt to open any website in Firefox.

**Troubleshooting performed:**
- Changed `network.proxy.type` from 5 to 0 – no improvement.
- Changed `network.trr.mode` from 0 to 5 – no improvement.
- Started Firefox in Troubleshoot Mode – websites loaded normally.
- Set `browser.ipProtection.enabled` to `false` in `about:config` – normal browsing was immediately restored.

### Actual results

After disabling the built-in VPN, Firefox stopped loading all websites. Pages remained in a continuous loading state without displaying content or an error message.

The internet connection itself was working correctly, and other browsers on the same computer had no connectivity issues.

The problem persisted after restarting Firefox and adjusting proxy and DNS settings.

Normal browsing was only restored after completely disabling the built-in VPN feature by setting `browser.ipProtection.enabled` to `false`.

### Expected results

After disabling the built-in Firefox VPN through the user interface, Firefox should immediately resume normal browsing using the regular internet connection.

All websites should load normally without requiring changes to advanced configuration settings (`about:config`) or restarting Firefox.

The VPN feature should be capable of being enabled and disabled without affecting normal browser connectivity.
state.summary: Firefox 158.0 on macOS stops loading all websites after disabling built-in VPN (IP Protection)

Reproducible back through the initial Split View release in Firefox 149.

STR
1. Create a split view and a few more normal tabs
2. Start dragging the split view from one of its tabs
3. Drag so that the inactive tab in the split view overlaps a normal tab
4. The tab label text of the inactive tab in the split view overlaps the tab label text of the normal tab

In most drag scenarios, we have an opaque background on the dragged object in our default themes:
1. a dragged tab is always active and therefore has an opaque background
2. multi-selected tabs use the active tab opaque background
3. tab group labels are always opaque

An active split view wrapper's background uses the tab hover color, which is translucent. That's good for showing the tab strip's background, but it allows tab text to overlap while dragging tabs.

Occurs with light/dark modes, default themes, and several AMO themes that I tried.

I think this is a minor visual issue and making an opaque background for active split view wrappers would have some visual/design tradeoffs. Maybe it could get an opaque background only while dragging.

state.description:
Follow-up to bug 2069796.

`selectIcons()` in `FaviconLoader.sys.mjs` picks, besides the tab icon, a rich icon that is stored in Places for surfaces showing large icons (e.g. New Tab). The candidates are the icons the page declared as rich (`apple-touch-icon`, `fluid-icon`) plus `rel="icon"` icons whose declared width is at least `FAVICON_RICH_ICON_MIN_WIDTH` (96), and the one with the largest declared width wins. The declared width is computed by `extractIconSize()`.

This has a few problems:

1. `extractIconSize()` only looks at the first token of `sizes`. An ICO correctly declaring all its frames, e.g. `sizes="16x16 32x32 48x48 256x256"`, gets a width of 16 and is never a candidate, while the same ICO declared as `sizes="256x256"` is. The width should be the largest of the declared sizes.

2. `rel="icon"` icons without `sizes`, or with `sizes="any"` (common for SVG), get a width of -1 and are never candidates, even if they are actually large (e.g. a 512px PNG, or a scalable SVG). Declared rich icons without `sizes` are instead accepted with the same -1 width.

3. On equal declared widths the first declared icon wins, while for the tab icon selection the last declared one wins ("When multiple icons are in the same set, the latest wins").

Expected: the rich icon pick considers all declared sizes, handles scalable and unsized icons consistently, and uses the same tie-breaking as the tab icon selection.
state.summary: Large page icons are not picked as rich icon when `sizes` lists several sizes or is missing

state.description:
Bug 1470570 made the full installer resolve a relative `/INI=` path against the directory that holds the installer EXE, for deployment tools like SCCM that stage the installer in a directory whose path isn't known in advance. Looking at the code, that resolution only seems to happen in one of the two places that read the INI file.

1. `InstallOnInitCommon` in `toolkit/mozapps/installer/windows/nsis/common.nsh` runs from `.onInit`. It reads `/INI=` again and checks `${FileExists} "$R7"` on the raw value, without the `$EXEDIR` resolution. This is the code that turns on silent mode and reads most of the `[Install]` keys: `InstallDirectoryName`, `InstallDirectoryPath`, `DesktopShortcut`, `StartMenuShortcut(s)`, `TaskbarShortcut`, `PrivateBrowsingShortcut`, `MaintenanceService`, `RegisterDefaultAgent`, `DesktopLauncher` and `OptionalExtensions`.
2. The `-InstallStartCleanup` section in `browser/installer/windows/nsis/installer.nsi` does resolve the path, but it only reads `RemoveDistributionDir` and `PreventRebootRequired`.

So when the installer's working directory differs from the directory the EXE is in, a relative `/INI=` path most likely fails the `FileExists` check in `.onInit`. The installer then doesn't switch to silent mode and ignores every setting except those two.

I found this by reading the code and haven't confirmed it by running the installer.

Steps to reproduce (expected, not yet tested):
1. Put `Firefox Setup.exe` and `config.ini` (for example with `InstallDirectoryPath=C:\FirefoxTest`) in `C:\stage`.
2. From a different directory, for example `C:\`, run `C:\stage\"Firefox Setup.exe" /INI=config.ini`.

Expected: a silent install into `C:\FirefoxTest`.
Actual (probably): the installer UI appears, or the install goes to the default location with default shortcuts.

A fix would most likely move the relative path resolution into `InstallOnInitCommon` (or a shared macro that both places use). `FullConfig.md` should also mention relative paths once this works.
state.summary: Full installer ignores most settings from a relative /INI= path unless run from the installer directory

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:156.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/156.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. Updated Firefox through APT from the Mozilla Team Ubuntu PPA.
2. Continued using Firefox after the version update.
3. Opened `about:newtab` with Recommended Stories enabled.
4. The stories were initially missing and later appeared in English, although Firefox was configured to use German.
5. Opened the Browser Toolbox and inspected the request to:
   `https://merino.services.mozilla.com/api/v1/curated-recommendations`
6. The request payload contained `"locale":"en-US"` and `"region":"DE"`.
7. In the same failing Firefox session, evaluated:
   `Services.locale.appLocaleAsBCP47`
   which returned `"de"`.
8. Tried `Refresh Cache`, `Sync Remote Settings`, and `Expire Cache` followed by `Refresh Cache` in `about:newtab#devtools`. New Merino requests still used `"locale":"en-US"`.
9. Completely terminated Firefox and started it again.
10. Repeated the Merino request inspection. It now contained `"locale":"de"` and `"region":"DE"`.

### Actual results

After the Firefox update, Recommended Stories were displayed in English.

During the failing state, the Merino request payload contained:

```json id="xb27mm"
{
  "inferredInterests": null,
  "locale": "en-US",
  "region": "DE",
  "topics": [],
  "sections": [],
  "enableInterestPicker": false
}
```

At the same time:

```js id="blbx1f"
Services.locale.appLocaleAsBCP47
```

returned `"de"`.

Therefore, Firefox's current application locale was `de`, but Discovery Stream continued sending `en-US` to Merino.

Refreshing or expiring the Discovery Stream cache and synchronizing Remote Settings did not correct the locale.

Only after completely terminating and restarting Firefox did the Merino payload change to `"locale":"de"`. German Recommended Stories were then returned.

### Expected results

Discovery Stream should use the current Firefox application locale when requesting Recommended Stories.

If:

```js id="yqqydf"
Services.locale.appLocaleAsBCP47 === "de"
```

and the region is `DE`, the Merino request should use:

```json id="7whm2h"
"locale": "de",
"region": "DE"
```

The locale used for the Merino request should not remain `en-US` after Firefox's effective application locale is already `de`, and an additional complete Firefox restart should not be required.
state.summary: Discovery Stream sends en-US to Merino after update although app locale is de

state.description:
The `trackerCount` setting in about:preferences (`privacy.mjs`) awaits `TrackingDBService.getEventsByDateRange` from page code. If the tab is closed while that query is pending, the query's promise chain keeps the page's window alive until the query completes. On slow Linux debug runs this makes [`browser_policy_trackingprotection.js`](https://tests.firefox.dev/test.html?test=browser/components/enterprisepolicies/tests/browser/trackingprotection/browser_policy_trackingprotection.js) fail intermittently with "leaked 1 window(s) until shutdown [url = about:preferences#etp]".

The fix: `PrivacyMetricsService` runs the query and reports the result through a callback that the setting registers. When the page unloads, the setting clears that callback, so the pending query no longer references the page and the window can be freed.
state.summary: Closed about:preferences window stays alive until its tracker count query finishes

state.description:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Use any profile created/last-migrated by Firefox ≤ 153 that has the four default containers. Its `containers.json` contains `"l10nId":"user-context-personal"` (and `-work`, `-banking`, `-shopping`) — **without** the trailing `2`. This is true at both `"version":5` and `"version":6`.
2. Open that profile in Nightly 158.0a1.
3. Install any extension that calls `browser.contextualIdentities.query({})` (e.g. PassFF, Multi-Account Containers) and trigger that call.

## Actual result

Console shows:

```
[fluent] Missing message in locale en-US: user-context-personal
[fluent] Couldn't find a message: user-context-personal
can't access property "attributes", msg is null   ContextualIdentityService.sys.mjs:790
```

The `contextualIdentities` API call rejects with the opaque message **"An unexpected error occurred"**, with nothing identifying containers as the cause.

## Expected result

The API resolves. An unresolvable `l10nId` should degrade gracefully, not throw.

## Root cause

Two independent defects combine.

**1. No migration rewrites the interim Fluent IDs.**

`migrate4to5` switches on `identity.l10nID` — the *legacy StringBundle* property (capital `D`, values like `userContextPersonal.label`):

```js
for (let identity of data.identities) {
  switch (identity.l10nID) {                        // legacy property, capital D
    case "userContextPersonal.label":
      identity.l10nId = "user-context-personal2";
      break;
    ...
  }
  delete identity.l10nID;
```

Profiles that already store the *interim Fluent* value in lowercase `l10nId` (`"user-context-personal"`) match no case, so nothing is rewritten. `migrate5to6` only canonicalises container **colors**. No migration path exists from `user-context-personal` → `user-context-personal2`, so affected profiles stay broken permanently — including at the current `LAST_CONTAINERS_JSON_VERSION = 6`.

**2. `formatContextLabel()` has no null guard.**

```js
formatContextLabel(l10nId) {
  const [msg] = lazy.l10n.formatMessagesSync([l10nId]);
  for (let attr of msg.attributes) {   // msg is null when the ID is unknown
```

`formatMessagesSync` yields `null` for an unknown ID, so this throws a TypeError. The two call sites guard only against a *falsy* `l10nId` (`return l10nId ? this.formatContextLabel(l10nId) : ""`), not against an ID that is present but unresolvable.

## Why it escalates to a full API failure

`ext-contextualIdentities.js:48` builds every identity's `name` via `getUserContextLabel()`:

```js
name: ContextualIdentityService.getUserContextLabel(identity.userContextId),
```

One stale ID therefore fails the *whole* `query({})` call, so every container-aware extension breaks, not just the affected container.

## Confirming the locale rename

- **ESR 153.3.0** (`omni.ja` → `localization/en-US/toolkit/global/contextual-identity.ftl`) defines `user-context-personal`, `-work`, `-banking`, `-shopping`.
- **Nightly 158.0a1** defines **only** `user-context-personal2`, `-work2`, `-banking2`, `-shopping2`.

So any profile written by a Firefox that used the non-`2` IDs breaks on current Nightly.

## Suggested fix

1. Add a migration (bump `LAST_CONTAINERS_JSON_VERSION` to 7) mapping `user-context-{personal,work,banking,shopping}` → the `*2` IDs.
2. Make `formatContextLabel()` defensive:

```js
formatContextLabel(l10nId) {
  const [msg] = lazy.l10n.formatMessagesSync([l10nId]);
  if (!msg?.attributes) {
    return "";
  }
  ...
```

Fix 2 alone stops the API-wide breakage; fix 1 is needed to restore the correct labels.

## Workaround

With Firefox closed, append `2` to the four `l10nId` values in `<profile>/containers.json`.

## Environment

- Firefox Nightly 158.0a1, BuildID 20260916094607, rev `ace91b8723d2cf52a5d35225c65e0321a6390839`
- Linux (Debian 13, Wayland)
- Affected profile `containers.json` was at `"version":6` with the old IDs — i.e. fully migrated yet still broken
state.summary: Stale `l10nId` values in `containers.json` crash `ContextualIdentityService.formatContextLabel()`, breaking the entire `browser.contextualIdentities` WebExtension API

state.description:
The invariant "a tab state may only reference tab groups defined in its own
window" is maintained by the writer and is not checked anywhere on the read side.
Only the writer keeps it true; every reader assumes it.

Where state enters without validation:
- SessionFile parses the state as JSON and checks the version, nothing else.
- session.schema.json defines no relationship between a tab's groupId and the
  window's groups; the window definition does not even require groups.
- the raw state can be rewritten by sessionstore-state-read observers before it is
  parsed and reused.
- SessionMigration reads another profile's file and reproduces the same shape.

Readers that assume the invariant (four, in different code paths):
- SessionStore.sys.mjs:7957 - #prepDataForDeferredRestore
- SessionMigration.sys.mjs:58 - profile migration
- Tabbrowser.sys.mjs:5204 - createTabsForSessionRestore (window restore)
- SessionStore.sys.mjs:2470 - #saveOpenTabGroupsOnClose (window close)

Consequences when a reference does not resolve:
- Window restore aborts at that tab and every later tab of the window is dropped.
  The fallback for this one path is bug 2080608 / D332744.
- In a deferred session the failure escalates instead of aborting: #initSession
  returns the unprepared state and #initializeWindow restores from it, so a
  DEFER_SESSION launch (automatic restore switched off) becomes a full automatic
  restore of every window, cookies included.

Proposed direction: normalize unresolvable groupIds once where the state enters,
the way #migrateSplitViewIds already normalizes invalid splitViewIds. That covers
all four readers instead of the single path the fallback patches.

On prevalence: no naturally occurring case is known. The fallback in bug 2080608
was driven by a malformed input produced by a third-party session-file rewriter, so
this bug is about the read side being unable to detect or repair an inconsistent
state from any source, not about an observed Firefox write path.
state.summary: Session restore trusts tab group references without validating them on load

The origin controls items an extension's toolbar button adds (Only When Clicked, Always Allow on <host>, On All Sites, Allow on Restricted Sites; `originControls.ftl` defines no accesskeys, `ExtensionsUI.sys.mjs` `originControlsMenu` builds them) and Turn on/off Vertical Tabs and Customize Sidebar have no accesskey, while the rest of the menu does.

Bug 2073853 adds an automation check: a menupopup or panel-list that opens with two visible items sharing an accesskey, or with items lacking one beside items that have one, logs an `AccessKeyConflictError` and fails the running browser-chrome test. This menu carries an `accesskey-conflicts-bug` attribute naming this bug so the check skips it. The fix picks unique letters for static items (a message whose accesskey changes gets a new Fluent id; no migration recipe) and removes the attribute in the same patch so the check guards the menu from then on. Items generated from data can't be given accesskeys, so a menu that mixes them with static items either drops the static items' accesskeys or moves the generated items into a submenu. Conflicts are per visible menu instance, so a letter has to be free among the items that can show together, not merely in the Fluent file.

Steps:
1. With `browser.sessionstore.restore_on_demand` on, restore a tab in the background so it is pending with `about:mozilla` as its current entry.
2. Call `browser.loadURI()` on it with `about:mozilla#frag`.

Expected: the tab stops being pending and loads `about:mozilla#frag`.

Actual: the tab stays pending on the blank placeholder document with its URI rewritten to `about:mozilla#frag` (empty title, `text/html`), and it never restores. Loading `about:robots` instead restores it as expected.

A pending tab's docshell reports the restored URL as its current URI (`SetCurrentURIForSessionStore`), so the load is a same-document navigation. It adds a history entry without a network load, and the restore listener in `SessionStore.sys.mjs` reacts only to `onStartRequest`; its `OnHistoryNewEntry` is empty behind a `TODO(kashav)`. `ContentRestore.sys.mjs`, removed in bug 1886892, handled this in `OnHistoryNewEntry` by resetting the current URI to `about:blank` and starting a real load.

`browser_replace_load.js` covers this case but has been disabled since bug 1646894. Its setup also waits on `promiseBrowserLoaded` for a tab added with `about:blank`, which never fires a load now.
state.summary: Pending tab stays blank and never restores when loaded with a URL that differs only in its fragment

state.description:
Several telemetry functions iterate over `Services.wm.getEnumerator("navigator:browser")`, which already lists a new window before its `gBrowser` exists. Collecting tab counts, tab group stats or the site origin count while a window is opening throws:

```
TypeError: can't access property "tabs", win.gBrowser is undefined
```

This happens in `getOpenTabsAndWinsCounts`, `getPinnedTabsCount` and the tab group telemetry in `BrowserUsageTelemetry.sys.mjs`, and in `BrowserTelemetryUtils.computeSiteOriginCount`.

User impact: the sample collected while another window opens is lost, e.g. when opening a window or popup while tabs are loading elsewhere.

On CI it was logged 14,492 times in 5,377 jobs, from 110 tests, out of the 31,690 mozilla-central mochitest jobs of 2026-10-15 in the errors dashboard (https://tests.firefox.dev/errors.html?kind=mochitest#date=2026-10-15).

Skipping windows without a `gBrowser` would be enough.
state.summary: Tab telemetry throws 'win.gBrowser is undefined' while a browser window is opening

state.description:
With vertical tabs enabled, File > Close Window is hidden. This shows on macOS, where the menubar is always available, and on other platforms when the menubar is opened from the keyboard.

`tab-bar-visibility.js` hides `menu_closeWindow` and gives `menu_close` the label "Close" when `hideTabsToolbar` is true, which was meant for windows that only ever hold one tab, such as popups. Since bug 1915739, `hideTabsToolbar` is also true with vertical tabs, which hold any number of tabs.

The "Close" label never shows: the File menu's `popupshowing` handler (`updateTabCloseCountState` in `browser.js`) always replaces it with `menu-file-close-tab`, so a popup window shows "Close Tab" too. Both messages `tab-bar-visibility.js` sets lack an accesskey.

The fix could base both on the single-tab window condition instead of `hideTabsToolbar`, and choose the label in `updateTabCloseCountState` with a message that has an accesskey.
state.summary: File menu has no Close Window item when vertical tabs are enabled

state.description:
Right now, when we ship a partner distribution, a special string "Distributed by { name of partner }" is added to the about dialog.

Currently, this string and any translations of the string live outside the tree, and tend to be machine-generated.

(Note that we only allowlist a small number of locales for a typical partner repack, so this is not a major problem.)

However I think we could improve on the current situation:
* move the string "Distributed by { partner }" in tree, so that it gets localized, and so we have graceful localization fallback  (say, from `de-de` to `de`)
* start setting the name of the partner in a specific pref as part of the repack pref setting process
* update the repack docs to mention this pref
* update the about dialog code to render the string using code in-tree

If we decide to do this, we'll also need to migrate all current partner repacks to add the missing pref so that the string renders correctly.

:mkaply, what do you think? would this be worth doing?
state.summary: Move about dialog string "Distributed by {partner}" in-tree

state.description:
When hovering a tab whose content reports a width or document height of 0, `PageThumbs.captureTabPreviewThumbnail` computes an infinite scale and `drawSnapshot` throws. The tab preview logs:

```
TypeError: WindowGlobalParent.drawSnapshot: Argument 2 is not a finite floating-point value.
```

Also, `drawSnapshot` on the browser element (`browser-custom-element.mjs`) is documented to return false on failure, but it returns the promise without awaiting it, so its catch never runs and callers get a rejected promise instead.

User impact: no thumbnail is shown for these tabs, which is expected, but every hover logs an error to the browser console.

On CI it was logged 64,833 times in 2,613 jobs, from 65 tests, out of the 26,201 mochitest jobs of 2026-10-08 in the errors dashboard (https://tests.firefox.dev/errors.html?data-source=try&kind=mochitest). Mostly tab strip tests that hover tabs. I haven't checked which tabs report a size of 0, but they're presumably background or blank tabs whose content hasn't been laid out yet.
state.summary: 'drawSnapshot: Argument 2 is not a finite floating-point value' error when hovering some tabs

```

On CI it was logged 23,310 times in 1,239 jobs, from 8 tests, out of the 26,201 mochitest jobs of 2026-10-08 in the errors dashboard (https://tests.firefox.dev/errors.html?data-source=try&kind=mochitest). Mostly private browsing tests, which change these prefs after closing private windows.

state.description:
Environment
Firefox 159.0 release, build 20261023105132.
Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Resolute Raccoon).
Linux kernel 7.0.0-42-generic (x86_64), X11.
Intel Core i9-12900H, 20 logical CPUs.

Symptoms and reproduction
During ordinary browsing with Firefox left open, high CPU spikes occur intermittently, a few times per week at most. Firefox's own about:processes page has shown about 380% CPU. The trigger is unknown and there is no deterministic reproducer.

Profile
https://share.firefox.dev/3WLCInw

Over approximately 7.09 seconds of sampled activity in parent process 9258:
- Process CPU counter averages approximately 325% (100% = one logical CPU).
- sqldb:places.sqlite #4: approximately 6.91 CPU-seconds, or 97% of one logical CPU, executing the shortcut-ranking SQL query.
- GeckoMain: approximately 6.83 CPU-seconds, or 96% of one logical CPU, with UI/localization and task processing.
- glean.dispatcher: approximately 6.78 CPU-seconds, or 96% of one logical CPU, serializing and committing its metrics database.
- Other threads combined: approximately 36%, estimated as the remainder of the process CPU counter after the three threads above.

The process average is therefore approximately 325%, equivalent to 3.25 logical CPUs. The approximately 380% reading in Firefox's about:processes page is a separate observation; it is not the recording's average. The Places query accounts for approximately one logical CPU. The recording also shows substantial concurrent main-thread and Glean activity, but it does not establish that shortcut ranking causes that activity.

The Places thread spends almost all its CPU under a Connection::stepStatement SQL frame. Its truncated SQL label starts with WITH input_keys(guid), contains 14 input GUIDs, joins moz_places without an alias, then selects place_ids.guid AS key. This matches fetchShortcutInteractions in SmartShortcutsRanker/RankShortcuts.mjs at the captured build revision:
https://hg.mozilla.org/releases/mozilla-release/file/5add844c26613d7e4d84c799d6e23cf987b1240d/browser/extensions/newtab/lib/SmartShortcutsRanker/RankShortcuts.mjs#l617

That query aggregates shortcut clicks/impressions from moz_newtab_shortcuts_interaction over the last two months. SQLite strftimeFunc appears in approximately 63% of the database thread's CPU-weighted stacks.

Expected
Refreshing shortcut rankings should not keep a database thread at almost one full core throughout this recording.

Scope and related reports
This report focuses on the Places query; it does not claim this query explains all process CPU. Glean is concurrently committing/serializing its metrics database, and the main thread is busy with UI/localization/task processing.

Bug 2042142 concerns a different query, fetchLast10VisitsByGuid, in the same ranking module:
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2042142

Disabling shortcut personalization and its interaction feed, while keeping ordinary shortcuts enabled, is being tried. It is too early to determine whether that prevents recurrence.
state.summary: Smart Shortcuts fetchShortcutInteractions query consumes a core during intermittent high CPU (Firefox 159/Linux)

state.description:
A local user can bypass the 3rdparty enterprise policy by editing a file in their home directory. It requires the administrator to have omitted the target extension's ID from the policy's Extensions map.

## Impact

`3rdparty` delivers admin-authored configuration to named extension IDs, and the extension reads it back through `browser.storage.managed`. For any ID the administrator did not enumerate, that read falls through to a native manifest resolver whose first search location is a directory the user owns. The user can therefore choose what a managed-storage-consuming extension believes its administrator configured -- or, by simply not creating the file, make it believe it has no managed configuration at all.

The extension most worth targeting is exactly the one an administrator is most likely to forget to enumerate: a security add-on that receives its policy through the root-only system manifest directory, or one that is expected to ship with no managed config. Its enforcement settings become user-chosen.

This is one defect reached two ways, not two defects:

- the administrator delivered nothing for that ID, and the user supplies values that were never intended to exist;
- the administrator delivered the ID's configuration through the root-only system manifest directory, and the user's home-directory file shadows the root-owned one.

No enterprise policy closes this. Nothing governs the native managed-storage manifest directories. A policy that enumerates every managed-storage-consuming extension ID is not affected, because for a configured ID the in-memory policy wins and the user's file is never read -- that precedence defence was tested and holds.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy `3rdparty` with `Extensions` naming some ID, e.g. `{"copycat@example.com": {"adminSecret": "ADMIN_VALUE", "enforce": true}}`, and confirm the policy is active.
2. Pick an extension ID that consumes `browser.storage.managed` but is *not* a key of that map.
3. As the ordinary user, create `~/.mozilla/managed-storage/<extension-id>.json` containing:

        {"name": "<extension-id>", "description": "x", "type": "storage",
         "data": {"policyKey": "attacker-value"}}

4. Have the extension call `browser.storage.managed.get()`. It receives the user's values.
5. Variant: repeat for an ID whose configuration the administrator delivered as a root-owned `/usr/lib/mozilla/managed-storage/<id>.json`. The home-directory file is found first.

## Root cause

`lookupManagedStorage` (`toolkit/components/extensions/parent/ext-storage.js:82-98`) asks the policy engine first and early-returns when it gets an object, but `getExtensionPolicy` (`toolkit/components/enterprisepolicies/EnterprisePoliciesParent.sys.mjs:1159-1163`) is an exact-match lookup that returns `null` for anything absent from the map. The `null` is treated as "no opinion" rather than "not managed", so execution falls through to `NativeManifests.lookupManifest("storage", id)`.

That resolver searches `XREUserNativeManifests` before `XRESysNativeManifests` (`toolkit/components/extensions/NativeManifests.sys.mjs:36-43`), `_tryPaths` returns the first hit (`:182-192`), and `XREUserNativeManifests` is forced to `~/.mozilla` on Linux (`toolkit/xre/nsXREDirProvider.cpp:417-427`). Storage manifests carry no `allowed_extensions` requirement -- that field is only checked when present (`NativeManifests.sys.mjs:143-150`) -- so every validity check is trivially satisfied by a file the user wrote.

The policy's whole footprint is the in-memory injection at `onBeforeAddons` (`browser/components/enterprisepolicies/Policies.sys.mjs:160-164`); it sets no pref and takes no position on the manifest directories, so there is nothing for a companion policy to lock.

## Suggested fix

Make the user-writable directory lose to administrator delivery for `storage` manifests: search the system directory first for `type: "storage"`, or ignore the user directory for storage manifests entirely while an enterprise po
state.summary: User-level managed storage manifests take precedence over system-level ones

Description:
Reordering containers in the "Containers" settings page (about:preferences#containers) does not always reorder them in the Multi-Account Containers (M-AC) main panel. This issue appears to be intermittent. 
Conversely, changing the container order within the M-AC panel always updates the order in Firefox correctly.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Ensure Multi-Account Containers (version 8.3.9) is installed
2. Navigate to about:preferences#containers and start reordering the containers in Firefox. After each change, open the M-AC extension panel to check if the order matches
3. Observe that at some point, the order stops syncing (i.e., reordering in Firefox is no longer reflected in M-AC)
4. Reorder the containers in Firefox back to match M-AC to re-establish a baseline
5. Start reordering containers directly inside the M-AC extension panel
6. Observe that the containers in Firefox are updated correctly every time

Expected results:
Reordering containers in Firefox should always reliably reorder them in the M-AC panel

Actual results:
Reordering containers in Firefox intermittently fails to update the container order in the M-AC panel
state.summary: Intermittent sync issue when reordering containers from Firefox to Multi-Account Containers

**[Notes]**
Since the experiment's Population % is set to a low percentage (1% in this case), we have encountered issues in enrolling in the experiment due to the bucket sampling. In this case, the Browser Console may show:
 - search-widget-m did not match bucket sampling

In this case, we need to obtain a different bucket assignment using the following steps (after Step 3):
- Close Firefox.
- Open the Firefox profile directory.
- Delete the Datareporting folder.
- Restart Firefox.
- Check about:studies to see if the profile has enrolled in the experiment.

You may need to repeat the process until the profile is assigned to the experiment's population.

**[Affected versions]:**
- Firefox Release 157.0 - Build ID: 20260924084938

**[Affected Platforms]:**
 - Windows 10 x64
- Linux Mint 22.2
- macOS 26.6.2

**[Prerequisites]:**
- Have Firefox Release 157.0 build installed/extracted, using any locale.
- Have the "user.js" file from [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1yaFlBnWi01Rfsgm4SkmUEJBnEOgyzJS3/view?usp=sharing) downloaded to your PC.

**[Steps to reproduce]:**
1. Open the profile from the prerequisites.
2. Navigate to “about:preferences#search” and change the default search engine to any search engine, except Google or Bing.
3. Go to the profile folder and paste the "user.js" file from the prerequisites.
4. Restart the browser.
5. Navigate to the "about:studies" page and check the contents of the page.

**[Expected result]:**
- The “Search Widget - M” experiment is correctly NOT displayed in the "Active studies" section.

**[Actual result]:**
- The “Search Widget - M” delivery is marked as active.
- The title "Search Widget - M" and the description "Search Widget" are displayed.

**[Additional notes]:**
- According to the [received documentation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1e2zXsEYXJuP_OUvB5qwkmAVuhBhyb3n4szWLwT2D5yk/edit?tab=t.whdgrhm26r4w#heading=h.w12zdisd47d9), the Search Widget - M/L experiments are intended to enroll only users whose default search engine is Google or Bing.
- However, the search engine requirement is stated only in the documentation and is not included in the experiment's targeting expression.
- This issue is reproducible on both [Search Widget - M](https://experimenter.services.mozilla.com/nimbus/search-widget-m/summary/) and [Search Widget - L](https://experimenter.services.mozilla.com/nimbus/search-widget-l/summary/) experiments.
state.summary: [Experiment] Search Widget - M/L - The client is enrolled in the experiment if the search engine is not set to Bing or Google since the search engine eligibility targeting is not set in the recipe

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:157.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/157.0

### Steps to reproduce

- Open a new Firefox session. 
- Go to any website where you can upload a file (generally a picture/image file) to share it, the path is supposedly the last one used to upload something for there.
- Download a file (ie right click, "save image as"), saving it in the downloads folder (ie. Downloads, being my default folder).

### Actual results

- As I upload a new file in a website, the last upload folder path is redirected to the Downloads folder. A few clicks here and there, I choose another folder (ie. from "Documents"), and the file uploads, fine.
- I then upload a new file, and the last upload folder is redirected to the Downloads folder, again.
- Closing the browser, resets this behavior, but once you download a new file, the upload path is changed to the Downloads folder, once again.

### Expected results

The upload folder path should be the last folder that Firefox remembers from the website I am uploading the file for (or _websites_, as I found out that, right now at this moment in Firefox 157.0, it's the same last folder path for every website I have used before; it doesn't matter which one I have used, it's the same upload path), not my Downloads folder. 

The paths from upload files shouldn't be crashing/colliding with the downloads folder path (unless I am uploading a file from the Downloads folder) as I download a new file (saved there or in any other folder), nor should be defaulting to it after I am uploading a file from anywhere else. I previously tested this as well in another profile, and the behavior remains the same. 

My observation is that this might be something provoked in Firefox 157.0, since the previous Firefox version (156.0.1, I believe?) wasn't behaving like this.
state.summary: Last upload folder paths not being remembered in specific websites (all sharing the same upload folder path), then defaulting to the downloads folder after saving a file in there, in Firefox 157.0

Created attachment 9649553
Demonstration video with Firefox 156's vertical tabs sidebar - proportions problem with many pinned tabs

This is kind of the opposite (but complementary) issue to bug #2033306.

When you have tons of pinned tabs, and you collapse the sidebar into a thin column, the pinned tabs auto-position the draggable separator to the maximum required to fit them all, regardless of how many normal tabs you have open, making it a scrollfest where it is nearly impossible to see normal tabs.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable vertical tabs mode
2. Open a ton of normal tabs (let's say, a hundred)
3. Pin a lot of tabs (let's say 15 to 30 pinned tabs)
4. Toggle the vertical tabs sidebar's compact mode, by using the toolbar's "Collapse sidebar" button or using `Alt+Ctrl+Z`

## Actual Results

See attached video: the numerous pinned tabs expand to fill nearly the entire height of the collapsed sidebar, leaving very little manoeuvering room for normal tabs.

## Expected results

I think there should be some sort of upper limit / proportionality rule for the auto-positioning of the movable separator divider widget when toggling to collapsed mode, when there are enough "normal" tabs (vs pinned tabs) to warrant it. Or maybe it should maintain the same ratio as what the user had set in expanded mode (again, "when there are enough normal tabs to fill the space below").
state.summary: When toggling sidebar's collapsed mode, pinned vertical tabs have no height limitation for the divider separating them from normal tabs

Created attachment 9661435
firefox-fullscreen-dialog-test.html

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:158.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/158.0

### Steps to reproduce

When a web page enters DOM fullscreen mode using the Fullscreen API, native JavaScript dialogs opened by alert() or confirm() are not immediately visible in Firefox.
The page appears unresponsive until Escape is pressed. After Escape exits fullscreen, the pending dialog becomes visible.
The problem is reproducible in a standalone HTML document without WordPress, Leaflet, or third-party libraries.
Steps to reproduce
1. Open the attached standalone HTML test case in Firefox on Windows 11.
2. Click "Vollbild starten".
3. Click "alert() testen".
4. Observe that the dialog does not appear immediately.
5. Press Escape.
6. Observe that the dialog becomes visible after fullscreen has been exited.
7. Repeat with "confirm() testen".

### Actual results

Both native dialogs remain invisible while the page is in DOM fullscreen. Pressing Escape makes the dialog visible.

Environment
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, Version 24H2
- OS build: 26100.9711
- Windows Feature Experience Pack: 1000.26100.372.0
- Firefox: 158.0
- Build ID: 20261007201254
- Chrome: 155.0.8059.80 (Official Build) (64-bit)

Additional information
The issue was also observed in Firefox 157.0. In normal window mode, both dialogs appear immediately. A custom DOM dialog displayed inside the fullscreen element works correctly.
Chrome displays the dialogs immediately, but fullscreen is exited when the dialog is dismissed. This is included as an observation, not as a claim of a specification violation.

### Expected results

The native dialog should become visible without requiring the user to press Escape to exit fullscreen first.
state.summary: Native alert() and confirm() dialogs are not visible in DOM fullscreen until Escape is pressed

state.description:
This bug tracks one cluster of the meta bug 2073353 (see bug 2073353 comment 16). It has 9 reports in the last 30 days and 44 in the last 180 days. It is still active on 158.0, 159.0 and ESR 140. This is the stack originally reported in bug 2073353 comment 0.

Example crash: https://crash-stats.mozilla.org/report/index/cd0b4930-b4d6-4130-9c41-a642b0261029 (Firefox 159.0, Windows 10.0.19045)

MOZ_CRASH Reason: `Shutdown hanging at step XPCOMWillShutdown. Something is blocking the main-thread.`

Main thread stack:
```
0  ntdll.dll  NtAlpcSendWaitReceivePort
1  LRPC_BASE_CCALL::SendReceive(_RPC_MESSAGE*)
...
6  EP_LOOKUP_DATA::LookupNextChunk(void)
7  EP_LOOKUP_DATA::ResolveEndpoint(...)
8  ResolveEndpointWithEpMapper
9  ResolveEndpointIfNecessary
...
13 LRPC_FAST_BINDING_HANDLE::Bind(_RPC_ASYNC_STATE*, void*)
14 RpcBindingBind
15 BindToServer(void*, void*)  onecore\admin\appmodel\packagemanager\client\helpers.cpp:133
16 CreateAndBindRpcBindingHandle(void*, void**)
17 PrepareForRpcCall(RpcCallPreparationOptions)
18 DoRpcCall<...>(...)
19 Windows::Management::Deployment::PackageManager::FindPackagesByUserSecurityIdWithPackageTypes(...)
20 Windows::Management::Deployment::PackageManager::FindPackagesByUserSecurityId(...)
21 mozilla::toolkit::system::nsWindowsPackageManager::FindUserInstalledPackages(nsTArray<nsTString<char16_t> > const&, nsTArray<nsTString<char16_t> >&)  toolkit/system/windowsPackageManager/nsWindowsPackageManager.cpp:67
22 XPTC__InvokebyIndex()
23 XPCWrappedNative::CallMethod(XPCCallContext&, XPCWrappedNative::CallMode)
24 XPC_WN_CallMethod(JSContext*, unsigned int, JS::Value*)
25 js::Interpret(JSContext*, js::RunState&)
26 JS::RunJSMicroTask(JSContext*, JS::Handle<mozilla::Maybe<JS::MicroTask> >)
27 mozilla::RunMicroTask(...)
28 NS_ProcessNextEvent(nsIThread*, bool)
29 nsThreadManager::SpinEventLoopUntilInternal(nsTSubstring<char> const&, nsINestedEventLoopCondition*, mozilla::ShutdownPhase)
...
38 nsObserverService::NotifyObservers(nsISupports*, char const*, char16_t const*)
39 mozilla::AppShutdown::AdvanceShutdownPhaseInternal(...)  xpcom/base/AppShutdown.cpp:486
40 nsXREDirProvider::DoShutdown()
...
```

`nsWindowsPackageManager::FindUserInstalledPackages` calls `PackageManager::FindPackagesByUserSecurityId` synchronously on the main thread. That call binds to the AppX deployment service over RPC with no timeout. It is reached from `collectInstallationTelemetry` in `browser/modules/BrowserUsageTelemetry.sys.mjs` (through `findUserInstalledPackages`), which can still be running as a JS microtask when the main thread spins the event loop during shutdown. When the deployment service does not respond, shutdown stays blocked until the watchdog kills the process.

The metrics that require this call are no longer needed (see bug 2073353 comment 2). The patch "Remove unused metrics that cause shutdown hangs", attached to bug 2073353, should move to this bug. It was backed out three times, for failures in `test_mirrors.py`, an MSIX xpcshell test and `browser_all_files_referenced.js` (see bug 2073353 comments 6, 7, 10, 11 and 14).
state.summary: Shutdown hang in [@ shutdownhang | NtAlpcSendWaitReceivePort] in nsWindowsPackageManager::FindUserInstalledPackages during shutdown

state.description:
In `share-tab-popup` and the content area's share submenu, the provider items `SharingUtils.sys.mjs` builds from `MacSharingService` (AirDrop, Mail, Messages, …) are generated from data and have no accesskey; More… (`menu-share-more`) and More Options (`menu-share-windows`) are static and need a key beside Copy Links (L) and the QR code item (Q).

Bug 2073853 adds an automation check: a menupopup or panel-list that opens with two visible items sharing an accesskey, or with items lacking one beside items that have one, logs an `AccessKeyConflictError` and fails the running browser-chrome test. This menu carries an `accesskey-conflicts-bug` attribute naming this bug so the check skips it. The fix picks unique letters for static items (a message whose accesskey changes gets a new Fluent id; no migration recipe) and removes the attribute in the same patch so the check guards the menu from then on. Items generated from data can't be given accesskeys, so a menu that mixes them with static items either drops the static items' accesskeys or moves the generated items into a submenu. Conflicts are per visible menu instance, so a letter has to be free among the items that can show together, not merely in the Fluent file.
state.summary: Share menu items from macOS and More… have no accesskey beside Copy Links and QR code

state.description:
`TabNotesController` removes its window listeners (`CanonicalURL:Identified`, `TabNote:*`, the tabs progress listener) only after `TabNotes.deinit()` has closed the database. If `browser.tabs.notes.enabled` is turned back on before the close finishes, the re-enable path adds the listeners first and the stale disable path then removes them, so tab notes stay broken in every window until the next toggle.

On enable and at startup, the listeners are added only after the database has opened, so canonical URLs reported in the meantime are dropped until the later `CanonicalURL:Detect` sweep.

This causes intermittent failures in [browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_note_preview.js](https://tests.firefox.dev/test.html?test=browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_note_preview.js) and [browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_preview.js](https://tests.firefox.dev/test.html?test=browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_preview.js) on linux standalone ("Found an unexpected tab at the end of test run").

Fix: add and remove the window listeners without waiting for the database (`TabNotes` initializes itself lazily). `TabNotes.deinit` forgets its init immediately and also closes a connection whose init is still in flight, and a new init waits for the pending close.
state.summary: Tab notes stop working after browser.tabs.notes.enabled is toggled off and quickly back on

state.description:
`IPPProxyManager.start()` and `stop()` decide whether an activation is already in flight by checking for `IPPProxyStates.ACTIVATING`. `updateState()` does not know about activations and moves the state back to `READY` while one is still running, so a `start()` issued from that state change opens a second activation. The two then race for the one channel filter.

Both methods should key off `#activatingPromise` instead.
state.summary: Calling start() while an activation is already running can open a second activation

state.description:
From claude:
`browser_multiselect_tabs_using_keyboard.js` calls `CustomizableUI.reset()` in its cleanup function. `reset()` sets `sidebar.verticalTabs` to `false`, and nothing sets it back. The browser-chrome harness only records changed prefs (as a todo unless `comparePrefs` is set); it does not restore them.

In the vertical-tabs variant (`--setpref=sidebar.verticalTabs=true`), every test in `browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser.toml` that runs after this one in the same browser therefore runs with horizontal tabs, so the variant is not testing what it claims to for most of that manifest.

Evidence: the `modifiedPrefs.json` artifact from a passing Windows shippable vertical-tabs browser-chrome task (FGsnFIdeRUa9TG_nFa5W0w) lists `sidebar.visibility`, `sidebar.verticalTabs` and `browser.uiCustomization.horizontalTabstrip` against `browser_multiselect_tabs_using_keyboard.js`, and no later test changes `sidebar.verticalTabs` again.

This also hides a real CustomizableUI bug: with a new profile and vertical tabs enabled, the nav-bar is missing `stop-reload-button` and other default buttons (filed separately). `browser_reload_deleted_file.js` passes in CI only because this reset runs first and rebuilds the horizontal defaults. It fails when the browser restarts in between.

Possible fixes:
- Restore `sidebar.verticalTabs` (and the CustomizableUI state for the current orientation) after the reset, or avoid `CustomizableUI.reset()` and just undo the specific `removeWidgetFromArea("developer-button")` change the test makes.
- `browser_drag_to_pin.js` uses the same `CustomizableUI.reset()` cleanup pattern. It is not tagged `vertical-tabs` today, so it does not affect the variant yet, but it would if it were added.
- Longer term, the harness could fail a test that changes a pref the variant sets, so this kind of problem is caught.
state.summary: Stop browser_multiselect_tabs_using_keyboard.js turning off vertical tabs for the rest of the vertical-tabs test run

state.description:
While working on [bug 2081441](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2081441) I found that if ConfirmationHint.show() gets called a second time while a hint is still opening, it ends up starting two auto-hide timers, and only one of them gets cleaned up when the hint closes. The leftover one fires about 3 seconds later and closes whatever hint is open at that point, so a later hint can disappear almost right after it shows up.

It looks like show() handles the hint being closed or fully open, but not the in-between "showing" state.

**Steps to reproduce:**

This is a timing issue (the second hint has to be triggered within a fraction of a second of the first), so it's hard to hit by hand. The easiest way to see it is with the test from bug 2081441, so it would likely be verified with further automated tests:

1. In browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_group_menu.js, remove the wait for the hint to open inside the loop in test_saveAndCloseGroup_confirmationHintCappedAtThree. That test saves and closes several tab groups back to back, so the second hint gets triggered while the first is still opening.
2. Run ./mach test browser/components/tabbrowser/test/browser/tabs/browser_tab_group_menu.js --verify --headless.

**Expected:** each hint stays open until the test closes it

**Actual:** the hint tests intermittently fail with "Confirmation hint panel is visible - false == true", because the leftover timer from the earlier test closes the hint
state.summary: Confirmation hint can close early when shown again while it is still opening

state.description:
Bug 2070182 addressed the `about:welcome` case by removing the `summary` outline and moving it to the `details` element.

This leaves two issues in Settings:

- The shared stylesheet gives `.resource-selection-details` no border radius, so the focus outline has sharp corners.
- When expanded, the outline surrounds the entire `details` element even though focus remains on the `summary`.

Firefox View History and the standalone migration dialog use the same styling, but neither has been visually verified.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Settings.
2. Under Account and sync, select **Import data**.
3. With a browser migrator available, press Tab until **Import all available data** is focused.
4. Press Space or Enter to expand the disclosure.

### Actual result

The focus outline has sharp corners. When open, it surrounds the expanded resource-selection container.

### Expected result

The focus outline around `.resource-selection-details` has rounded corners in both closed and open states. It appears only while the `summary` has keyboard-visible focus. Focusing a checkbox inside the open disclosure must not show the parent outline.
state.summary: Migration wizard ‘Import all available data’ focus outline has sharp corners in Settings and other dialogs

state.description:
When Firefox starts, `SessionStartup` reads the saved session and, once the browser is idle, counts the pinned tabs in it to record the `browser.engagement.max_concurrent_tab_pinned_count` metric. The same callback also counts saved tab groups for a debug log message, using `initialState.savedGroups.length`, which was added in bug 1973441. Session files written by Firefox 132 and earlier have no `savedGroups` property (it was introduced in bug 1908423), so for those profiles - for example someone upgrading from ESR 128 - that line throws a TypeError, and the pinned-tab metric is never recorded.

The rest of Session Restore already treats `savedGroups` as optional when reading saved state; SessionStore, for example, uses `state?.savedGroups ?? []`. Change [this line](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/8014960797439064c025f6bbc6a236558bd4f35f/browser/components/sessionstore/SessionStartup.sys.mjs#261
) to do the same:

```
  let savedGroupsCount = initialState.savedGroups?.length ?? 0;
```
Please also add an xpcshell test in browser/components/sessionstore/test/unit/ (and list it in xpcshell.toml there). `test_startup_session_async.js` and the `afterSessionStartupInitialization` helper in head.js show how to start `SessionStartup` against a session file. The new test should:

- call Services.fog.initializeFOG()
- write a session file to sessionstore.jsonlz4 in the profile, with IOUtils.writeJSON and `{ compress: true }`, containing one window with one pinned tab and no `savedGroups` property
- start `SessionStartup` and wait for it to initialize
- use `TestUtils.waitForCondition` to wait until `Glean.browserEngagement.maxConcurrentTabPinnedCount.testGetValue()` is 1

Without the fix the test times out after a few seconds; with it, it passes.

To verify the fix:

./mach test browser/components/sessionstore/test/unit/
./mach lint browser/components/sessionstore/

Tutorial to contribute:
https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/contributing/contribution_quickref.html
https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/contributing/stack_quickref.html

The bug will get automatically assigned to you when you submit a patch. Please comment here if you are actively working on it so people don't cross the streams.
state.summary: Don't throw when a session file has no savedGroups in SessionStartup's pinned-tab count

state.description:
`AttributionParent` in `browser/extensions/newtab/lib/actors/NewTabAttributionParent.sys.mjs` keeps its Remote Settings client in a module global, `gAllowListClient`, but binds its sync handler per instance in the constructor (`this._onSync = this.onSync.bind(this)`). Only the instance that creates the client subscribes, in `retrieveAllowList()`. Every other instance's `didDestroy()` hands `RemoteSettingsClient.off` a callback that was never registered, and `off` throws `Error: Unknown callback`.

Two consequences. The noisy one is an exception on every actor teardown: 5,465 of them from `browser_attribution_actor.js` alone in one CI day, the loudest error that test emits. The one that matters is that when the actor which *is* the subscriber is destroyed, the only `sync` listener goes with it, and `retrieveAllowList()` early-returns once `gAllowListClient` is set, so nothing re-subscribes. `onSync` is dead from then on and the allowlist stops following Remote Settings for the rest of the session.

The client is a module global that outlives every actor, so its subscription should be too: subscribe once alongside the client and leave `didDestroy()` out of it, or keep the bound handler next to the client and unsubscribe only when the client itself is dropped.

`browser.newtabpage.activity-stream.discoverystream.attribution.enabled` defaults to false, which is why this is S4: nothing ships with the feature on today.

`test_onSync_updates_allowlist` in `browser_attribution_actor.js` cannot catch either consequence. It calls `parent.onSync()` directly, so it never exercises the subscription, and it then overwrites the allowlist with `setAllowListForTest([origin])` before asserting, so its assertion passes whether `onSync` worked or not. Repairing it belongs in the same patch as the fix.
state.summary: AttributionParent.didDestroy() throws "Unknown callback" and drops the attribution allowlist's Remote Settings subscription

state.description:
Created attachment 9673103
tabs.mp4

**Environment:**
- platform: desktop;
- Firefox Nightly 161.0a1 (2026-11-03);
- Firefox Beta 160.0b4; 
- Firefox Release 159.0;

**Prerequisites:**
- Multiple tabs open with different VPN rules configured (e.g., Tab 1 with "Always on", Tab 2 with "VPN is off for this site" or no rule).

**Steps to Reproduce:**
- Open at least two tabs that have different VPN site rules applied.
- In the first tab, click or activate the VPN toolbar icon to open the VPN panel.
- Switch to another tab using keyboard shortcuts (e.g., Ctrl + [1-9]).
- Observe the behavior and content of the VPN panel.

**Expected Results:**
- Upon switching tabs, the VPN panel should either:
- Automatically close/dismiss as tab focus shifts away, OR
- Dynamically update its content and site rules to match the newly focused tab.

**Actual Results:**
- The VPN panel remains open and does not update its content, displaying stale information and site rules from the previous tab.

**Notes:**
- This creates a confusing state for keyboard and screen reader users, as the panel content remains out of sync with the webpage currently loaded in focus.
- See attached recording.
state.summary: [a11y] VPN panel fails to dismiss or update content when switching tabs via keyboard shortcuts

**Found in**
* Nightly 158.0a1

**Affected versions**
* Nightly 158.0a1
* Firefox 157.0b4

**Tested platforms**
* Affected platforms: Windows 11 x64, macOS 26, 

**Preconditions**
* Ensure a new profile is used.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Navigate to YouTube
2. Enable search bar by going to "Customize Toolbar", drag Search bar to Toolbar and click Done.
3. Focus the Search Bar and type any string to trigger the "Search with YouTube" button.
4. Observe the button.

**Expected result**
* The "Search with YouTube" button should be displayed correctly and fit within the Search dropdown.
 
**Actual result**
* The "Search with YouTube" button is cut off and does not fit within the Search dropdown. 
* I could only reproduce this on new profiles, after restarting the search and dropdown - the button si properly displayed.

**Regression range**
* The issue was introduced with the Nova styling changes.

**Additional notes**
* This is not reproducible if `browser.nova.enabled` is set to `false`.
* Reproducible also with other search engines like Ecosia.
state.summary: Search engine button is cut off in the Search dropdown with Nova styling

state.description:
Focusing a collapsed tab group's label with the keyboard schedules its preview. Moving focus off the label before the delay expires, with an arrow key or by leaving the tab strip, should cancel it, but the preview opens anyway.

`cancelTabGroupPreview()` in `tabs.mjs` calls `panelOpener.clear()` without an argument. Since bug 1980036, `clear(from)` only cancels when `from` is the panel that scheduled the open, so this call never cancels anything.
state.summary: Tab group preview opens after keyboard focus has moved off the group label
