- macOS / Windows / Linux (specify active OS version)
- Firefox VPN enabled and signed in
- At least two distinct website rules configured (e.g., Rule 1: example.com, Rule 2: mozilla.org)

**[Steps]**
1. Launch Firefox Nightly 160.0a1.
2. Open the Firefox VPN panel/settings and navigate to the website rules management section.
3. Ensure two distinct website rules exist (e.g., example.com and mozilla.org).
4. Click to edit Rule 1 (example.com).
5. Change the URL field to match Rule 2 (mozilla.org) and save the change.
6. Observe the resulting rules list and UI feedback.

**[Expected Results]**
The application should prevent saving and display a validation error indicating that a rule for this website/URL already exists. Both original rules should remain intact until a valid, non-duplicate URL is entered.

**[Actual Results]**
No duplicate rule error is displayed. The edited rule overwrites the original target rule, resulting in only one rule remaining in the list.

state.description:
Created attachment 9650647
Firefox sidebar panel header accent colour.png

The sidebar panel header doesn't use theme's text/accent colour for some of the panels, namely **Passwords** and any extension that utilises the sidebar.

state.description:
`TopSitesFeed.refresh()` computes the row asynchronously and lets only the newest refresh dispatch:

    const refreshId = ++this._refreshGeneration;
    ...
    if (refreshId !== this._refreshGeneration) { return; }

`_refreshGeneration` is a per-instance field, and `uninit()` does not stop a refresh that is already in flight. So when `feeds.system.topsites` goes false and then true, `Store.onPrefChanged` uninits the feed and constructs a new one, and the store holds that new `TopSitesFeed` while the old, uninitialized one is still inside `getLinksWithDefaults()`. The old one then dispatches `TOP_SITES_UPDATED` like any live feed -- broadcasting whenever the trigger that started it asked to, which `refreshDefaults` and `PLACES_HISTORY_CLEARED` both do -- and passes its own guard, because the new instance never touched its counter. Whichever instance finishes last wins in content, so the row every open about:newtab shows can be the one built from the configuration that has just been replaced.

An in-flight Contile fetch is a second way in: it calls `_readDefaults()` when it completes, which starts a whole refresh on a feed the store no longer holds.

Reachability is narrow: nothing in shipping code writes `feeds.system.topsites`. The customize panel's Shortcuts toggle writes `feeds.topsites` (`data-preference="feeds.topsites"` in `ContentSection.jsx`), a separate content-side section pref, and only `feeds.system.topsites` is a key in `Store`'s `_feedFactories`, so only it recreates the feed. Every other non-test reference to it is a read. It takes about:config, an enterprise policy or a test to reach this, hence S4 and no user-facing STR.

A test that does flip the pref caught it. `browser/extensions/newtab/test/browser/browser_topsites_contextMenu_options.js` and `browser_topsites_section.js` had a helper that toggled it to make the feed re-read prefs the test had just pushed. Instrumenting `refresh()` showed two feed instances dispatching per test, each with its own `_refreshGeneration`; delaying the dispatch of any instance whose `uninit()` has run fails both files 6/6 with `Wait for the https://www.youtube.com/ top site tile - timed out after 50 tries`, and they pass 6/6 once the helper stops recreating the feed.

Fix: `uninit()` marks the instance, and the refresh treats that mark like a superseded generation, both before starting work and before dispatching -- no store dispatch, no broadcast.
state.summary: TopSitesFeed keeps broadcasting a top sites row after uninit(), so toggling feeds.system.topsites can leave every about:newtab showing the old row

state.description:
User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/148.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

### Steps to reproduce

Local-only reproduction (no live sites or remote PDFs were used):

1. In the local pdf.js harness, run: node gen4tiny.mjs 800 600
2. 2. Run: node run.mjs t-bigimg.pdf 60000
3. 3. gen4tiny.mjs creates a 693-byte PDF with an RGB image XObject declaring 800x600, while its decoded stream contains only 1 KiB.
4. 4. The renderer fails with RangeError: Invalid typed array length, through new Uint32Array -> convertRGBToRGBA -> putBinaryImageData.
5. 5. The same happens at 1000x700 and 30000x30000. The HEAD helper was also replayed directly with a 1 KiB source buffer and throws.
Harness/write-up: hunt/big/harness and hunt/big/ADVISORY-PDFJS.md.

### Actual results

The affected page does not render. Local output:
{"ok":false,"ms":84,"err":"Invalid typed array length: 9600"}
with stack through convertRGBToRGBA / putBinaryImageData. A 693-byte input is sufficient. A complete 20000x20000 RGB image also causes about 28 seconds and about 3.6 GB RSS in the local Node renderer.

Root cause: src/shared/image_utils.js calculates len = width*height*3 from attacker-controlled PDF dimensions and constructs a Uint32Array view without clamping to the available decoded source buffer. src/core/image.js calls the same converter on the worker path.

### Expected results

A truncated or malformed image stream should be rejected gracefully or rendered as a partial/invalid image without throwing an uncaught RangeError or excessive memory use. The PDF viewer should remain usable.
state.summary: RangeError in convertRGBToRGBA when an RGB image stream is shorter than its declared size

`ExternalComponentWrapper`'s loading effect has no staleness check. `loadComponent()` awaits a dynamic `import()` and then acts on refs, but React can tear the effect down and start a new one while that await is pending, and the old continuation still runs.

A search feature-gate flip does exactly that. `newtabFeatureGate` swaps the SEARCH component between `UrlbarNewTabComponentRegistrant`'s `moz-urlbar` and `SearchUIUtils`'s `content-search-handoff-ui`, which re-runs the effect on a preloaded `about:newtab` that is still mounting. Two things then go wrong:

- Default branch: the stale continuation still passes `containerRef.current && !customElementRef.current`, so it appends the superseded configuration's element -- after its own cleanup has already run. The new effect's continuation then sees a set ref and creates nothing. Which search bar you end up with depends only on which of the two imports resolves first, and the wrong one survives until the page is reloaded.
- `react-bundle` branch: the stale continuation appends a second `<script>` to `document.head` and overwrites `scriptRef.current` and `cleanupRef.current`, leaking a script element and a mounted React tree that nothing will ever clean up, and mounts into a shadow root that cleanup has already emptied and disconnected from `document.l10n`.

The trigger is wider than a gate flip. The `REFRESH_EXTERNAL_COMPONENTS` reducer returns `components: action.data`, a fresh array identity, so any registry update re-runs the effect even when no configuration changed; `browser.nova.enabled` alone produces one, although neither registrant's `getComponents()` reads it. And a single gate flip calls `updated()` on both SEARCH registrants, so two broadcasts arrive back to back and the second lands inside the first one's import window.

Suggested fix: give the effect a cancellation flag, set it in the cleanup function, and bail out after each `await`, rather than treating `customElementRef.current` as proof of what is in the DOM. The comment excluding `props` from the dependency array records the assumption that is wrong.

Found by reading the code during a flakiness burndown of browser/extensions/newtab/test/browser. No test currently reaches it: bug 2062212 turned the gate off in `add_setup` for `browser_as_render.js`, which was the one test exercising a mid-mount flip.

state.description:
## Description

The group header label for recent searches (`urlbar-group-recent-searches`), shown
above the recent searches group in the address bar results panel, currently reads
"Recent Searches" in title case. This is inconsistent with Firefox's sentence case
convention for desktop UI labels, and specifically contradicts two things already in
the tree:

1. `addressbar-locbar-showrecentsearches-option-2` in
   `browser/locales/en-US/browser/preferences/preferences.ftl` labels this exact same
   feature "Recent searches" in about:preferences. The same feature is spelled two
   different ways in two places in the UI.

2. Its sibling group headers in the same results panel already use sentence case:
   `urlbar-group-search-suggestions` ("{ $engine } suggestions") and
   `urlbar-group-trending` ("Trending on { $engine }").

The address bar results panel is not a menu bar, app menu, or context menu, so the
title case exception does not apply here.

This is a casing-only change with no change in meaning, so the existing message ID is
edited in place and no new ID is needed.

## Location

```
browser/locales/en-US/browser/browser.ftl
urlbar-group-recent-searches: "Recent Searches" -> "Recent searches"
```

## Notes

- The automated casing test
  `browser/base/content/test/browser-static/browser_sentence_case_strings.js` does not
  cover address bar strings, and this phrase is not in its PHRASES allowlist, so no
  companion test change is required.

## Context

This fix was traced and validated using an AI-assisted content design workflow (Claude).

state.description:
### Steps to reproduce

Use Firefox (Arch Linux build) on a machine without working network access, where outgoing connections are silently dropped rather than refused.
Start Firefox, let it run, then quit.

### Actual results

Firefox crashes during shutdown:

MozCrashReason: [Parent, Main Thread] ###!!! ABORT: file resource://nimbus/lib/RemoteSettingsExperimentLoader.sys.mjs:308

The file and line point to the call in RemoteSettingsExperimentLoader.enable() that registers the "RemoteSettingsExperimentLoader: disabling" blocker on AsyncShutdown.appShutdownConfirmed.

### Expected results

Firefox shuts down cleanly even if a Nimbus recipe update is still in progress.

state.description:
`SidebarController.registerPrefSidebar` installs pref observers that hide the sidebar when the panel's pref is turned off. These observers outlive the window. Turning such a pref off after closing a window that had that panel open calls `hide()` on the closed window, which throws because its state was cleared on uninit:

```
TypeError: can't access property "arm", this._splitterAriaUpdateTask is null
```

User impact: only an error in the browser console, e.g. when one of these prefs is changed by Nimbus.

On CI it was logged 2,396 times in 1,465 jobs, from 2 tests, out of the 31,690 mozilla-central mochitest jobs of 2026-10-15 in the errors dashboard (https://tests.firefox.dev/errors.html?kind=mochitest#date=2026-10-15). `browser_opentabs_sidebar.js` and `browser_chat_sidebar.js`, which reset these prefs after closing windows.

state.description:
Created attachment 9672888
ManageVPNRulesSubsecion_NVDA.mp4

**Environment:**
- platform: Desktop (Windows / macOS / Linux);
- Firefox Nightly 161.0a1 (2026-11-02);

**Prerequisites:**
- Screen reader active (NVDA/VoiceOver/Orca/).

**Steps to Reproduce:**
- In Firefox Nightly navigate to about:preferences#privacy.
- Use the keyboard (Tab / arrow keys) to navigate to the "Built-in VPN" section.
- Move focus to the "Manage VPN rules" button/area and press Enter.
- Observe the screen reader announcement upon landing on the subpage.

**Expected Results:**
- The screen reader announces the destination subpage title/heading (e.g., "Manage VPN rules") or page context before or alongside announcing the currently focused "Go back" button, confirming where the user has landed.

**Actual Results:**
- The user is redirected to the "Manage VPN rules" subsection and focus moves to the "Go back" button, which is announced, but the new subpage title/heading is not announced at all.

**Notes:**
- The issue is also reproducible while navigating to other sections from the about:preferences page, e.g. “Advanced settings” from the “Enhanced Tracking Protection” section.
- See attached recording.
state.summary: [a11y] Screen reader does not announce subpage name or heading when navigating to "Manage VPN rules" in about:preferences#privacy

Created attachment 9674491
first-request-without-headers.png

There is a potential race condition in the `moz-cached-ohttp` protocol where the Image request can finishe before the headers request, and the header message can get dropped and saved without original-response-headers. This causes the `tryCache()` call on the next call to fail `getMetaDataElement()` with `NS_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE: Component returned failure code: 0x80040111 (NS_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE)`. This is treated as a cache miss and re-fetches over OHTTP, where the race condition may not occur again and successfully cache.

The attached images show the entry was initially written with the image but without its headers (`first-request-without-headers.png`). The next load treated it as a miss, fetched the image over OHTTP again and rewrote it, and this time the headers arrived in time (`second-request-with-headers.png`). The final attached image shows the actual requests in the browser toolbox network tab where you can see the same request being made for a previous request (assuming based on the kb matching).
state.summary: Potential race condition in the moz-cached-ohttp protocol on New Tab

Created attachment 9665505
image (10).png

When the fire button (behind `browser.fireButton.enabled`, added in bug 2076799) is removed from the toolbar, its label "Delete some or all of your browsing data" is too long for the Customize palette: it wraps to three lines while every other item fits on one or two, which looks off.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Set `browser.fireButton.enabled` to true and restart.
2. Open the menu > More tools > Customize toolbar.
3. Drag the fire button from the toolbar into the palette.

Expected: a short label that fits like the other palette items.
Actual: the label wraps to three lines (screenshot attached).

The `fire-button-toolbar-button` message in `browser/locales/en-US/browser/browser.ftl` uses the same long text for `.label` and `.tooltiptext`. The fix is a shorter `.label`, with wording from design, under a new ID, keeping the long text as the tooltip. The same label also shows when the button is pinned to the overflow menu.

The fire button experiment targets Firefox 161, so the new string needs to land before the 161 string freeze on 2026-11-04.
state.summary: Fire button label wraps to three lines in the Customize palette

state.description:
Typing a calculation that equals 150 (e.g. `100+50`) in the address bar and clicking the result starts the snake game, but the results dropdown is drawn over it, so the game can't be seen or played.

This is a regression from bug 2022527. Before that change the whole urlbar host was the popover in the top layer, so the game overlay (appended to the host by `startTail150()` in `UrlbarView.mjs`) was in the top layer too, and its `z-index` put it above the view. Now only `.urlbarView` is the popover. The overlay is ordinary content, and no `z-index` can put it above the top layer.
state.summary: Address bar results dropdown covers the calculator game

state.description:
**[Affected versions]:**
- Firefox Release 158.0 - Build ID: 20261007201254

**[Affected Platforms]:**
 - Windows 10 x64
- Linux Mint 22.2
- macOS 26..2

**[Prerequisites]:**
- Have Firefox Release 158.0 build installed/extracted and opened, using any locale.
- Have the “nimbus.debug” pref set to “true” in “about:config”.

**[Steps to reproduce]:**
1. Open the profile from the prerequisites and navigate to the following link to force-enroll in the “widget” treatment branch of the “[Search Widget - L](https://experimenter.services.mozilla.com/nimbus/search-widget-l/summary/)” experiment: 
about:studies?optin_slug=search-widget-l&optin_branch=widget&optin_collection=nimbus-preview
2. Open a new tab and observe the displayed widgets.
3. Restart the browser.
4. Open a New Tab and observe the displayed widgets and their toggle states.
5. Navigate to “about:studies” and remove the “New Tab 160.0.20261011.195215 to Release 158” rollout.
6. Restart the browser.
7. Open a new tab and observe the displayed widgets.

**[Expected result]:**
- The Search, Clocks, Picture of the Day  and Focus Timer widgets remain enabled and displayed according to the experiment recipe, including after restarting Firefox.

**[Actual result]:**
- Step 2: the widgets are displayed according to the experiment recipe.
- Step 4: After restarting Firefox, the Search and Picture of the Day widgets are toggled off.
- Step 7: after removing the New Tab add-on rollout and restarting Firefox, all widgets are displayed again according to the experiment recipe (Search, Clocks, POTD, FocusTimer).

**[Notes]:**
- The issue is reproducible with the New Tab add-on version 160.0.20261011.195215 and later versions installed.
- If the New Tab add-on rollout is removed before the first browser restart, the widget configuration remains correct and all widgets are displayed according to the experiment recipe.
- Removing the New Tab add-on rollout after the issue occurs and restarting Firefox restores the expected widget configuration.
- The issue is reproducible on both [Search Widget M/L](https://experimenter.services.mozilla.com/nimbus/?sort=&status=Preview&search=search+widget+-+&application=firefox-desktop&channel=release&feature_configs=125) experiments.
- Attached a [screen recording](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BBIzM3X9hbqBZiIg59NXSRv4jVJ2CZEH/view?usp=sharing) of the issue.
state.summary: [Experiment] Search Widget - M/L - The “Search” and “Picture of the day” widgets are toggled off when New Tab Addon version 160.0.20261011.195215 is installed

Outside Nova, `synced-tabs.svg` draws four corner pieces on top of the window and laptop shapes they overlap. With an opaque fill this is invisible, but with a translucent fill (`fill-opacity`, or a `color-mix()` with transparent as the toolbar button icon fill) the overlapping areas paint twice and the corners come out darker, e.g. on the synced tabs button in the sidebar launcher.

Merging the shapes into one path that covers the same area fixes this without changing how the icon renders with an opaque fill.
state.summary: Synced tabs icon shows darker corners when drawn with a translucent fill

fig1_sp_source.png

The SitePermissions.getForPrincipal() method may allow a browser-scoped temporary ALLOW permission to override an explicit persistent BLOCK rule for the same principal and permission. This behavior appears to conflict with the user's saved permission settings and may result in an incorrect effective permission state.

I have reproduced the behavior and captured supporting screenshots. The report includes the relevant code path, reproduction steps, and proposed remediation. Further validation is needed to establish whether this behavior can be triggered by unprivileged web content and has a security impact.
state.summary: SitePermissions.getForPrincipal may allow temporary permissions to override a persistent BLOCK rule
